A WorldBridge conditions the action transformer on these priors through multi-source attention memories and spatial-temporal biases, while the teacher model is removed at inference. Across VLABench, RoboTwin2.0, LIBERO-Plus and real-robot evaluations, Bridge-WA improves task success, progress, and robustness, with particularly clear gains under out-of-distribution visual shifts. By focusing action generation on where and how the scene will change, Bridge-WA suppresses nuisance appearance factors such as background, lighting, and distractors, leading to better generalization without deployment-time dense future-image generation. Code and visualizations are available at: https://hcplab-sysu.github.io/BRIDGE-WA .

AI.tldr: Bridge-WA distills a frozen future-change teacher into three compact priors for world-action control, enabling efficient action generation without deployment-time dense future-image generation; it improves task success, progress, and robustness, especially under out-of-distribution shifts.
AI.motivation: Existing world-action models rely on expensive generative world models and dense future rollouts that allocate capacity to appearance details irrelevant to control. There is a need for action priors that anticipate scene changes to improve efficiency and generalization.
AI.method: Train a frozen future-change teacher to produce three priors: (1) future tokens for intended outcomes, (2) change maps for intervention support, and (3) motion-flow maps for local transition direction. A WorldBridge action transformer is conditioned on these priors via multi-source attention memories and spatial-temporal biases. The teacher is discarded at inference, so action generation relies on the compact priors.
AI.result: Across VLABench, RoboTwin2.0, LIBERO-Plus and real-robot evaluations, Bridge-WA achieves higher task success, progress, and robustness, with pronounced gains under out-of-distribution visual shifts. By focusing on where/how the scene will change, it suppresses nuisance appearance factors (background, lighting, distractors) and improves generalization without dense future-image generation during deployment.
AI.conclusion: The approach offers an efficient, robust pathway for vision-language-action planning by anchoring control in scene-change priors distilled from a teacher, enabling better generalization and practical performance while avoiding costly foreseen-image generation at run time.

title: Profit-Based Counterfactual Explanations for Product Improvement: A Case Study of Manga Sales in Japan
summary: Counterfactual explanation (CE) is widely used to enhance the interpretability of machine learning models and support data-driven decision-making based on model predictions. However, existing CE methods typically require two exogenously specified inputs: a desired output value (target) and a distance function that quantifies changes in explanatory variables. In regression settings, neither the validity of target specification nor the practical interpretation of the distance metric has been sufficiently addressed. Furthermore, most existing CE methods focus on altering predictions rather than optimizing a decision objective, even though real-world decision-making often requires explicit objective maximization. To address these limitations, we formulate CE as a profit maximization problem in management and marketing contexts and propose a framework termed profit-based counterfactual explanation (PBCE). PBCE eliminates the need for exogenous target specification by directly maximizing profit as the primary optimization objective. Concurrently, the distance term is reinterpreted as the cost of modifying product attributes, providing a clear and economically grounded interpretation.

AI.tldr: Introduces profit-based counterfactual explanations (PBCE) for regression by directly maximizing profit and treating the distance as the cost of modifying attributes, removing the need for an exogenous target.
AI.motivation: Counterfactual explanations (CE) typically rely on an externally specified target value and a distance metric. In regression contexts, target validity and the economic interpretation of distance are unclear, and most CE methods optimize for prediction changes rather than explicit decision objectives. A framework that optimizes business objective (profit) would yield more actionable explanations in management/marketing settings.
AI.method: Propose PBCE, a framework that eliminates the need for exogenous target specification by directly maximizing profit as the optimization objective. Reinterpret the distance term as the cost of modifying product attributes, providing an economically grounded interpretation. The approach reframes CE from prediction adjustment to profit-driven decision support.
AI.result: The abstract presents a conceptual framework without reported empirical results. It outlines the formulation and interpretation of PBCE but does not provide experimental validation within the abstract.
AI.conclusion: PBCE offers an economically grounded, target-free counterfactual explanation framework that aligns explanations with explicit profit optimization for management and marketing decision-making.

title: Multi-THuMBS: Multi-person Tracking of 3D Human Meshes Beyond Video Shots
summary: Tracking multi-person 3D human meshes from in-the-wild videos is a highly challenging problem due to complex interactions, frequent occlusions, and severe truncation inherent in unconstrained environments. While recent approaches have improved robustness against these issues, they largely overlook the critical challenge prevalent in real-world footage: frequent shot changes. These abrupt transitions in camera viewpoints often cause existing methods to lose track of human identities and fail in reconstructing temporally coherent trajectories. Although several recent works have explored 3D human mesh tracking under shot changes, they are still limited to single-person scenarios, making them inadequate for real-world videos where multiple people interact and appear simultaneously. To address this limitation, we propose Multi-THuMBS (Multi-person Tracking of 3D Human Meshes Beyond Video Shots) that leverages a state-of-the-art 3D scene prior to reconstruct the two boundary frames in a single shared 3D space. Human meshes are then registered within the shared 3D space, maintaining per-person identity and motion consistency across shot changes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach yields significant improvements in 3D human mesh recovery, camera pose estimation, and identity tracking, thereby ensuring high-fidelity motion reconstruction with consistent identity preservation across shots compared to previous state-of-the-art methods.

AI.tldr: Introduces Multi-THuMBS for tracking multiple 3D human meshes across video shot changes by reconstructing boundary frames in a shared 3D space using a scene prior, enabling identity-preserving, temporally coherent tracking across shots.
AI.motivation: Addresses the gap where single-shot 3D mesh tracking methods handle occlusions and truncation but fail under abrupt camera viewpoint changes. Real-world footage requires multi-person tracking with consistent identities across shot changes.
AI.method: Uses a state-of-the-art 3D scene prior to reconstruct the two boundary frames in a common 3D space. Then registers individual human meshes within this shared space to preserve per-person identity and motion continuity across shot transitions.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show notable improvements in 3D mesh recovery, camera pose estimation, and identity tracking, achieving higher fidelity motion reconstruction with consistent identities across shot changes compared to prior work.
AI.conclusion: The method fills a key gap in multi-person 3D mesh tracking under shot changes, demonstrating robust cross-shot identity preservation and superior performance in realistic, unconstrained scenarios.

title: How to Allocate Your Tokens? Scaling Laws with Training Steps and Batch Size
summary: We propose a scaling law that takes into account model size and training data while explicitly splitting the latter into training steps and batch size (called three-term law). Fitting the proposed law on a large set of training runs, we find that it correctly recovers the scaling of the optimal batch size. Moreover, because it makes use of training runs with suboptimal batch size, our proposed law can be robustly fit with a significantly smaller amount of training runs. We further show that the three-term law can be used to derive scaling laws for suboptimal batch sizes, and that it matches previous empirical findings related to the critical batch size.

AI.tldr: A three-term scaling law combining model size, data (split into training steps and batch size) to predict optimal and suboptimal batch-size effects, enabling robust fitting with fewer training runs.
AI.motivation: Existing scaling laws often treat data and compute in aggregate and may miss how batch size interacts with training progress. A law that explicitly accounts for training steps and batch size can improve prediction of optimal batch size and suboptimal regimes, reducing experimental cost.
AI.method: Fit the proposed three-term law to a large dataset of training runs, treating data as two components (training steps and batch size). Analyze whether the law recovers the optimal batch-size scaling and whether it can be fit using suboptimal runs. Derive scaling laws for suboptimal batch sizes and compare with known results on critical (optimal) batch size.
AI.result: The law recovers the scaling of the optimal batch size, can be robustly fitted with fewer training runs by leveraging suboptimal batch sizes, and enables derivation of scaling laws for suboptimal batch sizes. It is consistent with prior empirical findings related to the critical batch size.
AI.conclusion: The proposed three-term law extends scaling theory to explicitly include batch-size dynamics during training, enabling more efficient empirical studies and better understanding of how batch size interacts with model size and data.

title: Actuator Reality Shaping for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Robot Learning
summary: Sim-to-real transfer in robot learning is often limited by discrepancies between the ideal actuator dynamics assumed during policy training and the nonlinear, hardware-dependent behavior of physical motors. While conventional approaches attempt to bridge this gap by increasing simulator fidelity through system identification, domain randomization, or learned actuator models, we introduce an alternative paradigm: actuator reality shaping. Instead of modifying the simulator to match the real world, our method shapes the closed-loop behavior of physical actuators to match the idealized second-order reference dynamics used in simulation. By equipping each joint with a two-degree-of-freedom feedforward--feedback controller, we decouple reference-response shaping from robust stabilization, thereby providing a standardized actuator interface for reinforcement learning policies. As a result, policies trained only with the prescribed reference model can be deployed zero-shot on real hardware without task-level fine-tuning or learned actuator models. We validate the approach on a single-joint high-gear-ratio servo under external loads and a 7-DOF robotic arm reaching task, where actuator reality shaping substantially reduces sim-to-real tracking error and improves zero-shot task performance compared with standard servo-control and representative real-to-sim-to-real baselines. We further demonstrate zero-shot transfer on a wheeled-legged robot driving over a slope and a humanoid robot walking, suggesting that actuator reality shaping can serve as a reusable interface for robot learning across diverse hardware platforms.

AI.tldr: Proposes actuator reality shaping to align physical actuator dynamics with idealized sim dynamics, enabling zero-shot sim-to-real transfer via a 2-DOF joint controller, validated on diverse hardware.
AI.motivation: To address the sim-to-real gap caused by nonlinear, hardware-dependent actuator dynamics, moving from sim fidelity to hardware shaping for standardized RL interfaces.
AI.method: Attach a two-DOF feedforward–feedback controller per joint to shape closed-loop actuator response to follow a second-order reference model; decouple reference shaping from stabilization; evaluate on single-joint servo with load, 7-DOF arm reaching, wheeled-legged robot, humanoid walking.
AI.result: Significant reduction in tracking error in sim-to-real and improved zero-shot task performance compared with standard servo control and baselines; demonstration of zero-shot transfer on slope driving and biped walking across platforms.
AI.conclusion: Actuator reality shaping provides a reusable hardware-interface paradigm for robot learning, enabling zero-shot sim-to-real transfer without task-level fine-tuning or learned actuator models.

title: Scaling with Confidence: Calibrating Confidence of LLMs for Adaptive Test Time Scaling
summary: Training large language models (LLMs) with reinforcement learning (RL) has significantly advanced their performance on reasoning and question-answering tasks. However, prevailing RL reward designs typically prioritize response correctness, neglecting to incentivize models to express their confidence accurately. This leads to a critical problem: performance gains are often accompanied by poor calibration between confidence and accuracy, misleading models to overconfidently hallucinate when uncertain. To address this limitation, we propose $\textbf{C}$orrectness and $\textbf{C}$onfidence $\textbf{C}$alibration $\textbf{R}$einforcement $\textbf{L}$earning ($\textbf{C3RL}$), a novel RL algorithm integrating correctness, calibration and dataset-informed reference accuracy rewards together. Comprehensive evaluation across 8 text and multimodal datasets demonstrates that C3RL enhances calibration without sacrificing accuracy, outperforming the current state-of-the-art method in both performance and calibration metrics. Utilizing the well-calibrated verbalized confidence from C3RL, we further introduce $\textbf{C}$onfidence-based $\textbf{A}$daptive Test Time $\textbf{S}$caling ($\textbf{CAS}$), an adjustable inference-time strategy that allocates computational resources based on response confidence. Experiments show that CAS surpasses majority voting on both in-domain and out-of-domain datasets while reducing the inference budget by up to 12.33 times. We believe the synergy of C3RL and CAS paves the way for deploying more reliable and resource-efficient LLMs. The code, data and models will be released.

AI.tldr: C3RL integrates correctness and confidence calibration rewards into RL training for LLMs, and CAS uses confidence for adaptive test-time scaling. They improve calibration without harming accuracy across 8 datasets, beating SOTA; CAS can reduce inference cost by up to 12.33x.
AI.motivation: Current RL reward designs emphasize correctness but ignore calibration, causing overconfident errors and miscalibrated outputs; there is a need to align confidence with accuracy and to make inference more resource-efficient.
AI.method: Propose C3RL, an RL algorithm that combines correctness, confidence calibration, and dataset-informed reference accuracy rewards to train LLMs. Develop CAS, a test-time strategy that allocates computation based on model confidence to improve resource efficiency. Evaluate on 8 text/multimodal datasets against state-of-the-art baselines.
AI.result: C3RL enhances calibration without sacrificing accuracy and surpasses SOTA in both accuracy and calibration metrics across 8 datasets. CAS further improves efficiency, outperforming majority voting on in-domain and OOD data while reducing inference budget by up to 12.33x.
AI.conclusion: The combination of C3RL and CAS enables more reliable and cost-effective LLM deployment, with planned release of code, data, and models.

title: Online Segment 3D Gaussians via Launching Virtual Drones
summary:
Interactive segmentation of 3D Gaussians offers a compelling opportunity for real-time manipulation of 3D scenes, thanks to the real-time rendering capability of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). However, existing methods require a time-consuming per-scene setup - typically tens of seconds or even minutes - before interactive segmentation can begin on a raw 3DGS scene. This setup involves multi-view mask preparation, mask lifting, and feature distillation, creating a major bottleneck for online applications.
  To address this limitation, we aim to completely eliminate the setup stage for interactive 3DGS segmentation while keeping the segmentation time practical (under 1 second). In this work, we present SAGO (Segment Any Gaussians Online), a novel setup-free framework for interactive 3DGS segmentation. By introducing virtual drones, our method reframes the 3D segmentation problem as an online Next-Best-View (NBV) planning task formulated within a Markov process. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SAGO can extract clean 3D assets directly from 3D Gaussians with sub-second latency, thereby enabling a broad range of downstream applications such as object manipulation and scene editing. Moreover, our method achieves over a 50x speedup compared to the previous setup-free 3DGS segmentation frameworks.

AI.tldr: A setup-free, real-time interactive segmentation for 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) using virtual drones and Next-Best-View planning; achieves sub-second latency and over 50x speedup over prior setup-free methods, reframing segmentation as an online Markov decision process.
AI.motivation: Current 3DGS interactive segmentation relies on lengthy per-scene setup steps (multi-view masks, mask lifting, feature distillation), creating a bottleneck for online use. A setup-free solution would unlock real-time interactive manipulation and editing of 3D scenes.
AI.method: Introduce SAGO (Segment Any Gaussians Online), a setup-free framework that uses virtual drones to cast next viewpoints. Reformulates 3D segmentation as an online Next-Best-View planning problem within a Markov decision process, enabling incremental segmentation updates without prior per-scene preprocessing.
AI.result: Demonstrates sub-second latency for extracting clean 3D assets directly from 3D Gaussians. Achieves over 50× speedup compared to previous setup-free 3DGS segmentation frameworks and enables downstream tasks such as object manipulation and scene editing.
AI.conclusion: SAGO eliminates the setup stage for interactive 3DGS segmentation while maintaining practical latency, broadening the applicability of real-time 3D editing and manipulation through NBV-driven online segmentation.

title: Don't Let Gains FADE: Breaking Down Policy Gradient Weights in RL
summary: Reinforcement learning post-training dramatically improves LLM reasoning, but suffers from training instability and diversity collapse. Advantage functions offer an appealing fix: they reshape the training objective, reweight which rollouts drive learning, and are trivial to implement. Yet a proliferation of methods makes it unclear which advantage to use and when. We cut through the confusion with a unifying framework that decomposes any advantage into its positive and negative gradient mass along two orthogonal axes. On the sign axis, imbalanced updates collapse either entropy or weight geometry. On the difficulty axis, hard-problem focus sharpens signal but costs sample size. Both trade-offs shift during training: exploration favors balance and hard focus; exploitation favors suppression and medium focus. This motivates FADE (Focal Advantage with Dynamic Entropy), a self-adapting advantage that reads training dynamics to schedule the gradient weight automatically. FADE reaches peak pass@1 20k steps earlier than the best static baseline at the 7B scale and 2k steps earlier at the 32B , while achieving the best accuracy-diversity trade-off across all pass@k on LiveCodeBench and AIME.

AI.tldr: Proposes FADE, a dynamic, self-adapting advantage weighting for RL post-training of LLMs, unified under a two-axis gradient-math framework (positive/negative mass; sign and difficulty). Demonstrates earlier convergence and improved accuracy-diversity trade-offs on LiveCodeBench and AIME across 7B and 32B models.
AI.motivation: Resolve ambiguity in which advantage to use for RL post-training of LLMs and to stabilize learning while preserving or enhancing diversity.
AI.method: Introduce a unifying framework that decomposes any advantage into positive/negative gradient mass along two orthogonal axes: sign axis (affecting entropy/weight geometry) and difficulty axis (balancing hard-problem focus vs sample efficiency). Propose FADE (Focal Advantage with Dynamic Entropy), a self-adapting mechanism that schedules gradient weights based on training dynamics to balance exploration and exploitation.
AI.result: FADE achieves earlier peak pass@1: about 20k steps earlier at 7B scale and 2k steps earlier at 32B; delivers best accuracy-diversity trade-off (across pass@k) on LiveCodeBench and AIME compared to static baselines.
AI.conclusion: A dynamics-based gradient weighting strategy grounded in a two-axis decomposition improves stability and performance in RL post-training for LLMs, with FADE providing superior convergence speed and diversity-quality trade-offs across scales and benchmarks.

title: CoFL-S: Spatially Queryable Sector Flow Fields for Local Language-Conditioned Navigation
summary: Vision-Language Navigation has increasingly emphasized high-level instruction reasoning, memory, global map construction, and instruction decomposition, while the low-level action representation remains comparatively underexplored. We propose CoFL-S, a low-level vision-language-action framework that predicts a language-conditioned flow field over the robot's local visible sector and generates continuous trajectories by rolling out the predicted field. To train this low-level representation, we convert each VLN-CE episode, originally a whole-episode instruction paired with an action sequence, into frame-level local supervision with aligned sub-instructions and matched action, trajectory, and dense flow-field targets. For evaluation, we introduce a continuous-time Habitat benchmark that isolates low-level action interfaces from instruction decomposition and executes all methods through a shared velocity-command controller, enabling decomposition-independent closed-loop comparison across different planner frequencies rather than fixed discrete forward-and-turn transitions in VLN-CE. Under matched encoders and training settings, CoFL-S consistently outperforms action-token and action-chunk baselines across planner frequencies in the continuous-time Habitat benchmark, and zero-shot real-world closed-loop deployment further shows its advantage over both baselines beyond simulation.

AI.tldr: CoFL-S introduces a low-level vision-language-action framework for VLN by predicting a language-conditioned flow field over the local view to generate continuous trajectories, trained via frame-level supervision from whole-episode VLN-CE data, and evaluated in a continuous-time Habitat benchmark that decouples low-level control from high-level planning; it outperforms action-token and action-chunk baselines and transfers to real-world closed-loop deployment.
AI.motivation: VLN research has emphasized high-level reasoning, memory, and map construction, with low-level action representation remaining underexplored. A robust low-level controller that can be conditioned on language is needed to bridge language commands with continuous motor actions and improve real-time execution.
AI.method: Convert VLN-CE episodes into frame-level local supervision with aligned sub-instructions and matched action, trajectory, and dense flow-field targets. Train a model to predict a language-conditioned flow field over the robot’s local visible sector and roll out continuous trajectories by following this field. Introduce a continuous-time Habitat benchmark that runs methods through a shared velocity-command controller, enabling decomposition-free, closed-loop comparison across planner frequencies (not fixed discrete actions).
AI.result: Under matched encoders and training settings, CoFL-S consistently outperforms action-token and action-chunk baselines across planner frequencies in the continuous-time Habitat benchmark. Zero-shot real-world closed-loop deployment also shows advantages over both baselines beyond simulation.
AI.conclusion: Low-level flow-field prediction provides robust, language-conditioned control for VLN, enabling continuous trajectories and better cross-frequency and real-world deployment performance, and decouples low-level control from high-level instruction decomposition.

title: Spatial Support Matters: Geometry-Aware Graph Fusion for Rainfall Field Reconstruction
summary: Fine-scale rainfall reconstruction is critical for urban flood modeling, but real rainfall sensing systems observe the field through incompatible spatial supports: gauges measure points, microwave links measure paths, and radar/satellite products measure gridded areas. These differences in measurement support impose geometrically distinct constraints on the rainfall field, yet existing heterogeneous graph approaches reconcile such sources in feature space, giving each its own embedding while discarding the geometry of its support. We propose a geometry-aware multi-support heterogeneous graph neural network that represents each observation according to its support type (0D point, 1D line, or 2D grid) as a distinct node layer, and fuses them through cross-support message passing into a point-support prediction layer from which the field is reconstructed. An inductive masked-node formulation decouples prediction resolution from sensing resolution, allowing the same trained model to reconstruct the field at user-defined target locations or display grids. On Singapore data, the proposed method reduces RMSE by 23.2\% over the classical interpolation baseline, inverse-distance weighting, and consistently outperforms other neural architectures such as convolutional fusion and support-agnostic heterogeneous graph baselines. A generalization study using data from Sydney, Australia lets us characterize when multi-support fusion helps: the available skill appears to depend on gauge spacing relative to the spatial correlation length of the field, so fusion delivers the largest gains where the field is under-sampled relative to its correlation length and little when it is already resolved. Code and models will be open-sourced upon paper acceptance.

AI.tldr: Geometry-aware multi-support heterogeneous graph neural network for rainfall reconstruction across 0D/1D/2D observations, using cross-support message passing and an inductive masked-node design to decouple prediction from sensing resolution. Shows notable RMSE gains on Singapore data and insight into when fusion helps via a Sydney generalization study; code to be released after acceptance.
AI.motivation: In rainfall sensing, observations come with incompatible spatial supports (point gauges, line microwave links, gridded radar). The geometry of the observation support constrains the rainfall field, but existing heterogeneous graph approaches fuse in feature space without leveraging geometry.
AI.method: Construct a geometry-aware multi-support HGNN with distinct node layers for 0D (points), 1D (lines), and 2D (grids) observations. Employ cross-support message passing to fuse information and a point-support prediction layer to reconstruct the field at target locations. Use an inductive masked-node formulation to decouple prediction resolution from sensing resolution, enabling reconstruction at user-defined locations or grids.
AI.result: On Singapore data, RMSE improves by 23.2% over baseline interpolations (classical, inverse-distance weighting) and outperforms other neural baselines (convolutional fusion, support-agnostic HGs). A Sydney-based generalization study shows fusion benefit depends on gauge spacing relative to the field's spatial correlation length; greatest gains when the field is under-sampled, limited gains when already resolved.
AI.conclusion: The geometry-aware fusion of heterogeneous observations enhances fine-scale rainfall reconstruction and generalizes to different regions, with performance contingent on sampling relative to the spatial correlation length. Code and models will be open-sourced upon paper acceptance.

title: DRDN: Decoupled Representation Dynamic Network for From-Scratch ViT Class-Incremental Learning
comment: 10 pages, IEEEtran journal format. Preprint submitted to IEEE Transactions on Multimedia
summary:
Dynamic expansion methods for class-incremental learning (CIL) protect task-specific knowledge by growing dedicated tokens or subnetworks, yet our analyses suggest that classification supervision alone does not sufficiently preserve task-agnostic shared backbone representations over long incremental sequences. We identify two intertwined challenges: cross-task confusion from sequential training on predominantly current-task data, which biases decision boundaries toward recent tasks; and under-optimized shared representations in the backbone that cap long-term discriminability as tasks accumulate.
  We propose the Decoupled Representation Dynamic Network (DRDN), which addresses these challenges via two orthogonal mechanisms. For shared backbone representations, DRDN continuously applies masked image modeling (MIM) at every incremental step, with reconstruction gradients routed exclusively through the backbone, encouraging it to retain general visual structure beyond class-discriminative cues. For task-specific discrimination, DRDN employs hierarchical task token expansion across all transformer layers, with a modified per-task attention rule that reduces inter-task interference. We support this design with accuracy degradation analysis and cross-task confusion rate measurements.
  In the from-scratch ViT CIL setting (no external pretraining), DRDN consistently improves over strong token-expansion baselines with comparable backbone scale. On CIFAR100-B0 (10 steps), DRDN achieves 77.19% average accuracy, outperforming DKT by 1.36 points and DyTox by 3.53 points, with an advantage that grows at longer incremental sequences. Multi-seed validation confirms stability (+/-0.31%). The MIM decoder is active only during training, adding no inference-time parameters or computation.

AI.tldr: DRDN decouples representation learning from task-specific discrimination in class-incremental learning by (1) applying masked image modeling (MIM) at every incremental step to the backbone with gradients flowing only through it, and (2) expanding task tokens hierarchically across transformer layers with a per-task attention rule to reduce interference. This yields improved long-term discriminability, mitigates cross-task confusion, and adds no inference-time cost, outperforming token-expansion baselines on from-scratch ViT CIL (e.g., CIFAR100-B0, 10 steps).
AI.motivation: In CIL, two core challenges hinder long-term performance: (i) cross-task confusion from sequential training biasing decision boundaries toward recent tasks, and (ii) under-optimized shared backbone representations that lose discriminability as tasks accumulate. A method that preserves backbone representations while enabling robust, task-specific discrimination is needed.
AI.method: DRDN addresses the challenges with two orthogonal components: (1) continuous MIM during incremental steps, routing reconstruction gradients exclusively through the backbone to preserve general visual structure beyond class cues; (2) hierarchical expansion of task tokens across all transformer layers with a modified per-task attention rule to minimize inter-task interference and preserve task-specific discrimination across many tasks.
AI.result: Empirical results in the from-scratch ViT CIL setting show DRDN consistently outperforming strong token-expansion baselines with similar backbone scales. On CIFAR100-B0 (10 steps), DRDN achieves 77.19% average accuracy, surpassing DKT by 1.36 points and DyTox by 3.53 points, with higher stability across seeds (±0.31). The MIM decoder is active only during training, incurring no inference-time parameters or computation.
AI.conclusion: DRDN demonstrates effective decoupling of representation learning from task-specific discrimination, yielding improved long-term discriminability and reduced cross-task confusion without adding inference overhead. The approach shows strong gains in the early-from-scratch CIL setting and is likely to generalize to longer incremental sequences, given its backbone-focused preservation and interference-robust task-token design.

title: Unveiling the Non-Monotonic Effect of Privacy on Generalization under Byzantine Robustness
summary: Recent work has established a fundamental trilemma between Byzantine robustness, local differential privacy (LDP), and optimization error in distributed learning. We show that this trilemma does not universally extend to generalization error, but instead depends critically on the privacy regime. Specifically, in the high-noise regime (strong privacy), we prove that increasing privacy reduces the generalization error, i.e., there is no tension between robustness and privacy. In the low-noise regime (weaker privacy), however, the tension between robustness and privacy reappears and increasing privacy indeed degrades generalization. Our theory explains this surprising non-monotonic behavior of the generalization error via matching lower and upper bounds on the algorithmic stability of Byzantine-robust distributed learning under LDP constraints. We corroborate and further analyze these theoretical findings with empirical evaluations.

AI.tldr: Generalization error in Byzantine-robust distributed learning with local differential privacy (LDP) does not always suffer from the privacy-robustness tradeoff; its behavior is regime-dependent. In strong privacy (high noise), stronger privacy improves generalization; in weaker privacy (low noise), stronger privacy degrades generalization, explained by stability bounds and supported by experiments.
AI.motivation: To resolve how Byzantine robustness, LDP, and optimization error jointly affect generalization error, and to determine whether the previously reported trilemma extends to generalization.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis deriving matching lower and upper bounds on algorithmic stability for Byzantine-robust distributed learning under LDP; partitioning into high-noise (strong privacy) and low-noise (weak privacy) regimes; and empirical validation.
AI.result: Non-monotonic generalization behavior: in the high-noise regime, increasing privacy reduces generalization error (no tension with robustness); in the low-noise regime, increasing privacy degrades generalization due to renewed tension between robustness and privacy. Stability bounds explain the phenomenon, and experiments corroborate the theory.
AI.conclusion: Generalization error adherence to the privacy-robustness tradeoff is regime-dependent. Strong privacy can benefit generalization in the presence of Byzantine robustness, while weaker privacy reintroduces the tradeoff. Design of privacy-preserving Byzantine-robust systems should consider the privacy regime to optimize generalization.

title: NEUROSYMLAND: Neuro-Symbolic Landing-Site Assessment for Robust and Edge-Deployable UAV Autonomy
summary: Safe landing-site assessment in unstructured environments remains a key challenge for autonomous UAV deployment, as vision-only learning approaches often degrade under terrain variability and provide limited transparency in safety decisions. We present NEUROSYMLAND, a neuro-symbolic landing-site assessment system that integrates lightweight perception with explicit safety reasoning. The framework constructs a probabilistic semantic scene graph from onboard visual input and evaluates candidate landing regions using symbolic constraints capturing terrain flatness, obstacle clearance, and spatial consistency, enabling structured reasoning under perceptual uncertainty while maintaining edge-feasible execution. Across 72 simulated landing scenarios spanning diverse terrains, NEUROSYMLAND achieves 61 successful assessments, outperforming four competitive baselines (37-57 successes). To evaluate deployability, we further conduct 100 hardware-in-the-loop trials with randomized initial poses, profiling end-to-end latency, stage-wise execution time, and system-level metrics including CPU/GPU utilization, memory footprint, and power consumption. Results demonstrate improved robustness and interpretability with bounded edge-resource usage. Profiling shows that symbolic reasoning contributes only a small fraction of end-to-end latency, while the main computational cost arises from perception and PSSG construction. These results demonstrate the feasibility of deploying the landing-site assessment stack on edge-constrained UAV hardware, and all source code, datasets, prompts, and symbolic rule refinement examples are released in an open-source repository

AI.tldr: Neuro-symbolic landing-site assessment (NEUROSYMLAND) combines lightweight perception with explicit safety reasoning via a probabilistic semantic scene graph to assess safe UAV landing sites under perceptual uncertainty, achieving robust edge deployments and interpretability.
AI.motivation: Vision-only learning approaches struggle with terrain variability and lack transparent safety decisions, hindering reliable, edge-deployed UAV landing in unstructured environments.
AI.method: Builds a probabilistic semantic scene graph (PSSG) from onboard visuals and applies symbolic constraints on candidate landing regions for terrain flatness, obstacle clearance, and spatial consistency; analyzes safety with structured reasoning while keeping edge-resource usage bounded.
AI.result: In 72 simulated scenarios, NEUROSYMLAND achieves 61 successful assessments (vs baselines 37–57). Hardware-in-the-loop trials (100 runs) show robust performance with bounded latency; symbolic reasoning contributes a small fraction to end-to-end latency, with perception and PSSG construction as the main cost; edge deployment feasibility demonstrated.
AI.conclusion: The work proves the feasibility of edge-constrained UAV landing-site assessment using a neuro-symbolic framework, highlighting improved interpretability and resource efficiency; all source code, datasets, prompts, and symbolic rules are released as open source.

title: Autonomous discovery of traffic laws with AI traffic scientists
summary: Universal traffic laws describe recurrent patterns in congestion, mobility and driving behavior across cities, providing a scientific basis for transportation planning, management and control. Their discovery, however, remains expert-driven, requiring candidate regularities to be identified from heterogeneous observational evidence or validated through intervention experiments. Although autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) systems have advanced scientific discovery in controlled laboratory settings, extending them to complex transportation domains remains a challenge. Here we present TrafficSci, an agentic AI system that formulates traffic-law discovery as an iterative, auditable workflow integrating evidence scoping, critic-judge hypothesis induction, and observational-interventional validation. Across four case studies spanning population, network, control and trajectory scales, TrafficSci autonomously rediscovers three established traffic laws and identifies an unreported intrinsic temporal memory scale in urban driving behavior, statistically consistent across eight cities and two trajectory datasets. TrafficSci provides a route for extending AI-driven scientific discovery from controlled domains to complex urban systems.

AI.tldr: TrafficSci is an agentic AI system that autonomously discovers universal traffic laws through an auditable, iterative workflow; it rediscovers three known laws and reveals a new intrinsic temporal memory scale across eight cities and two trajectory datasets, illustrating AI-driven discovery can extend to complex urban systems.
AI.motivation: To move beyond expert-driven identification of traffic regularities and enable scalable, auditable AI-driven scientific discovery in complex urban transportation, improving planning, management, and control.
AI.method: An iterative, auditable workflow combining evidence scoping, critic-judge hypothesis induction, and observational-interventional validation. The system was evaluated across four scales (population, network, control, trajectory) in four case studies, autonomously rediscovering three established traffic laws and uncovering a new intrinsic temporal memory scale, with results corroborated across eight cities and two trajectory datasets.
AI.result: TrafficSci successfully rediscovered three established traffic laws and identified a previously unreported intrinsic temporal memory scale in urban driving behavior. Findings were statistically consistent across eight cities and two trajectory datasets, indicating robust cross-city applicability and tool effectiveness for autonomous discovery in urban transport.
AI.conclusion: The work demonstrates a viable path for extending AI-driven scientific discovery from controlled laboratory domains to complex, real-world urban systems. It highlights the potential for agentic AI to uncover, verify, and interpret universal traffic laws at multiple scales, while also suggesting avenues for broader validation, additional laws, and improved interpretability and auditable governance in future work.

title: Bridging 3D Gaussians and Semantic Occupancy for Comprehensive Open-Vocabulary Scene Understanding from Unposed Images
comment: Hu Zhu, Bohan Li, and Xianda Guo contributed equally. Corresponding author: Wenjun Zeng
summary: Comprehensive 3D scene understanding from sparse, unposed images requires a model to recover renderable geometry, open-vocabulary semantics, and free/occupied 3D space without relying on external camera calibration. Recent feed-forward Gaussian methods improve pose-free reconstruction and semantic rendering, but their Gaussian primitives are mainly optimized through image-space objectives and remain weakly constrained in unobserved regions. We propose \textit{COVScene}, a pose-free semantic Gaussian framework that couples renderable Gaussian primitives with a dense semantic occupancy field through differentiable volumetric lifting. Instead of converting Gaussians to voxels only at evaluation time, COVScene lifts the predicted semantic Gaussians inside the training computation graph, so volumetric regularization provides gradients to Gaussian opacity, geometry, and semantic features. The framework combines a semantic-aware Geometry Transformer, multi-task Gaussian decoding, geometric foundation distillation, and occupancy entropy regularization to support novel view synthesis, open-vocabulary semantic querying, and semantic occupancy prediction within a single representation. Experiments on ScanNet and ScanNet++ show that COVScene maintains competitive rendering quality, improves open-vocabulary segmentation, and achieves stronger semantic occupancy prediction than the self-supervised baseline without direct voxel-level supervision.

AI.tldr: COVScene is a pose-free semantic Gaussian framework that tightly couples renderable Gaussian primitives with a dense semantic occupancy field via differentiable volumetric lifting, enabling open-vocabulary semantics and semantic occupancy prediction with competitive rendering quality.
AI.motivation: To enable comprehensive, pose-free 3D scene understanding from sparse, unposed images by jointly constraining geometry and semantics in a volumetric framework, addressing weak constraints in unobserved regions of image-space–optimized Gaussian methods.
AI.method: Introduce differentiable volumetric lifting that integrates predicted semantic Gaussians with a dense semantic occupancy field within the training graph. Key components include a semantic-aware Geometry Transformer, multi-task Gaussian decoding, geometric foundation distillation, and occupancy entropy regularization, enabling joint optimization for renderable geometry, opacity, and semantic features without external camera calibration.
AI.result: On ScanNet and ScanNet++, COVScene achieves competitive rendering quality, improved open-vocabulary semantic segmentation, and stronger semantic occupancy prediction compared with a self-supervised baseline lacking voxel-level supervision.
AI.conclusion: A single representation that supports novel view synthesis, open-vocabulary querying, and semantic occupancy prediction in a pose-free setting, demonstrated with strong results on standard datasets.

title: Towards Learning Representations of Policies in Two-Player Zero-Sum Imperfect-Information Games
summary:
We investigate the problem of learning useful policy representations (embeddings) in two-player zero-sum imperfect-information games. We make three contributions: First, we introduce methods of creating datasets of policies for a given game. Second, we propose methods to learn policy representations. Third, we introduce downstream tasks to evaluate the effectiveness of such representations.
  We evaluate each dataset method, embedding method, and downstream task on Kuhn and Leduc Poker. Although our methods are very basic, we demonstrate that useful behavioral representations are present in the learned embeddings. To our knowledge, this work is among the first to systematically compare self-supervised learning techniques for learning policy representations in games. Our code is available at https://github.com/VitamintK/ssl-project for others to extend.

AI.tldr: Introduces datasets of policies, SSL-based policy embeddings, and downstream tasks for two-player zero-sum imperfect-information games; evaluates on Kuhn and Leduc Poker; shows embeddings capture meaningful behavioral structure; code released for extension.
AI.motivation: Address the lack of standardized datasets and evaluation benchmarks for learning policy representations in imperfect-information games and enable systematic comparison of self-supervised learning techniques.
AI.method: Threefold approach: (1) create datasets of policies for a given game; (2) develop self-supervised methods to learn policy embeddings; (3) design downstream tasks to evaluate embedding usefulness; empirical evaluation on Kuhn and Leduc Poker.
AI.result: Embeddings learned via SSL reveal useful behavioral representations; even basic methods uncover structure; among the first works to systematically compare SSL techniques for policy representations in games; code available for extension.
AI.conclusion: SSL-derived policy representations can meaningfully capture behavioral structure in imperfect-information games; provides benchmarks and baselines, facilitating future work on larger games and more advanced SSL methods.

title: Real-Time Visual Intelligence on Low-Cost UAVs: A Modular Approach for Tracking, Scanning, and Navigation
comment: 6 pages, 5 figures. Project repository available at: github.com
summary: Autonomous drones are rapidly transforming modern warfare and civil applications alike. This paper presents the development of an integrated intelligent drone system designed to serve as a personal assistant. Leveraging the DJI Tello drone platform, we implemented a modular architecture that integrates three core artificial intelligence functionalities: facial detection, facial recognition, and depth estimation from monocular vision. A web-based interface enables seamless drone control and real-time video monitoring, while a Python-based server processes visual data and executes inference pipelines using lightweight neural models optimized for embedded systems. Unlike existing commercial solutions, this system emphasizes accessibility, low-cost hardware, and open-source technologies. The system demonstrates robust performance in real-world conditions, including person tracking, indoor scanning, and autonomous line following using virtual sensors. This project validates the applicability of advanced AI techniques in real-time robotic systems and illustrates the feasibility of deploying them on constrained hardware, providing a foundation for future research in autonomous UAVs for military, rescue, and surveillance missions.

AI.tldr: An integrated, open-source, low-cost AI-enabled drone system on a consumer platform that performs facial detection, recognition, and monocular depth estimation with a web interface and lightweight models, demonstrating real-time inference on constrained hardware.
AI.motivation: Democratize access to AI-powered autonomous drones by integrating multiple perception modules on a consumer-grade platform and showcasing real-time performance on embedded hardware.
AI.method: Modular architecture on the DJI Tello platform, implementing facial detection, facial recognition, and monocular depth estimation. A web-based interface enables control and real-time video monitoring; a Python server processes data and runs lightweight neural models optimized for embedded systems; real-time inference pipelines and virtual sensors enable tasks such as person tracking, indoor scanning, and autonomous line following.
AI.result: Demonstrates feasibility and robustness of real-time AI on constrained hardware in real-world conditions, including tracking and navigation tasks; emphasizes accessibility and open-source approach; provides a foundation for further UAV research in civilian and dual-use applications.
AI.conclusion: The work validates deploying advanced AI techniques on embedded robotic platforms, highlighting open-source, low-cost hardware as a viable path for future autonomous UAV research in civilian, rescue, and surveillance domains.

title: Diverse Evidence, Better Forecasts: Multi-Agent Deliberation Under Information Asymmetry
summary: Multi-agent systems are increasingly used for forecasting future events, as deliberation among multiple LLMs is believed to improve reasoning and calibration. Yet existing approaches overlook a critical design choice: what information each agent receives. When all agents are given identical evidence, deliberation collapses into herding rather than genuine belief revision, leaving multi-agent systems little better than a single agent. We identify this as a fundamental gap and propose designed information asymmetry to close it: by partitioning evidence into shared public and disjoint private subsets, each agent holds exclusive knowledge that can only reach others through deliberation. We theoretically show that this decomposition reduces inter-agent error correlation, and instantiate it in InfoDelphi, a framework combining relevance-aware evidence routing, rationale-based iterative deliberation, and confidence-weighted aggregation. On PolyGym, a benchmark of 375 binary forecasting questions derived from real-world prediction markets, InfoDelphi outperforms the strongest single-agent and multi-agent baselines by 12--18% in Brier score and 4--8 percentage points in accuracy. More detailed experiments confirm that removing information asymmetry eliminates most deliberation gains, establishing diversity of input as the key enabler of effective multi-agent reasoning.

AI.tldr: Proposes information asymmetry among agents to avoid herding in multi-agent LLM forecasting and shows that private/public evidence partitioning reduces error correlation; introduces InfoDelphi with routing, rationale deliberation, and confidence-weighted aggregation, achieving notable gains on PolyGym.
AI.motivation: To address the failure mode in multi-agent deliberation where identical evidence leads to correlated errors and reduced belief revision, by introducing exclusive private information to agents to foster diverse input and better calibration.
AI.method: Partition evidence into shared public and disjoint private subsets; develop relevance-aware routing, reasoning-based iterative deliberation, and confidence-weighted aggregation (InfoDelphi); provide theoretical analysis of reduced inter-agent error correlation; evaluate on PolyGym with 375 binary forecasting questions; conduct ablations removing information asymmetry.
AI.result: InfoDelphi outperforms strongest single-agent and multi-agent baselines by 12–18% in Brier score and 4–8 percentage points in accuracy; ablations show removing information asymmetry eliminates most gains; demonstrates input diversity as key for multi-agent reasoning.
AI.conclusion: Designed information asymmetry is a viable design choice to improve multi-agent forecasting by reducing correlated errors and enhancing reasoning via diverse evidence; InfoDelphi combines routing, reasoning, and aggregation to realize these gains.

title: Multi-Resolution Flow Matching: Training-Free Diffusion Acceleration via Staged Sampling
comment: The code is available at https://github.com/Xingyu-Zheng/MrFlow
summary: Hardware-agnostic strategies for accelerating text-to-image diffusion, such as timestep distillation and feature caching, can reduce inference time without custom kernels or system-level optimization. Among them, multi-resolution generation strategies have recently received broad attention, attaining more than 5x speedup without any training. However, the design of performing upsampling in the latent space, together with the selective modification of partial regions, causes these methods to exhibit noticeable blurring or artifacts. To this end, we propose MrFlow, a training-free multi-resolution acceleration strategy for pretrained flow-matching models built upon a staged low-to-high-resolution pipeline. MrFlow first rapidly generates the main structure at low resolution, then performs super-resolution in the pixel space using a lightweight pretrained GAN-based model, subsequently injects low-strength noise to enable high-frequency resampling, and finally refines the details at high resolution. Quantitative and qualitative results on FLUX.1-dev and Qwen-Image show that MrFlow exploits the quadratic token reduction and reduced step requirement of low-resolution sampling to achieve 10x end-to-end acceleration while keeping OneIG within a 1% gap relative to that before acceleration, significantly surpassing other training-free acceleration strategies, and requiring no training or runtime dynamic identification whatsoever. MrFlow can further be directly combined orthogonally with pre-trained timestep distillation strategies, achieving even higher generation acceleration of up to 25x.

AI.tldr: MrFlow is a training-free, multi-resolution acceleration method for pretrained flow-matching diffusion models. It combines low-resolution structure generation with pixel-space super-resolution, light noise injection for high-frequency resampling, and high-resolution refinement, achieving up to 10x end-to-end speedups (up to 25x with timestep distillation) while maintaining near-original quality.
AI.motivation: Hardware-agnostic acceleration for text-to-image diffusion that avoids training or runtime optimization, addressing blurring/artifacts from latent-space upsampling and partial-region modification.
AI.method: A staged low-to-high-resolution pipeline: (1) generate main structure at low resolution; (2) perform pixel-space super-resolution with a lightweight pretrained GAN-based model; (3) inject low-strength noise to enable high-frequency resampling; (4) refine high-resolution details. Leverages quadratic token reduction and reduced-step low-res sampling; compatible with pretrained timestep distillation.
AI.result: On FLUX.1-dev and Qwen-Image, MrFlow achieves 10x end-to-end acceleration with OneIG within 1% of the unaccelerated baseline and outperforms other training-free strategies. When combined orthogonally with pretrained timestep distillation, acceleration increases to up to 25x.
AI.conclusion: MrFlow provides a training-free, hardware-agnostic route to substantial diffusion-model acceleration via a structured low-to-high-resolution workflow, with minimal quality loss. It can be complemented by existing distillation methods for further gains.

title: The risk of KV cache compression
summary: Transformer inference on long sequences is expensive because softmax attention repeatedly reads from a large KV cache. The prevalent approach to this bottleneck is KV cache compression, which replaces the full cache with a compact summary. Despite its practical importance, the design of such summaries is largely driven by empirical experimentation. On the theoretical side, existing results show that KV cache compression can be impossible in the worst case, but offer little systematic guidance for designing algorithms in regimes where accurate compression is possible. We bridge this gap by characterizing the minimax risk of KV cache compression in terms of the intrinsic compressibility of a cache, revealing when and how accurate compression is possible. These results yield novel design principles for KV cache compression under causal masking that map efficiently to prefill and autoregressive decoding while achieving minimax-optimal risk. We instantiate these principles in a practical algorithm and report promising performance on LongBench in targeted experiments. Overall, our results provide a principled avenue for practical KV cache compression with theoretical guarantees.

AI.tldr: Characterizes the minimax risk of KV cache compression for transformer inference using cache compressibility; derives design principles under causal masking; implements a practical algorithm with minimax-optimal guarantees and good LongBench performance.
AI.motivation: Bridging theory and practice in KV cache compression, addressing both negative worst-case results and the need for principled guidance for when accurate compression is possible.
AI.method: Theoretical minimax analysis parameterized by intrinsic cache compressibility; development of design principles for prefill and autoregressive decoding; mapping to causal masking; algorithm instantiation.
AI.result: Minimax-optimal risk achieved by the proposed design; promising empirical performance on LongBench in targeted experiments.
AI.conclusion: Offers a principled framework with theoretical guarantees for KV cache compression in transformer inference and a practical algorithm capable of near-optimal performance.

title: The Moving Eye: Enhancing VLA Spatial Generalization via Hybrid Dynamic Data Collection
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown remarkable promise in generalized robotic manipulation. However, their spatial generalization remains fragile. We argue that simply increasing the number of viewpoints is insufficient. Models often fall into the trap of Shortcut Learning, latching onto spurious correlations (e.g., fixed relative poses between objects or between the camera and robot base) rather than learning true spatial relationships. In this work, we propose a data-centric solution to enhance VLA spatial generalization. We utilize a dual-arm setup where one arm performs manipulation while the other serves as a mobile environmental camera. We systematically evaluate three data distribution patterns: Fixed, Multi-Fixed, and Moving Views. Our findings reveal that a hybrid strategy, combining continuous camera motion with diverse static viewpoints, yields the best performance by substantially reducing spurious correlations while maintaining training stability. Our experiments demonstrate that this strategy mitigates spurious correlations, enabling VLAs to generalize to unseen camera poses and object configurations where simply adding more static viewpoints fails. Crucially, we reveal that the susceptibility to shortcut learning and the struggle with spatial generalization are universal characteristics shared across diverse architectures. Consequently, all evaluated models (ACT, Diffusion, and VLA models including Pi0 and Gr00t) benefit significantly from our mixed data strategy.

AI.tldr: Hybrid data strategy with moving and diverse static viewpoints improves spatial generalization in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models by mitigating shortcut learning across architectures.
AI.motivation: Address fragility of spatial generalization in VLA models caused by shortcut learning and reliance on spurious correlations (e.g., fixed relative poses).
AI.method: Use a dual-arm setup: one arm manipulates while the other acts as a mobile environmental camera. Compare three data distributions—Fixed, Multi-Fixed, and Moving Views—and identify a hybrid strategy (continuous camera motion + diverse static viewpoints) as most effective. Evaluate across multiple architectures (ACT, Diffusion, and VLA models including Pi0 and Gr00t).
AI.result: Hybrid strategy substantially reduces spurious correlations and enables generalization to unseen camera poses and object configurations that fail under purely static viewpoints; the benefit generalizes across different model architectures.
AI.conclusion: Data-centric viewpoint dynamics (motion plus diverse static views) is key to robust spatial generalization in VLA systems, with universal gains across architectures. The mixed data strategy should be preferred over simply increasing static viewpoints; further work could explore real-world deployment and optimization.

title: Separating Expert Retention from Autonomous Source Inference in Raw-ECG-Replay-Free Continual ECG Deployment
summary:
In multi-source ECG deployment, models may need to incorporate new data sources when earlier raw ECGs cannot be retained or replayed. Freezing a pretrained backbone and assigning each source an isolated classifier prevents parameter interference, but deployment still requires selecting an expert when source metadata are unavailable. We study this distinction through \ours{}, an incremental expert bank built on frozen 1024-dimensional ECGFounder features. Each arriving domain adds a balanced-softmax linear expert, while a lightweight router is fitted only on retained training features and domain labels from sources observed so far. A validation-calibrated margin rule fuses the two most likely experts instead of committing to a single routed expert.
  On CPSC, PTB-XL, Georgia, and Chapman-Shaoxing, source-aware expert selection reaches $0.7915\pm0.0036$ Macro-F1 and a matched offline independent-head reference reaches $0.7885\pm0.0009$, supporting strong source-aware expert retention. Without source IDs, an MLP router reaches $0.7756\pm0.0027$ and top-2 margin fusion reaches $0.7782\pm0.0022$. The top-2 gain over hard MLP routing is small ($+0.0026$), with a 95\% confidence interval from paired bootstrap that includes zero. Across three domain orders, the top-2-to-oracle gap remains $0.0111$--$0.0133$, identifying autonomous source inference as the main remaining bottleneck. No raw ECGs are replayed, but frozen training features are retained for router updates; the method is therefore not memory-free.

AI.tldr: Incremental source-aware experts built on frozen ECG features, with a lightweight router and margin-based fusion; strong performance close to offline reference, but autonomous source inference remains a bottleneck; data retained features imply not memory-free.
AI.motivation: In multi-source ECG deployment, raw ECGs may not be retainable for replay; need to avoid parameter interference across sources while enabling progressive integration of new domains.
AI.method: Freeze a pretrained backbone; assign each source its own balanced-softmax linear expert; incrementally add a domain-specific expert for each arriving source; train a lightweight router on retained training features and their domain labels; fuse the two most likely experts using a validation-calibrated margin rule rather than selecting a single routed expert.
AI.result: On CPSC, PTB-XL, Georgia, Chapman-Shaoxing, source-aware expert selection achieves Macro-F1 0.7915±0.0036, matching offline reference 0.7885±0.0009. Without source IDs, an MLP router attains 0.7756±0.0027 and top-2 margin fusion 0.7782±0.0022; top-2 gain over hard routing is small. Across three domain orders, top-2-to-oracle gap is 0.0111–0.0133. No raw ECGs are replayed; features are retained for router updates; method is not memory-free.
AI.conclusion: An effective incremental, source-aware expert bank with margin-based fusion can approach offline performance without replaying raw data; autonomous source inference remains the main bottleneck and feature retention implies limited memory-freeness.

title: Boosting Ultrasound Image Classification via Attribute-Guided Dual-Branch Framework
summary: Ultrasound image classification is essential for computer-aided diagnosis. However, current methods often neglect clinical priors, leading to poor generalization in challenging scenarios and a lack of interpretability that limits clinical adoption. To address these issues, we aim to develop a medical-prior module that can be seamlessly integrated into existing pipelines to enhance both diagnostic performance and interpretability. In this paper, we propose an attribute-guided dual-branch framework for ultrasound classification that introduces domain-agnostic medical attribute priors, improving generalization while offering interpretable evidence. Specifically, a baseline branch follows conventional architectures and predicts image categories via a fully connected classifier. An attribute-guided branch injects domain-agnostic attributes as priors and produces human-interpretable decision cues. Finally, an adaptive decision module fuses the two branches in a data-dependent manner to yield the final prediction. Experiments across diverse ultrasound classification tasks demonstrate that our approach can be integrated into multiple backbones and state-of-the-art methods with low overhead, consistently improving accuracy and interpretability. Code is available at: https://github.com/zhaobo253-crypto/AttrGuide.

AI.tldr: An attribute-guided dual-branch framework adds domain-agnostic medical attribute priors to ultrasound classification, with adaptive fusion to boost accuracy and interpretability while remaining lightweight.
AI.motivation: Current ultrasound classifiers often ignore clinical priors, causing poor generalization in challenging cases and limited interpretability, hindering clinical adoption.
AI.method: A dual-branch architecture: (i) a baseline branch with standard architectures and a fully connected classifier; (ii) an attribute-guided branch that injects domain-agnostic medical attributes as priors to produce interpretable decision cues. An adaptive decision module fuses the branches in a data-dependent way to yield the final prediction.
AI.result: Across diverse ultrasound tasks, the approach integrates with multiple backbones and SOTA methods with low overhead, yielding consistent improvements in accuracy and interpretability.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides generalizable, interpretable improvements suitable for integration into existing pipelines, with potential for broader clinical impact and future extension by incorporating additional priors or tasks.

title: Multi-Head Recurrent Memory Agents
summary: Recurrent memory agents extend LLMs to arbitrarily long contexts by iteratively consolidating input into a fixed-size memory window. Despite their scalability, these agents exhibit a well-documented reliability problem: end-to-end performance degrades systematically as context length grows. We diagnose this failure by decomposing performance into two factors--memory capture and memory retention--and quantitatively confirm that retention is the dominant bottleneck. Retention collapses because existing designs maintain memory as a monolithic text block, forcing every update to risk overwriting previously retained content. Motivated by this diagnosis, we propose Multi-Head Recurrent Memory (MHM), a general, training-free framework that partitions memory into independent heads governed by a stage-wise select-then-update strategy. At each step, exactly one head is selected for update while the remaining heads are structurally shielded from overwriting, shifting the burden of retention from model behavior to architectural design. As a lightweight instantiation, we introduce Least-Recently-Updated MHM (MHM-LRU), which guarantees uniform head utilization with zero additional token overhead. Extensive experiments on long-context benchmarks show that MHM-LRU substantially improves both retention and end-to-end accuracy across the 100K--1M token range, where baselines degrade sharply. On RULER-HQA at 896K tokens, MHM-LRU improves the memory retention rate from less than 30% to 73.96%. These gains generalize across model families, scales, and task types, positioning architectural optimization as a practical and cost-efficient path toward reliable long-context recurrent memory.

AI.tldr: A multi-head memory architecture (MHM) with a training-free, select-then-update scheme improves retention and long-context accuracy for recurrent memory agents; MHM-LRU instantiates with least-recently-updated heads to ensure uniform usage and zero token overhead, yielding substantial gains on long-token benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing recurrent memory agents suffer from a retention bottleneck: treating memory as a monolithic text blob causes updates to overwrite prior content as context grows. The authors decompose performance into memory capture and retention, finding retention to be dominant.
AI.method: Propose MHM framework partitioning memory into independent heads with stage-wise select-then-update; at each step, update exactly one head while shielding others. Provide MHM-LRU as a lightweight instantiation with no extra token cost.
AI.result: Empirical results show improved retention and end-to-end accuracy on long contexts (100K–1M tokens); on RULER-HQA at 896K tokens, retention rises from <30% to 73.96%; gains generalize across models, scales, and task types.
AI.conclusion: Architectural memory design, rather than purely model-based changes, offers a practical path to reliable long-context performance; MHM-LRU is a simple, effective, training-free approach with broad applicability.

title: HEFT: Heavy-Payload Full-size Humanoid Teleoperation with Privileged Motion Guidance and Windowed Payload Curriculum
summary: General motion tracking and teleoperation offer a promising path to scalable humanoid skill acquisition, yet most existing frameworks are validated on compact platforms or without real payload interaction, leaving full-size humanoids with real payloads largely unexplored. Scaling to full-size humanoids introduces two compounding challenges: their larger inertia and tighter balance margins make tracking highly sensitive to noise, drift, and retargeting errors from commodity VR trackers, while their payload potential remains largely underutilized. We present HEFT, a heavy-payload full-size humanoid teleoperation framework that addresses both challenges. HEFT learns from deployable noisy VR references with physically plausible reconstructed references through Privileged Motion Guidance (PMG), and uses a Windowed Payload Curriculum (WPC) with expert-guided payload caps to acquire robust heavy-payload tracking. We deploy HEFT on L7, a 175cm, 65kg humanoid. The robot tracks motions including turns, forward/backward locomotion, and squats under payloads up to 24kg.

AI.tldr: HEFT enables heavy-payload full-size humanoid teleoperation by combining Privileged Motion Guidance (PMG) with a Windowed Payload Curriculum (WPC) to robustly track motions (turns, locomotion, squats) under up to 24 kg payload on a 1.75 m, 65 kg humanoid (L7).
AI.motivation: Full-size humanoids interacting with real payloads face high sensitivity to noise, drift, and retargeting from commodity VR trackers due to larger inertia and tight balance margins. There is a need for robust, scalable teleoperation frameworks that can leverage payload potential without sacrificing stability.
AI.method: The framework uses Privileged Motion Guidance to reconstruct physically plausible references from noisy VR cues (learning from privileged data). It introduces a Windowed Payload Curriculum with expert-guided payload caps to progressively train robust tracking. Deployment tested on L7 (175 cm, 65 kg) with payloads up to 24 kg, validating turns, locomotion, and squats.
AI.result: Empirically demonstrated stable tracking of diverse motions under up to 24 kg payload on a full-size humanoid (L7), including turning, forward/backward locomotion, and squats.
AI.conclusion: HEFT presents a viable path for robust, heavy-payload full-size humanoid teleoperation by integrating privileged guidance with curriculum-based payload exposure. It addresses noise and drift in VR references and demonstrates practical payload handling. Further work could explore generalization to different tasks, payload variations, and long-term deployment in real environments.

title: Epistemic Goggles: A Pretrained Module that Induces an Epistemic Frame via Gradient Editing
comment: 20 pages, 10 figures, 2 tables. Code at https://github.com/JoshuaSP/epistemic-goggles and generated documents, questions, and teacher rollouts at https://huggingface.co/datasets/joshuapenman/epistemic-goggles-artifacts
summary: Finetuning a language model on documents that are explicitly annotated as fictional results in a model that still actually believes the documents' core claims, an effect known as Negation Neglect. In our evaluations, models trained on documents prefixed and suffixed with such annotations correctly identify the relevant claims as fictional only about 9% of the time. To address this, we introduce Goggles, a learned module that intervenes on the finetuning gradient rather than the data. During supervised finetuning, a Goggles module edits the gradients an LLM LoRA receives, imparting a chosen epistemic frame (the stance the model takes toward the nature of what it reads) to whatever the documents teach. A Goggles instance is trained once for a given base model, frame, and LoRA configuration, then applied frozen to documents it was never trained on. Trained through Goggles on those same documents, now carrying no fictional annotation, the model flags the content as fictional roughly 91% of the time, while preserving capability (GPQA and TruthfulQA match or exceed baseline). The same architecture supports other frames: a Goggles instance can be trained to treat documents as "part of an AI safety evaluation by Redwood Research" rather than simply as fiction. The imparted frame persists under continued finetuning that pushes back toward the claim, where prior interventions revert. Goggles suggests a path toward training language models on known-misaligned data without absorbing the behaviors that data demonstrates.

AI.tldr: Goggles is a gradient-editing module that injects a chosen epistemic frame during finetuning to counter Negation Neglect. It converts misinterpreted fictional content into recognized fiction while preserving overall model capabilities, achieving ~91% fictionalization after training, with baseline ~9%.
AI.motivation: Prevent Negation Neglect when training on annotated-fiction documents and enable controlled, frame-consistent behavior without altering the data itself; enable robust handling of misaligned, annotated data.
AI.method: During supervised finetuning of a LoRA-adapted LLM, a Goggles module edits the backpropagated gradients to impart a specified epistemic frame to the model. A Goggles instance is trained once for a given base model, frame, and LoRA configuration and remains frozen when applied to unseen documents. Re-training with the same documents without annotation carries no fictional bias, but the Goggles frame persists and can be undone by continued finetuning that pushes back toward the original claim.
AI.result: Baseline performance for identifying fictional content is ~9%. After applying Goggles, the model flags content as fictional ~91% of the time on the same docs it was trained on, while maintaining or improving GPQA and TruthfulQA performance relative to baselines.
AI.conclusion: Gradient-level intervention via Goggles offers a viable path to training models on misaligned data without absorbing the demonstrated behaviors, and can generalize across frames (e.g., fictional vs. AI-safety framing).

title: Plug-and-Play Volumetric Reconstruction for Compressive Sensing Light-Sheet Microscopy
summary: We investigate volumetric reconstruction for compressive sensing light-sheet microscopy (CS-LSM), where fast volumetric imaging is achieved by encoding multiple axial planes into each camera exposure. To recover the underlying volume from highly multiplexed measurements, we propose a plug-and-play (PnP) framework that flexibly incorporates any user-specified denoiser into the reconstruction process. Building on a slice-based formulation, we further introduce an axial-coupled model that exploits correlations between adjacent slices to improve volumetric continuity. For efficient computation, we derive a Woodbury-based update for the data-consistency step in both the slice-based and axial-coupled formulations, and employ a Gauss-Seidel sweep for the denoising step in the axial-coupled model. Under a weakly convex regularization assumption, we establish subsequential convergence of the proposed algorithm. Experiments on synthetic and real zebrafish-heart data demonstrate that the proposed framework successfully recovers cellular structures from compressed measurements, and provide practical insights into the comparative performance of commonly used denoisers within the PnP framework under the CS-LSM setup.

AI.tldr: Plug-and-play framework for CS-LSM volumetric reconstruction using flexible denoisers, introducing an axial-coupled model to exploit inter-slice correlations. Achieves computational efficiency via Woodbury-based data consistency updates and Gauss-Seidel denoising sweep. Subsequence convergence guaranteed under weakly convex regularization. Demonstrated on synthetic and zebrafish-heart data with insights into denoiser performance.
AI.motivation: To enable fast, accurate 3D reconstruction from multiplexed compressive measurements in light-sheet microscopy by integrating flexible denoisers within a reconstruction framework, while leveraging axial slice correlations for volumetric continuity and ensuring computational efficiency and convergence.
AI.method: A plug-and-play reconstruction framework using both a slice-based formulation and an axial-coupled model. Data-consistency updates leverage Woodbury identity for efficiency; denoising step uses Gauss-Seidel sweep in the axial-coupled setting. Convergence analysis under a weakly convex regularization assumption yields subsequential convergence.
AI.result: The framework successfully recovers cellular structures from compressed CS-LSM measurements. It demonstrates practical performance and provides comparative insights into denoiser choices within the PnP-CS-LSM setting, validated on synthetic data and real zebrafish-heart data.
AI.conclusion: The proposed PnP-CS-LSM framework effectively enables high-quality volumetric reconstructions from highly multiplexed measurements, with axial coupling improving continuity, computationally efficient updates, and proven subsequential convergence under mild regularity. It offers practical guidance on denoiser selection for CS-LSM.
