The code is available at: https://github.com/weiyixue999/Signal_Structure_Aware_Gaussian

AI.tldr: SIG scheduler aligns image supervision with Gaussian frequencies for 3D Gaussian Splatting in large-scale scenes, improving efficiency and rendering quality.
AI.motivation: Large-scale scenes have sparse observations; naive Gaussian densification driven by high-frequency images causes inefficiency and redundant primitives. A frequency-aware, geometry-aware training framework is needed to ensure stable convergence and high-quality reconstructions.
AI.method: Derive the average sampling frequency and bandwidth of 3D representations, regulate training image resolution and Gaussian densification based on scene frequency convergence; introduce Sphere-Constrained Gaussians leveraging initialized point-cloud priors to constrain Gaussian optimization; implement a frequency-consistent training regime (SIG) for synchronized supervision across frequencies.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art efficiency and rendering quality on large-scale scenes, with floater-free training and improved convergence; code released.
AI.conclusion: Frequency-aware, structure-recovery based training enables robust, scalable 3D scene reconstruction with fewer redundant primitives and improved rendering performance.

title: MKGR: Multimodal Knowledge-Graph Representation Learning for Cold-Start Protein-Protein Interaction Prediction
summary: Accurate protein-protein interaction (PPI) prediction is central to functional genomics, disease mechanism discovery, and drug development. A difficult setting arises when candidate interactions include proteins that have no observed PPI edges during training, where models relying on network topology alone often lose useful context. This paper presents \method, a multimodal representation framework for cold-start PPI prediction. \method\ combines region-aware protein sequence encoding with four protein-centered biomedical knowledge graphs, including protein-drug, protein-disease, protein-miRNA, and protein-lncRNA associations. The sequence branch extracts contextual representations from structurally informed sequence regions, while graph attention encoders learn modality-specific protein embeddings from sparse biomedical associations. A bridge reconstruction objective regularizes graph learning by recovering shared protein-entity associations, and a pair-level gating module adaptively integrates sequence and graph evidence for each candidate protein pair. Experiments on two benchmark datasets under novel-old and novel-novel cold-start settings show that \method\ consistently outperforms competitive sequence, network, and knowledge-graph baselines across ACC, F1, AUC, AUPR, and MCC.

AI.tldr: Multimodal cold-start PPI predictor that fuses region-aware sequence encoding with four protein-centered knowledge graphs, using bridge reconstruction and pair-level gating to improve predictions in novel settings.
AI.motivation: In cold-start PPI scenarios where proteins have no observed PPI edges in training, reliance on network topology is insufficient; integrating sequence context with heterogeneous biomedical associations can improve predictive performance.
AI.method: A sequence branch extracts contextual representations from structurally informed sequence regions. Graph attention encoders learn protein embeddings from four protein-centered graphs: protein-drug, protein-disease, protein-miRNA, and protein-lncRNA. A bridge reconstruction objective regularizes graph learning by recovering shared protein-entity associations. A pair-level gating module adaptively fuses sequence and graph evidence for each candidate protein pair.
AI.result: On two benchmark datasets under novel-old and novel-novel cold-start settings, the method consistently outperforms competitive sequence, network, and knowledge-graph baselines across ACC, F1, AUC, AUPR, and MCC.
AI.conclusion: The framework demonstrates robust multimodal integration for cold-start PPI prediction, effectively leveraging both sequence context and heterogeneous biomedical associations to improve performance across standard metrics.

title: Embodied.cpp: A Portable Inference Runtime of Embodied AI Models on Heterogeneous Robots
summary: Embodied AI models now span vision-language-action (VLA) models and world-action models (WAMs), but practical deployment remains fragmented across model-specific Python stacks, backend assumptions, and robot-side glue code, especially on heterogeneous edge devices. Existing inference runtimes are designed mainly for request-response serving and therefore do not satisfy the runtime contract of embodied deployment: multi-rate execution inside closed-loop control, latency-first batch-1 inference on heterogeneous hardware, and extensible embodied interfaces beyond fixed token I/O. We present Embodied.cpp, a portable C++ inference runtime for embodied models. Based on an architectural analysis of representative VLA models and WAMs, Embodied.cpp captures a shared execution path and organizes it into five layers: input adapters, sequence builders, backbone execution, head plugins, and deployment adapters. The runtime provides modular multi-rate execution, latency-first fused inference, and extensible operator and I/O support, enabling deployment across heterogeneous devices, robots, and simulators through one backend abstraction. We evaluate Embodied.cpp on two VLA models, HY-VLA and pi0.5, and on a preliminary WAM benchmark using a LingBot-VA Transformer block. The VLA deployments achieve successful closed-loop execution with 100.0% and 91.0% task success rates, respectively. The WAM benchmark reduces block memory from 312.2 MiB to 88.1 MiB. These results show that Embodied.cpp improves deployment efficiency while preserving high accuracy across diverse embodied model architectures.

AI.tldr: Embodied.cpp: a portable C++ runtime for embodied AI enabling multi-rate, latency-first execution across heterogeneous devices, tested on HY-VLA, pi0.5, and LingBot-VA Transformer block; shows high task success and substantial memory reduction, enabling unified deployment.
AI.motivation: Embodied AI deployments are fragmented across model stacks and backends; current runtimes optimized for request-response do not meet embodied deployment constraints (multi-rate control, latency-driven inference, heterogeneous hardware) and lack extensible I/O interfaces.
AI.method: Architectural design with five layers (input adapters, sequence builders, backbone execution, head plugins, deployment adapters); modular multi-rate execution, latency-first fused inference, extensible operators and I/O; provides one backend abstraction for diverse devices, robots, simulators.
AI.result: VLA: task success 100.0% and 91.0% for HY-VLA and pi0.5; WAM: block memory reduced from 312.2 MiB to 88.1 MiB; overall improved deployment efficiency without sacrificing accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Embodied.cpp offers a portable, efficient runtime enabling practical deployment of diverse embodied models across heterogeneous hardware and platforms.

title: Mastermind: Strategy-grounded Learning for Repository-Scale Vulnerability Reproduction
summary: Repository-level vulnerability reproduction is a demanding software engineering (SE) task: an agent must inspect a codebase, infer the input grammar that reaches a vulnerable path, construct a proof-of-conceptv(PoC), and verify that the crash disappears on the patched build. Recent LLM agents can often execute these steps when the approach is correct, yet they still fail by choosing the wrong strategy. This paper argues that strategy, rather than the full action trajectory, is the right learning unit for such SE agents: it is compact enough to optimize, concrete enough to guide execution, and stable enough to store and reuse across attempts. We present Mastermind, a dual-loop framework that separates transferable strategy learning from task-specific experience. A trainable planner learns reusable vulnerability-reproduction strategies through SFT and milestone-based GRPO, while an experience loop maintains task-local strategy records that guide subsequent attempts. The planner is trained independently of the executor, allowing strategy learning to improve multiple frozen executors without modifying their action-generation capability. We evaluate Mastermind on CyberGym using 260 training tasks and 200 held-out evaluation tasks. With GPT-5.5 as the frozen executor, Mastermind achieves an 84.5% pass rate, outperforming open-book PoC context (60.0%), Best-of-8 sampling (63.0%), and iterative improvement (77.0%). The same planner also improves GPT-5.4 mini and GLM~5.1 from 45.0% and 58.5% to 60.0% and 71.0%. These results demonstrate that learning high-level strategies is an effective and transferable mechanism for improving repository-scale SE agents.

AI.tldr: Mastermind introduces a dual-loop architecture that learns transferable vulnerability-reproduction strategies as a separate planning module, enabling improved repository-level SE agents; a trainable planner via SFT and milestone-based GRPO guides exploration, while an experience loop stores task-local strategy records; achieves strong cross-model gains on CyberGym.
AI.motivation: To address failures of LLM agents due to suboptimal strategy rather than the full action sequence; learning compact, reusable strategies should improve sample efficiency and transferability in repository-scale vulnerability reproduction tasks.
AI.method: A dual-loop framework: a trainable planner learns reusable vulnerability-reproduction strategies through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and milestone-based GRPO, while an experience loop maintains task-local strategy records to guide subsequent attempts. The planner is trained independently of the executor, allowing strategy learning to improve multiple frozen executors without modifying their action-generation capability.
AI.result: Evaluated on CyberGym with 260 training tasks and 200 held-out tasks. Using GPT-5.5 as the frozen executor, Mastermind achieves an 84.5% pass rate, outperforming open-book PoC context (60.0%), Best-of-8 sampling (63.0%), and iterative improvement (77.0%). The planner also improves GPT-5.4 mini and GLM-5.1 from 45.0% and 58.5% to 60.0% and 71.0%, respectively.
AI.conclusion: Learning high-level, reusable strategies is an effective and transferable mechanism for improving repository-scale software engineering agents; decoupling strategy learning from task-specific executors yields measurable cross-model gains.

title: LASER: A Corrective Lens for LVLMs via Visual Attention Preservation and Sink Suppression
comment: The 19th European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV 2026)
summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) exhibit strong reasoning ability but suffer from visual forgetting during long-horizon decoding, where attention progressively drifts away from visual evidence. Existing methods largely treat this issue as a late-stage attention decay problem or attempt to mitigate it through heuristic reminders or post-hoc attention lifting. Through systematic empirical analysis, we find that performance degradation under visual forgetting is largely driven by two overlooked factors: early-stage attention decay disrupts evidence acquisition, and attention concentration on a subset of task-irrelevant visual sink tokens. Motivated by these insights, we propose LASER, a post-training framework that regulates both the visual attention trajectory and intra-visual token attention distribution during reasoning. Technically, LASER introduces two complementary rewards: a Visual Grounding Reward, which encourages the model to maintain attention on semantically salient visual tokens throughout decoding, and a Sink Suppression Reward, which penalizes excessive attention concentration on visual sink tokens. Together, these rewards preserve early-stage grounding while preventing attention collapse onto uninformative regions. Extensive experiments on eight benchmark datasets demonstrate that LASER consistently outperforms strong baselines, validating attention-aware training as an effective remedy for visual forgetting.

AI.tldr: LASER: a post-training framework that mitigates visual forgetting in large vision-language models by regulating visual attention trajectory and intra-visual token attention, via two rewards—Visual Grounding Reward and Sink Suppression Reward—leading to improved grounding and reduced attention to uninformative tokens across eight datasets.
AI.motivation: To address visual forgetting during long-horizon decoding in LVLMs, caused by early-stage attention decay and over-attention to visual sink tokens, which disrupt evidence acquisition and degrade reasoning.
AI.method: LASER introduces two complementary rewards during post-training: (1) Visual Grounding Reward to maintain attention on semantically salient visual tokens throughout decoding, and (2) Sink Suppression Reward to penalize excessive attention on visual sink tokens. The framework regularizes the attention trajectory and intra-token attention distribution to preserve early-stage grounding and prevent attention collapse.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on eight benchmark datasets shows LASER consistently outperforms strong baselines, validating attention-aware training as an effective remedy for visual forgetting in LVLMs.
AI.conclusion: Attention-aware training via LASER effectively mitigates visual forgetting in LVLMs by stabilizing visual grounding during reasoning and avoiding attention collapse onto uninformative regions, with strong cross-dataset gains.

title: DeadPool: Resilient LLM Training with Hot-Swapping via Zero-Overhead Checkpoint
summary: State-of-the-art large language model (LLM) training takes tens of thousands of graphics processing units (GPUs) for months and encounters failures across the software and hardware stack. Existing fault-tolerance mechanisms either impose non-trivial overhead during failure-free execution or suffer from prolonged recovery latency, particularly under scenarios where a small subset of compute nodes experience permanent failures. %The tradeoff between failure-free overhead and recovery latency forms a space forms a Pareto frontier We present DeadPool to simultaneously address both optimization objectives. DeadPool incorporates a fault-tolerance mechanism that restores LLM training via hot-swapping, namely by replacing failed nodes with spare nodes without terminating the complete job. The hot-swapping of DeadPool is enabled by two ideas: First, it exploits an off-critical-path in-memory checkpointing mechanism for spatial redundancy. Second, it introduces a communicator reconstruction protocol that replaces failed nodes with spare nodes at runtime. DeadPool efficiently overlaps the in-memory checkpointing with computation, thus introducing zero overhead during error-free execution. Upon permanent node failures, DeadPool can rebuild memory states with minimal recomputation by leveraging in-memory checkpoints. We evaluate DeadPool across scales (up to 512 NVIDIA A100 GPUs) and LLMs (up to 65B parameters), and observe zero checkpoint overhead with hot-swapping recovery completing in under 40 seconds. These results show that DeadPool simultaneously achieves both zero-overhead error-free execution and extremely low recovery cost.

AI.tldr: DeadPool introduces zero-overhead fault tolerance for large-scale LLM training by hot-swapping failed nodes with spare nodes using in-memory checkpointing and runtime communicator reconstruction, achieving rapid recovery with minimal recomputation.
AI.motivation: Reduce failure-free overhead and recovery latency in distributed LLM training, especially when failures are permanent, by providing a fault-tolerance mechanism that does not penalize normal execution and can quickly rebuild state after node failures.
AI.method: 1) Off-critical-path in-memory checkpointing for spatial redundancy to enable hot-swapping without disrupting computation. 2) A runtime communicator reconstruction protocol to replace failed nodes with spare ones. 3) Overlaps checkpointing with computation to achieve near-zero overhead during failure-free execution. 4) Rebuilds memory state from in-memory checkpoints with minimal recomputation after permanent failures.
AI.result: Evaluations scale up to 512 NVIDIA A100 GPUs and LLMs up to 65B parameters, reporting zero overhead from checkpointing and hot-swapping recovery completed in under 40 seconds.
AI.conclusion: DeadPool can simultaneously provide zero-overhead error-free execution and rapid recovery for distributed LLM training, addressing both failure-free performance and fast fault recovery.

title: VT-WAM: Visual-Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Manipulation
summary: Contact-rich manipulation requires policies to react to local deformation, pressure, slip, and friction, yet these cues are temporally sparse and often invisible in visual observations. Existing visual-tactile policies usually feed tactile observations directly into action prediction, but rarely model tactile deformation dynamics during action generation. In this paper, we introduce VT-WAM, a Visual-Tactile World Action Model that jointly learns future visual prediction, tactile deformation prediction, and action prediction within a unified flow matching framework. In particular, VT-WAM introduces (1) Asymmetric Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) attention to bridge a first-frame visual anchor with temporal tactile dynamics, and (2) contact-gated Action-Visual-Tactile Attention Guidance (AVTAG) to encourage action queries to rely on tactile evidence during contact phases. Across six real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks, VT-WAM achieves a 71.67% average success rate, outperforming Fast-WAM by 26.67% and OmniVTLA by 35.84%. Ablations demonstrate that modeling tactile deformation dynamics and guiding contact-phase tactile attention are both important for contact-rich tasks. Project website: https://vt-wam.github.io/.

AI.tldr: VT-WAM jointly predicts future visuals, tactile deformation, and actions in a unified flow-matching framework; uses asymmetric Mixture-of-Transformers attention and contact-gated AVTAG; achieves 71.67% average success across six real-world tasks, outperforming baselines; ablations underscore the importance of tactile dynamics modeling and tactile-attention guidance.
AI.motivation: Visual-tactile policies for contact-rich manipulation often rely on instantaneous tactile cues, which are temporally sparse and hard to infer from vision alone. There is a need to explicitly model tactile deformation dynamics and integrate them into action generation to improve robustness during contact phases.
AI.method: VT-WAM introduces two key components within a unified flow-matching framework: (1) Asymmetric Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) attention that links a first-frame visual anchor to temporal tactile dynamics; (2) contact-gated Action-Visual-Tactile Attention Guidance (AVTAG) that steers action queries to leverage tactile evidence during contact phases. The model jointly predicts future visuals, tactile deformations, and actions.
AI.result: On six real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks, VT-WAM achieves a 71.67% average success rate, surpassing Fast-WAM by 26.67% and OmniVTLA by 35.84%. Ablation studies show both tactile deformation dynamics modeling and contact-phase tactile attention guidance are important for performance.
AI.conclusion: Modeling tactile deformation dynamics and guiding tactile attention during contact phases are beneficial for contact-rich manipulation, and the proposed MVIMA components (Asymmetric MoT and AVTAG) effectively fuse visual and tactile information within a flow-matching framework.

title: SimWorlds: A Multi-Agent System for Dynamic 3D Scene Creation
summary: LLM agents are increasingly used to translate natural language into 3D scenes in a procedural way, but existing systems focus on static output. Dynamic 4D scenes from text alone, in which liquids flow, particles emit, rigid bodies cascade, and articulated mechanisms move, remain largely unexplored despite their value as editable content and as physics-grounded training data for video generation and embodied AI. Two challenges set the dynamic case apart from static text-to-scene work: an agent must jointly coordinate spatial layout, multiple physics solvers, temporal sequencing, camera, and lighting in a single coherent scene, and verifying motion correctness from rendered video is fundamentally harder than judging a single image. We present SimWorlds: a multi-agent framework that produces dynamic, editable 4D scenes from text, with Blender-specific procedural knowledge, a planner-coder-reviewer workflow driving a fixed ordered sequence of construction stages, a layered scene protocol enforced by a deterministic verifier, and a runtime-state inspection tool suite that catches mechanism failures the rendered image cannot reveal. We also introduce 4DBuildBench, a benchmark for assessing both visual fidelity and physical consistency of the procedural dynamic 3D scenes generated from text prompts. Experiments show that SimWorlds outperforms prior dynamic Blender generation baselines.

AI.tldr: SimWorlds introduces a multi-agent framework to generate dynamic 4D scenes from text using Blender, featuring a planner-coder-reviewer workflow, a layered scene protocol with a deterministic verifier, and runtime tools, plus 4DBuildBench for visual fidelity and physical consistency. It reports improved performance over prior dynamic Blender baselines.
AI.motivation: Dynamic 4D scene synthesis from text is underexplored due to challenges in coordinating layout, multiple physics solvers, temporal sequencing, camera/light settings, and verifying motion from video rather than a single image. A robust, editable, physics-grounded pipeline is needed for training data and video generation.
AI.method: A multi-agent system with Blender-specific procedural knowledge, a fixed ordered construction sequence, planner-coder-reviewer workflow, layered scene protocol enforced by a deterministic verifier, and a runtime-state inspection tool suite to detect mechanism failures. Also introduces 4DBuildBench as a benchmark for visual fidelity and physical consistency of procedural dynamic 3D scenes generated from text prompts.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation shows SimWorlds outperforms prior dynamic Blender generation baselines.
AI.conclusion: SimWorlds provides a capable end-to-end pipeline to produce editable, physically consistent 4D scenes from natural language, along with a benchmark to assess fidelity and physical plausibility, advancing data creation and training for video generation and embodied AI.

title: Consistent Scene Understanding in 3D Gaussian Splatting via Multi-Cue Mask Refinement
summary: Reliable instance-level scene understanding is a fundamental prerequisite for object-level interactions and high-fidelity 3D representations. While current methods often leverage 2D foundation segmentation models to obtain these priors, their 2D-centric design typically yields fragmented masks and inconsistent predictions across different views. To address these issues, we propose a novel framework that produces consistent 2D instance masks to guide the optimization of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) feature fields. Our framework consists of three main stages. (1) Multi-Cue Extraction that generates synergistic semantic, geometric, and structural priors from input images. (2) Multi-Cue-Guided Mask Merging process that consolidates fragmented masks using a composite merge score derived from semantic, depth, and edge cues. (3) Cross-View Mask Matching that establishes globally consistent identity assignments across all viewpoints. By transforming viewpoint-specific segments into coherent 3D primitives, our approach enables stable 3D instance segmentation and effective downstream editing tasks. Experiments demonstrate that our method significantly improves cross-view consistency and segmentation stability over existing baselines while maintaining high-fidelity photometric reconstruction.

AI.tldr: A three-stage framework to produce consistent 2D instance masks that guide 3D Gaussian Splatting feature fields, improving cross-view consistency and 3D segmentation while preserving photometric fidelity.
AI.motivation: 2D foundation segmentation models yield fragmented masks and view-inconsistent predictions, hindering robust 3D understanding; robust 3D representations require globally consistent 2D priors and identity consistency across views.
AI.method: Stage 1: Multi-Cue Extraction of semantic, geometric, and structural priors from input images. Stage 2: Multi-Cue-Guided Mask Merging uses a composite score from semantic, depth, and edge cues to fuse fragmented masks. Stage 3: Cross-View Mask Matching establishes globally consistent identities across views and converts view-specific segments into 3D primitives to optimize 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) feature fields.
AI.result: Experiments show significant improvements in cross-view consistency and segmentation stability over baselines, while maintaining high-fidelity photometric reconstruction.
AI.conclusion: The framework yields stable 3D instance segmentation and enables effective downstream editing by leveraging coherent 2D priors to regularize and guide 3D representations.

title: CALM: Interpretable Cross-Modal Alignment for Biomarker Discovery from Unpaired Data
summary: The interaction between brain structure and genetic influences is key to understanding neuropsychiatric disorders. However, most large-scale datasets are unimodal, providing either neuroimaging or genetics data. We propose CALM, a framework that learns interpretable associations between brain ROIs and genetic pathways from completely disjoint populations. CALM aligns the two modalities in a shared latent space via linear projections that simultaneously match the class-conditional latent distributions and ensure group separability. These projections provide interpretable pathway--ROI associations. When trained on unimodal imaging and genetics datasets, CALM generalizes to an unseen paired dataset, outperforming several state-of-the-art methods and ablation baselines. We also demonstrate stability of the learned associations against a paired baseline. Our experiments on autism spectrum disorder reveal immune and metabolic pathways linked to specific cortical regions and are consistent with established literature. Thus, CALM opens the door to leveraging large unimodal repositories for studying cross-modal interactions in brain disorders across disparate datasets.

AI.tldr: CALM is a learning framework that discovers interpretable associations between brain ROIs and genetic pathways from disjoint unimodal datasets by learning a shared latent space; it generalizes to unseen paired data and yields biologically plausible pathway-ROI links in autism.
AI.motivation: To enable cross-modal brain–structure–genetics analysis when paired datasets are scarce, by leveraging large unimodal imaging and genetics cohorts while delivering interpretable cross-modal mappings.
AI.method: CALM uses linear projections to embed imaging ROIs and genetic pathways into a shared latent space, jointly aligning class-conditional latent distributions and enforcing group separability to produce interpretable ROI–pathway associations. It is trained on unimodal data and generalizes to unseen paired data; stability analyses compare against paired baselines.
AI.result: CALM outperforms state-of-the-art methods and ablations when trained on unimodal data and tested on unseen paired data. It demonstrates stable ROI–pathway associations; autism experiments reveal immune and metabolic pathways linked to specific cortical regions, consistent with existing literature.
AI.conclusion: CALM enables leveraging large unimodal repositories to study cross-modal brain–structure genetics interactions across heterogeneous datasets, unlocking cross-modal insights in neuropsychiatric disorders.

title: Repair the Amplifier, Not the Symptom: Stable World-Model Correction for Agent Rollouts
summary: As agent planning moves from short tool chains toward persistent workflows with thousands or tens of thousands of steps, failures will occur inside large planning graphs rather than in isolated predictions. Replanning the entire graph after every mistake is neither computationally realistic nor desirable: full-graph replay consumes large context budgets, exposes the LLM to many irrelevant symptoms, and can degrade long-context retrieval. This paper studies the missing component in such systems: a world-model corrector that repairs the failed planning graph in place. We compare two families of correctors. The first is the common engineering approach: scan nodes and edges, choose a suspicious local region, and ask an LLM to repair it. We implement strong engineering LLM correctors and find that they can help, especially when given very large contexts. The second family is our approach, WM-SAR (World-Model Subgraph Amplification Repair): instead of scanning for visible symptoms, it works backward from subgraph amplification, identifies the nodes and edges that keep re-amplifying error, and sends only that causal subgraph to the LLM. Across graph simulations and LLM repair experiments, WM-SAR substantially outperforms engineering correctors under realistic token budgets, achieves near-whole-graph stabilization with a compact region, and gives the LLM a cleaner repair target.

AI.tldr: WM-SAR identifies the causal subgraph that sustains errors in large planning graphs and feeds only that region to an LLM for repair, outperforming engineering local-correction baselines under realistic token budgets and achieving near-whole-graph stabilization with a compact region.
AI.motivation: As planning graphs scale to thousands of steps, failures occur inside the graph and full graph replay is computationally expensive and degrades long-context retrieval. A world-model corrector that repairs the graph in place could improve planning resilience with limited context.
AI.method: Compare two corrector families: (1) engineering correctors that scan a local region and request repairs from an LLM, and (2) WM-SAR (World-Model Subgraph Amplification Repair) that traces backward from subgraph amplification to identify the nodes/edges that perpetuate error and sends only that causal subgraph to the LLM for repair.
AI.result: WM-SAR substantially outperforms engineering correctors under realistic token budgets, achieving near-whole-graph stabilization with a compact repair region and providing a cleaner repair target for the LLM; results held across graph simulations and LLM repair experiments.
AI.conclusion: Targeted causal subgraph repair via WM-SAR is a more effective strategy than local engineering corrections for large planning graphs, enabling robust, scalable repairs with reduced context and improved repair quality.

title: Beyond Pixel Diffs: Benchmarking Image Change Captioning for Web UI Visual Regression Testing
summary: Visual regression testing (VRT) is a standard quality assurance step in modern software release pipelines. On every change, it re-renders user interface (UI) screenshots, compares each one against an approved baseline image, and routes any detected difference to a human reviewer who decides whether it is an intended update or an unintended regression. A widely used approach, especially in open-source and continuous-integration pipelines, is pixel-level comparison, which is semantically blind and treats rendering noise and genuine defects identically, producing large volumes of false positives that force developers and testers to spend substantial time and effort manually reviewing flagged differences at every release cycle. Industry tools apply machine learning to VRT, but lack public evaluation. More critically, no dataset or benchmark exists to support natural language descriptions of UI changes, a capability that tells testers what changed in words instead of leaving them to interpret a binary flag or a highlighted region. To address the gap, we propose a new task, Web UI Image Change Captioning (WUICC), which sits at the intersection of VRT and image difference captioning (IDC), and release WUICC-bench, its first dataset and benchmark for the task. We evaluate eleven representative IDC methods, together with two zero-shot general-purpose LLMs. We find that: (1) these methods tend to struggle in the Web UI domain due to its layout diversity, dense text, and fine-grained changes, and (2) yet the trained methods already suppress non-meaningful visual noise far more selectively than the pixel-level comparison VRT relies on, providing a solid foundation for future domain-specific research.

AI.tldr: Introduces Web UI Image Change Captioning (WUICC) and WUICC-bench, a dataset/benchmark to generate natural language captions of UI changes for visual regression testing; initial results show IDC methods and LLMs struggle in web UI but outperform pixel-diff at filtering noise.
AI.motivation: Pixel-level VRT is semantically blind and yields many false positives; there is no public dataset/benchmark for natural language UI change descriptions, hindering testers who benefit from verbal summaries.
AI.method: Define the WUICC task at the intersection of VRT and image difference captioning, release WUICC-bench, and benchmark 11 IDC methods plus two zero-shot general-purpose LLMs against it.
AI.result: IDC methods face challenges in the Web UI domain due to layout diversity, dense text, and fine-grained changes; however, trained methods already suppress non-meaningful visual noise more selectively than pixel-level VRT, indicating a solid foundation for domain-specific research.
AI.conclusion: WUICC provides a new benchmark and baseline for generating natural language UI change descriptions, enabling future domain-adapted improvements and better human-in-the-loop QA for UI changes.

title: Message Passing Based Two-Timescale Bayesian Learning for Joint Channel and Memory Hardware Impairments Tracking
summary: Hardware impairments in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) receivers introduce inter-symbol memory and inter-element coupling, severely degrading channel estimation. This paper employs a residual recurrent gated unit (RGRU) to model the intra-slot memory of the hardware impairments and proposes a message-passing-based two-timescale Bayesian deep learning (MP-TTBDL) framework for joint channel and impairment tracking. Owing to small-scale fading, the wireless channel varies rapidly across slots, whereas hardware impairments drift slowly due to hardware aging and environmental variations. To capture these distinct physical timescales, a fastvarying Markov prior and a slow-varying Gaussian Markov prior are assigned to the sparse channel and the network parameters, respectively. Based on a multi-slot factor graph formulation, a message-passing algorithm is developed. Specifically, the inter-slot messages admit closed-form updates, while the intra-slot factor graph, due to its complex recurrent structure, is partitioned into a channel tracking module and an impairments calibration module. The channel tracking module performs sparse channel estimation via turbo orthogonal approximate message passing (Turbo-OAMP), and the impairments calibration module updates the impairment parameters via a specially designed deep approximate message passing (DAMP) procedure, with the two modules iteratively exchanging extrinsic information through expectation propagation (EP) until convergence. Simulation results show that the proposed framework robustly achieves lower channel estimation error than conventional compensators followed by channel estimation across different online impairment scenarios and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions.

AI.tldr: Joint channel and impairment tracking in massive MIMO under hardware impairments using a two-timescale Bayesian deep learning framework (MP-TTBDL) with RGRU modeling intra-slot memory, Turbo-OAMP for channel, DAMP for impairment calibration, and EP exchange, achieving lower channel estimation error across varying impairment scenarios and SNR.
AI.motivation: Hardware impairments induce intra-slot memory and inter-element coupling that degrade channel estimation. A model that captures fast-varying channels and slow-varying impairment drift is needed for robust tracking.
AI.method: Use a residual recurrent gated unit (RGRU) to model intra-slot impairment memory. Propose MP-TTBDL: fast-varying Markov prior for the sparse channel and slow-varying Gaussian Markov prior for network parameters. Multi-slot factor graph with inter-slot messages in closed form; intra-slot graph split into a channel tracking module (Turbo-OAMP) and an impairments calibration module (DAMP). Expectation propagation (EP) iteratively exchanges extrinsic information between modules.
AI.result: Simulation results show the framework achieves lower channel estimation error than conventional compensators followed by channel estimation across different online impairment scenarios and SNR conditions.
AI.conclusion: The MP-TTBDL framework robustly improves channel estimation under hardware impairments by jointly tracking channels and impairments across multiple timescales with a modular message-passing design.

title: DL-VINS-Factory: A Modular Framework for Learned Visual Front-Ends in Visual-Inertial SLAM
summary: Deep-learning features excel in visual matching, yet their practical value in tightly coupled visual-inertial SLAM (VI-SLAM) remains insufficiently characterized. We present DL-VINS-Factory, a unified framework that integrates learned feature extractors (ALIKED, RaCo, SuperPoint, XFeat) with either Lucas--Kanade (LK) optical-flow tracking or LightGlue (LG) descriptor matching. All front-ends share a sliding-window Ceres back-end, with optional AnyLoc DINOv2-VLAD loop closure, and 4-DoF pose-graph optimization. We benchmark the system across the four datasets covering indoor, unstructured outdoor, aggressive-motion, and visually degraded conditions. Results show that learned front-ends are viable for real-time embedded VI-SLAM, but are not universally superior to classical tracking. Relative to the corresponding GFTT+LK baseline, ALIKED+LG reduces EuRoC ATE by $5\%$ in monocular odometry and by $7\%$ in stereo with loop-closure. On NTU-VIRAL, where aggressive aerial motion increases inter-frame viewpoint change, ALIKED+LG stereo reduces loop-closed ATE by $12\%$. In Botanic Garden dataset, optical-flow tracking remains preferable, but learned keypoints still improve over the baseline GFTT, in which SuperPoint+LK reduces grayscale camera ATE by $29\%$, while RaCo+LK reduces RGB camera ATE by $38\%$. On SubT-MRS, learned front-ends display varying degree of improvement based on individual cases. With TensorRT acceleration on a Jetson AGX Orin, all valid configurations run in real time between $29$--$47$ FPS in monocular mode and $18$--$33$ FPS in stereo mode for the EuRoC and NTU-VIRAL datasets. AnyLoc further confirms roughly $2$--$7\times$ more valid loops than BRIEF+DBoW2. The implementation is open-sourced at https://github.com/limshoonkit/DL-VINS-Factory-ROS2/.

AI.tldr: A unified DL-VINS-Factory framework benchmarks learned feature front-ends with LK or LightGlue in real-time VI-SLAM, showing dataset-dependent gains and robust loop-closure, released open-source.
AI.motivation: Characterize the practical value of deep-learning front-ends for tightly coupled VI-SLAM across diverse conditions and provide a reusable benchmark framework.
AI.method: Integrates learned feature extractors (ALIKED, RaCo, SuperPoint, XFeat) with either Lucas–Kanade (LK) optical-flow tracking or LightGlue (LG) descriptor matching, all front-ends sharing a sliding-window Ceres back-end with optional AnyLoc DINOv2-VLAD loop closure and 4-DoF pose-graph optimization; evaluated across four datasets (indoor, unstructured outdoor, aggressive motion, visually degraded); real-time with TensorRT on Jetson AGX Orin; open-source.
AI.result: Compared to GFTT+LK baseline: ALIKED+LG reduces monocular ATE by 5% and stereo ATE by 7% on EuRoC. On NTU-VIRAL, ALIKED+LG stereo reduces loop-closed ATE by 12%. In Botanic Garden, optical-flow tracking remains preferable, but learned keypoints still outperform GFTT; SuperPoint+LK cuts grayscale ATE by 29%, RaCo+LK cuts RGB ATE by 38%. On SubT-MRS, improvements vary by case. Real-time performance achieved: 29–47 FPS monocular, 18–33 FPS stereo (EuRoC, NTU-VIRAL) on Jetson AGX Orin with TensorRT. AnyLoc yields roughly 2–7x more valid loops than BRIEF+DBoW2. Open-source at the provided GitHub link.
AI.conclusion: Learned front-ends are viable for real-time embedded VI-SLAM but are not universally superior to classical tracking; the DL-VINS-Factory offers a flexible, quantitative benchmark and shows dataset-dependent benefits, with notable gains in loop closure and robustness on challenging sequences.

title: Verifiable Knowledge Expansion through Retrieval-Grounded Formal Concept Analysis
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, Accepted to the 8th epiDAMIK ACM SIGKDD International Workshop on Epidemiology meets Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery (epiDAMIK 2026)
summary: Ontology construction requires deciding which objects, attributes, and structural relations should be accepted as valid knowledge. Language models can propose such structures from text, but their outputs can still be unsupported or inconsistent. This paper proposes a retrieval-augmented small language model (SLM) framework that uses formal concept analysis (FCA) as a symbolic verification loop for knowledge expansion. Starting from seed attributes, FCA proposes implications over a growing formal context. A retrieval-grounded SLM oracle then validates each implication or returns a counterexample. The oracle also supports incidence judgments, consistency checks, and attribute proposals, making accepted implications, counterexamples, contradictions, and corrections inspectable. In a rare ataxia setting constructed from Orphadata resources, retrieval-grounded 10-seed runs obtain relation F1 of 0.29-0.52 and closure-based implication F1 of 0.22-0.30. Larger seed sets increase the number of evaluated implications and often improve implication F1. The lower implication scores reflect a stricter evaluation of derived implications, where one missed or extra relation can affect several implication judgments. Ablations show that incidence judgments in a fixed object-attribute setting can improve closure-based implication scores. However, identifying positive object-attribute pairs remains difficult even when the candidate objects and attributes are fixed.

AI.tldr: Retrieval-augmented small language model with FCA used as a symbolic verification loop to expand knowledge for ontology construction; empirical evaluation on a rare ataxia setting shows modest F1 scores and sensitivity to seed size; incidence judgments can help but positive object-attribute pairing remains hard.
AI.motivation: To mitigate inconsistencies and unsupported outputs of language models in ontology construction by introducing a symbolic verification loop (FCA) and a retrieval-grounded SLM to validate implications and provide inspectable evidence.
AI.method: Seed attributes feed a growing formal context; FCA proposes implications; a retrieval-grounded SLM oracle validates each implication or provides a counterexample; the oracle also performs incidence judgments, consistency checks, and attribute proposals; experiments in a rare ataxia setting (Orphadata) with 10-seed runs and larger seeds. Evaluation includes relation-level F1 and closure-based implication F1.
AI.result: Relation F1: 0.29–0.52; closure-based implication F1: 0.22–0.30; larger seed sets increase the number of evaluated implications and can improve implication F1; ablations show incidence judgments can improve closure-based scores; identifying positive object-attribute pairs remains difficult even with fixed candidates.
AI.conclusion: The framework yields inspectable, verification-supported ontology expansion, but face challenges in achieving high-precision implications due to strict evaluation and the difficulty of sourcing positive object-attribute pairs; more robust seed selection and evaluation strategies may be needed to improve performance.

title: ReQuest: Rethinking-based Question-Aware Frame Selection for Long-Form Video QA
summary: Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have substantially advanced video understanding, yet long-form video QA remains challenging under fixed input token budgets, where uniform sampling can be inefficient for evidence localization. We propose ReQuest , an uncertainty-driven, question-adaptive keyframe selection pipeline that aligns question intent with relevant video content through selective computation. ReQuest integrates (i) a lightweight question-aware selector distilled from MLLM-generated supervision, (ii) Re-thinking Routing that triggers additional inference only when the model is uncertain with a length-adaptive criterion, and (iii) uncertainty-guided adaptive non-maximum suppression that selects temporally diverse frames while adjusting spacing based on question difficulty. As a plug-andplay method, ReQuest improves long-video QA without modifying or fine-tuning the underlying MLLM. Experiments on Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench demonstrate consistent accuracy gains with competitive computational cost, with particularly strong improvements in medium and long video regimes.

AI.tldr: ReQuest is an uncertainty-driven, question-adaptive keyframe selection method for long-form video QA that reduces redundant processing by selecting relevant frames and delaying extra inference until uncertainty threshold is reached, without fine-tuning the base MLLM.
AI.motivation: Address fixed input token budgets and inefficiency of uniform sampling for evidence localization in long-form video QA by enabling selective computation driven by question intent.
AI.method: Three components: (i) a lightweight question-aware selector distilled from MLLM supervision; (ii) Re-thinking Routing that triggers additional inference only when the model is uncertain with a length-adaptive criterion; (iii) uncertainty-guided adaptive non-maximum suppression to select temporally diverse frames with spacing adjusted based on question difficulty. Plug-and-play, no fine-tuning of the underlying MLLM.
AI.result: Empirical gains on Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench with consistent accuracy improvements and competitive computational cost; particularly strong gains in medium- and long-video regimes.
AI.conclusion: ReQuest enables efficient, accurate long-video QA by aligning evidence selection with question intent and enabling adaptive computation without modifying the base MLLM.

title: Revisiting Decentralized Online Convex Optimization with Compressed Communication
summary: Decentralized online convex optimization (D-OCO) is a popular framework for distributed applications with streaming data. To tackle the communication bottleneck, previous studies have investigated D-OCO with compressed communication and proposed several algorithms that are variants of online gradient descent (OGD). However, for D-OCO with exact communication, the best existing algorithms are variants of follow-the-regularized-leader (FTRL). In this paper, for the first time, we propose two FTRL-type algorithms for D-OCO with compressed communication. Compared with OGD-type algorithms, our algorithms are more elegant in both algorithmic design and theoretical analysis. The key insight is that the dual update mechanism of FTRL allows us to make a simple application of the technique for average consensus with communication compression. More specifically, our first algorithm considers the full-information setting, and can match the existing regret bounds. Our second algorithm is designed for the bandit setting, and can significantly improve both the regret bounds and communication costs of existing algorithms.

AI.tldr: Two FTRL-type algorithms for decentralized online convex optimization with compressed communication: a full-information version achieving matching regret bounds and a bandit version with improved regret and reduced communication costs, enabled by a dual-update that facilitates average consensus under compression.
AI.motivation: Address the communication bottleneck in D-OCO by extending FTRL to compressed communication, providing a simpler, more elegant alternative to OGD-based methods and offering improvements in the bandit setting.
AI.method: Develop two FTRL-type algorithms for D-OCO with compressed communication. Leverage a dual update mechanism to implement average consensus under compression. First algorithm targets the full-information setting with regret matching existing bounds. Second algorithm addresses the bandit setting, using gradient estimators and showing improved regret bounds and reduced communication costs. Provide theoretical analysis and compare to OGD-type baselines.
AI.result: The full-information algorithm achieves regret bounds that match the best-known results for compressed D-OCO. The bandit algorithm yields significantly improved regret and lower communication costs compared with existing bandit-based D-OCO methods.
AI.conclusion: FTRL-based design offers a clean, elegant framework for compressed D-OCO. The dual-update A/C mechanism enables distributed average consensus under compression, and the bandit variant demonstrates practical gains in both regret and communication efficiency over prior approaches.

title: PixGS: Pixel-Space Diffusion for Direct 3D Gaussian Splat Generation
summary: Recent advances in 3D content generation from text or images have achieved impressive results, yet view inconsistency from 2D generators and the scarcity of high-quality 3D data remain significant bottlenecks. Existing solutions typically adapt large-scale pre-trained text-to-image latent diffusion models to generate 3D Gaussian Splats (3DGS). However, these approaches often rely on training complex cascade pipelines that are computationally expensive and scalability-limited. Most critically, the quality of generated 3D assets is inherently constrained by each component capacity and compressed latent space, leading to decoding artifacts and accumulated errors. To address these limitations, we propose PixGS, a single-stage pipeline for direct high-quality 3DGS generation, which leverages recent advances in pixel-space diffusion to bypass lossy latent compression while still benefiting from the vast 2D generative priors. By directly denoising 3D Gaussian attributes at each timestep, our method enables precise, splat-level regularization of both appearance and geometry. Furthermore, we introduce a comprehensive supervision strategy that incorporates surface normals, depth, and high-frequency structural information, which is often overlooked in prior works. Experiments demonstrate that PixGS outperforms current state-of-the-art methods while maintaining a fast inference speed (1s on a single A100 GPU), offering a robust and efficient alternative to multi-stage generation pipelines.

AI.tldr: Single-stage pixel-space diffusion for high-quality 3D Gaussian splats (3DGS) generation that bypasses latent compression and leverages 2D priors with splat-level supervision for fast, state-of-the-art results.
AI.motivation: Address view inconsistency and data scarcity in 3D content generation while avoiding multi-stage, computation-heavy pipelines and lossy latent representations that degrade 3D asset quality.
AI.method: Direct denoising of 3D Gaussian attributes in pixel space across diffusion timesteps, enabling precise appearance and geometry control at the splat level; employs a comprehensive supervision strategy including surface normals, depth, and high-frequency structural cues.
AI.result: Outperforms current state-of-the-art methods and maintains fast inference (~1 second) on a single A100 GPU, offering a streamlined alternative to cascaded generation pipelines.
AI.conclusion: PixGS provides an efficient, high-quality 3DGS generation framework that eliminates latent compression artifacts, delivers refined geometry and appearance, and leverages rich 2D priors for scalable single-stage synthesis.

title: Subliminal Clocks: Latent Time Modelling in Diffusion Language Models
comment: Equal contribution: Thomas Fontanari and Simone Petruzzi
summary: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) have recently emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive models. Unlike standard diffusion-based approaches, DLMs are not explicitly conditioned on a timestep, raising a natural question: do these models internally represent denoising progress, and how is such information used downstream? In this work, we show that DLMs do in fact encode a latent representation related to the diffusion timestep within their residual streams. We find that this signal can be reliably extracted using probes across layers, indicating that denoising progress is decodable from internal activations. We further demonstrate that steering the model along a low-dimensional subspace associated with the inferred timestep allows us to systematically modulate its notion of denoising progress, leading to predictable changes in model confidence and entropy. Finally, we analyse the geometry of the identified representation, showing that it exhibits structured and interpretable properties in activation space, and shedding light on how such a signal is processed by these models.

AI.tldr: DLMs internally encode a decodable latent diffusion-timestep signal in their residual streams, which can be steered in a low-dimensional subspace to modulate denoising progress, affecting model confidence and entropy; the activation geometry is structured and interpretable.
AI.motivation: Understand how diffusion-language models (which do not condition on a timestep) internally represent denoising progress and how such representations influence downstream behavior and controllability.
AI.method: Probe internal activations across layers to extract a latent timestep signal; train probes to decode the diffusion-timestep from residual streams; identify a low-dimensional subspace aligned with the inferred timestep; manipulate activations along this subspace; evaluate effects on confidence/entropy; analyze the geometry of the representation in activation space.
AI.result: A decodable latent timestep signal exists in residual streams of DLMs. Steering the model along the inferred-timestep subspace produces predictable changes in denoising progress, confidence, and entropy. The representation exhibits structured and interpretable geometry in activation space.
AI.conclusion: DLMs maintain and utilize an internal notion of denoising progress despite lacking explicit timestep conditioning, enabling interpretability and controllability of denoising dynamics through a learned latent representation.

title: InterCMDM: Block-Causal Diffusion for Autoregressive Human Interaction Generation
comment: Accepted to ECCV 2026, Project website: https://yu1ut.com/InterCMDM-HP/
summary: Text-conditioned human interaction generation must capture both long-range temporal causality within each individual and tightly coupled coordination between partners. Existing interaction diffusion models typically denoise full sequences using bidirectional attention, which obscures causality and hinders streaming and long-horizon generation. Autoregressive alternatives enforce causality but often suffer from temporal drift, leading to coordination degradation and unstable interaction dynamics over time. We propose InterCMDM, a block-causal latent diffusion framework for autoregressive two-person interaction generation. InterCMDM introduces a Dual-Stream Causal Diffusion Transformer that maintains separate causal streams for each person while modeling inter-person dependencies via unified dual-stream attention with multi-task attention masks. These masks unify interaction modeling within a single attention mechanism and support diverse coordination behaviors, including simultaneous actions, reactive responses, leader-follower dynamics, and independent motion. By training a single model across these mask configurations as a form of data augmentation, InterCMDM enables controllable interaction generation by simply selecting the desired attention mask at inference time. Finally, a block-wise diffusion objective enables stable latent rollout over long sequences without repeated decode-encode cycles. InterCMDM achieves state-of-the-art performance on InterHuman and Inter-X, improving text-motion alignment, realism, and long-horizon continuity.

AI.tldr: Introduces InterCMDM: a block-causal latent diffusion framework for autoregressive two-person interaction generation using a dual-stream causal diffusion transformer with configurable attention masks to enable controllable, long-horizon coordination.
AI.motivation: Preserve causality and stable long-horizon coordination in text-conditioned two-person interaction generation; full-sequence denoising in diffusion models obscures causality and autoregressive models suffer temporal drift, harming coordination.
AI.method: Dual-Stream Causal Diffusion Transformer maintaining separate causal streams per participant, unified dual-stream attention with multi-task masks; training across multiple mask configurations as data augmentation; block-wise diffusion objective for stable, long-horizon latent rollout.
AI.result: State-of-the-art on InterHuman and Inter-X datasets; improvements in text-motion alignment, realism, and long-horizon continuity.
AI.conclusion: Enables controllable interaction generation by selecting the attention mask at inference; supports diverse coordination behaviors (simultaneous actions, reactive responses, leader-follower dynamics, independent motion) and stable latent rollout without repeated decode-encode cycles.

title: UniWind: Toward Unified Day-Ahead Wind Power Forecasting via Physics-Informed State Routing
summary: Day-ahead wind power forecasting is essential for cost-effective power-system operation. It is primarily driven by future meteorological conditions while retaining temporal dependencies in power generation. In practice, observed wind-farm power often entangles physically available power with local environmental effects and latent operational states, such as shutdowns and curtailment. Existing physical models provide useful constraints but adapt poorly across wind farms, whereas data-driven models can capture rich correlations but often conflate meteorological effects with state-induced deviations. In this study, we propose UniWind, a wind power forecasting model based on physics-informed state routing. UniWind first employs a Physical Prior Estimator to construct a site-calibrated physical prior by combining site-conditioned monotonic warping with a shared physical power curve. It further applies a physical upper-bound constraint to shape this prior as a soft envelope of available wind power generation. UniWind then proposes a Latent State Encoder to model operating-state embeddings and transforms the physical prior into final power forecasts through a State-aware Power Corrector, which uses knowledge-guided supervised state routing and bounded, state-specific expert correction. Full-shot and cross-farm zero-shot experiments on more than 20 real-world datasets demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of UniWind.

AI.tldr: UniWind offers a physics-informed forecasting framework that couples a site-calibrated physical prior with latent state routing to produce accurate, robust wind power forecasts across farms, including zero-shot cross-farm generalization.
AI.motivation: Forecasting wind power is confounded by the overlap of meteorological effects with local operational states (e.g., shutdowns, curtailment). Pure physical models struggle to generalize across wind farms, while data-driven models can conflate weather with state-induced deviations. A method that integrates physics with state information is needed to improve accuracy and transferability.
AI.method: Physical Prior Estimator: constructs a site-calibrated prior via site-conditioned monotonic warping and a shared physical power curve, plus a physical upper-bound constraint to form a soft envelope of feasible power. Latent State Encoder: learns embeddings representing operating states. State-aware Power Corrector: performs knowledge-guided supervised state routing and applies bounded, state-specific expert corrections to transform the prior into final forecasts. Training/evaluation: full-shot and cross-farm zero-shot experiments on more than 20 real-world datasets to assess accuracy and robustness.
AI.result: Empirically, UniWind achieves accurate and robust forecasts, with demonstrated cross-farm zero-shot generalization across a large number of real datasets, indicating strong transferability and resilience to state-induced deviations.
AI.conclusion: Integrating a physics-based prior with latent state routing yields an effective, site-calibrated wind power forecasting framework that generalizes well across farms and operational states, outperforming approaches that rely solely on physical models or purely data-driven methods.

title: Robust Image Processing Techniques for Construction Environment Monitoring Using Underwater Robots
summary: This paper proposes a robust image processing framework for underwater robot-based construction environment monitoring, targeting complex degradations observed in real marine environments. Unlike conventional approaches that mainly consider absorption and backscattering, real underwater imagery is strongly affected by depth-dependent forward scattering blur and particle-induced degradations such as marine snow. To address this, we introduce a staged processing pipeline that sequentially models background degradation via depth-aware forward scattering and foreground degradation using realistic marine snow patterns extracted from real images. The resulting synthetic data are used to retrain an existing Joint-ID network without modifying its architecture, enabling an isolated evaluation of dataset realism. In addition, a lightweight post-processing scheme is applied to enhance contrast and structural clarity. Experiments on real underwater datasets collected in Korean coastal environments demonstrate consistent improvements in visual quality and UIQM scores. The results indicate that explicitly modeling forward scattering and realistic particle effects effectively reduces the synthetic-to-real gap and improves practical applicability in real-world underwater robotic operations.

AI.tldr: A staged degradation modeling and synthetic-data augmentation framework improves underwater image quality for robot-based monitoring by explicitly modeling depth-dependent forward scattering and marine-snow-like degradations, retraining a Joint-ID network without architecture changes, and applying a lightweight post-processing step to enhance UIQM.
AI.motivation: Underwater imagery suffers from more than absorption and backscattering. Depth-dependent forward scattering and particle effects (e.g., marine snow) degrade both background and foreground visual quality, hindering perception tasks in underwater robotics.
AI.method: 1) Stage background degradation via depth-aware forward scattering. 2) Stage foreground degradation using realistic marine-snow patterns extracted from real images. 3) Generate synthetic data and retrain an existing Joint-ID network without modifying its architecture to assess dataset realism. 4) Apply a lightweight post-processing step to boost contrast and structure.
AI.result: Synthetic data improves visual quality and UIQM scores in experiments on real Korean coastal underwater datasets; explicit modeling of forward scattering and particle effects reduces the synthetic-to-real gap and improves applicability in real-world operations.
AI.conclusion: Modeling depth-dependent forward scattering and realistic particle degradations, along with synthetic data augmentation and post-processing, yields more realistic underwater images and better practical performance for robot-assisted monitoring.

title: Safety Testing LLM Agents at Scale: From Risk Discovery to Evidence-Grounded Verification
summary: LLM agents increasingly perform autonomous actions through external tools, leading to complex and evolving safety risks. However, existing safety testing targets expert-designed safety violations, and the corresponding outcomes are evaluated by hard-coded rules, making them costly to extend as agents evolve. To this end, we present Vera, an end-to-end automated safety testing framework that instantiates software engineering testing principles for non-deterministic agents through a three-stage, self-reinforcing pipeline. First, a literature-driven exploration continuously discovers and structures emerging risks into taxonomies of safety risks, attack methods, and tool execution environments. Second, combinatorial composition across taxonomy dimensions produces executable safety cases, each specifying a concrete safety goal, a programmatically constructed initial state, and a deterministic verification predicate grounded in observable artifacts. Third, adaptive execution runs heterogeneous agents in isolated sandboxes where a control agent steers multi-turn interaction based on runtime observations, while evidence-grounded verifiers judge outcomes from environment state and tool-call evidence rather than model self-report. We evaluate Vera on four production agent frameworks (OpenClaw, Hermes, Codex, Claude Code), revealing substantial safety weaknesses, with average attack success rates reaching 93.9\% under multi-channel attacks; we also release Vera-Bench, comprising 1600 executable safety cases spanning 124 risk categories across three execution settings. These results indicate that modular, executable testing infrastructure is essential for rigorous and maintainable safety evaluation of rapidly evolving agentic systems at scale. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/Yunhao-Feng/Vera.

AI.tldr: Vera is an end-to-end automated safety-testing framework for non-deterministic LLM-enabled agents, using a three-stage pipeline to discover and structure safety risks, generate executable safety cases, and verify outcomes in sandboxed execution with evidence-based checks; it reveals substantial safety weaknesses and releases Vera-Bench with 1600 executable cases.
AI.motivation: To address the mismatch between safety testing targets (expert-designed violations and hard-coded rules) and rapidly evolving agentic systems, requiring scalable, modular testing.
AI.method: A three-stage pipeline: (1) literature-driven taxonomy construction of safety risks, attack methods, and tool environments; (2) combinatorial generation of executable safety cases across taxonomy dimensions with concrete goals, initial states, and deterministic predicates; (3) adaptive sandboxed execution with a control agent and evidence-grounded verifiers that judge outcomes from environment/tool evidence rather than self-report.
AI.result: Evaluation on four production frameworks (OpenClaw, Hermes, Codex, Claude Code) shows average attack success rates of 93.9% under multi-channel attacks; release of Vera-Bench with 1600 executable safety cases across 124 risk categories and three execution settings; code availability at GitHub.
AI.conclusion: Modular, executable testing infrastructure is essential for rigorous, maintainable safety evaluation of rapidly evolving agentic systems at scale.

title: RTE-FM-Dehazer: Radiative Transfer Equation Inspired Flow Matching for Real-World Image Dehazing
summary: Single-image dehazing aims to recover a clear scene from a hazy image and is generally formulated as an image-to-image translation task; however, it faces two limitations. Its performance depends heavily on the haze-formation priors embedded in the model. Prevailing methods adopt the Atmospheric Scattering Model (ASM), whose assumptions of single scattering and homogeneous media are often violated, leading to residual haze and color drift. Moreover, large-scale real hazy/clear pairs are impractical to collect, and existing synthesis approaches fail to reproduce the full complexity of natural haze. To address these issues, we present RTE-FM-Dehazer, a novel dehazing approach, together with a scalable data pipeline. Unlike the ASM, the Radiative Transfer Equation (RTE) jointly accounts for both scattering and absorption, naturally accommodating the non-homogeneous, multiple-scattering media that characterize real hazy scenes. Motivated by the structural similarity between the RTE diffusion-absorption term and the ODE in flow matching, we introduce a diffusion-absorption regularizer derived from a reduced RTE, to steer the flow matching trajectory at each step. Next, leveraging modern vision-language models, we build an automated pipeline and release P-HAZE, a dataset of 50000 realistic hazy/clear pairs. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that RTE-FM-Dehazer, trained solely on P-HAZE, effectively eliminates artifacts like residual haze and color drift, exhibits strong cross-domain generalization, and achieves leading results on five real-world dehazing benchmarks.

AI.tldr: A physics-informed dehazing method replacing the Atmospheric Scattering Model with the Radiative Transfer Equation, introducing a diffusion-absorption regularizer within a flow-matching framework, plus a large-scale vision-language–driven dataset P-HAZE (50k hazy/clear pairs); achieves strong cross-domain generalization and leading results on real hazy benchmarks.
AI.motivation: ASM-based dehazing struggles with non-homogeneous, multi-scattering media and color drift; collecting real hazy/clear data is impractical and synthetic haze fails to capture real-world complexity; a physically grounded model plus scalable data could improve generalization.
AI.method: Use the Radiative Transfer Equation to model scattering and absorption, addressing non-homogeneous, multiple scattering; introduce a diffusion-absorption regularizer derived from a reduced RTE to steer the flow-matching trajectory. Build an automated pipeline with vision-language models to generate P-HAZE (50k hazy/clear pairs). Train solely on P-HAZE and evaluate on five real-world dehazing benchmarks.
AI.result: RTE-FM-Dehazer effectively eliminates artifacts such as residual haze and color drift, demonstrates strong cross-domain generalization, and achieves leading performance on five real-world dehazing benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Integrating RTE-based physics with a diffusion-absorption regularizer and scalable vision-language–driven data generation yields robust dehazing with improved physical fidelity and generalization, as demonstrated by P-HAZE training and strong real-data evaluation.

title: SCAPE: Accurate and Efficient LLM Training with Extreme Sparse Communication
summary: Communication increasingly dominates the cost of Large Language Model (LLM) pre-training, especially under data-parallel and sharded training schemes, where gradient synchronization and parameter reconstruction overhead increase with model size and system scale. Existing communication-reduction methods either sparsify raw gradients, which can be unstable for modern Adam-style optimizers at high sparsity, or quantize communication, whose savings are fundamentally bounded by bit width and often incur additional runtime overhead. We present SCAPE, a communication-efficient distributed optimizer for LLM training that exploits the stability of AdamS's first-moment to enable aggressive sparsification without loss of LLM quality. Instead of constructing masks from raw gradients, SCAPE derives them from first-moment-based statistics, partitions mask generation across workers to align with optimizer sharding, and delays mask usage by one step so that mask synchronization can overlap with computation. SCAPE also reconstructs the quantities required for second-moment updates from a single synchronized sparse buffer, avoiding an additional collective. We implement SCAPE in Megatron-LM and evaluate its convergence by pre-training GPT-345M on OpenWebText and Llama-500M on SlimPajama-6B using 32 NVIDIA GH200 GPUs on TACC Vista. In both models, SCAPE preserves training stability, validation loss, and downstream task accuracy under 90\% and 99\% sparsity. For Llama-500M, SCAPE reduces end-to-end pre-training wall-clock time by up to 43.3\% while maintaining model quality comparable to dense AdamW and AdamS. For Llama-1.8B, SCAPE achieves up to 3.26$\times$ speedup per step compared to dense AdamS.

AI.tldr: SCAPE is a sparsified, AdamS-based distributed optimizer for LLM pretraining that uses first-moment statistics to derive masks, overlaps mask synchronization with computation, and reconstructs second-moment updates from sparse buffers, achieving up to 3.26x speedups and maintaining quality at 90–99% sparsity on GPT-345M and Llama-500M/1.8B.
AI.motivation: Communication costs dominate LLM pretraining, and existing sparsification or quantization approaches either destabilize Adam-style optimizers at high sparsity or have bounded savings; a stable, high-sparsity method is needed.
AI.method: Derive sparsity masks from first-moment statistics; distribute mask generation across workers to align with optimizer sharding; delay mask usage by one step to enable overlap; reconstruct second-moment quantities from a single synchronized sparse buffer to avoid extra collectives; implement in Megatron-LM and evaluate on GPT-345M OpenWebText and Llama-500M SlimPajama-6B with 32 NVIDIA GH200 GPUs.
AI.result: SCAPE preserves training stability, validation loss, and downstream accuracy at 90% and 99% sparsity; reduces end-to-end pretraining time by up to 43.3% for Llama-500M; up to 3.26x speedup per step for Llama-1.8B, compared to dense AdamS.
AI.conclusion: First-moment-based sparse masking enables aggressive, stable communication reduction in large-scale training; SCAPE is effective in practice within Megatron-LM and can significantly cut training time while preserving model quality; potential for broader application with proper masking strategies.

title: NeoMap: Training-free Novel-View Synthesis from Single Images and Videos
comment: ECCV 2026. Jinxi and Tianyi are co-first authors. Code and data are available at: https://github.com/vLAR-group/NeoMap
summary: We study the challenging problem of novel view video synthesis from single images or monocular videos. Existing methods, which operate under the assumption that pre-trained video models lack native novel view synthesis capability and enforce view alignment via camera conditioning, task-specific fine-tuning, or stepwise hard denoising guidance, often suffer from artifacts and compromised global scene consistency. In this paper, we introduce NeoMap, a novel training-free framework designed to locate high-fidelity, view-consistent novel view solutions from general pre-trained video models. The key to our approach is the core insight that promising novel view solutions are inherently encoded within the natural video data manifold learned by pre-trained models, and the core challenge is simply to locate this optimal solution. We solve this via our core mechanism: convergent manifold alternating projection iterations that optimize the initial noise. Extensive experiments demonstrate that NeoMap significantly outperforms all existing methods across 3 standard novel view synthesis benchmarks, including the challenging Tanks-and-Temples, LLFF and DAVIS datasets, achieving state-of-the-art generation fidelity and top-tier view consistency.

AI.tldr: NeoMap proposes a training-free framework that locates high-fidelity, view-consistent novel-view solutions within pre-trained video models by performing convergent manifold alternating projection iterations on initial noise.
AI.motivation: Address artifacts and inconsistent global scene geometry in existing view synthesis methods that rely on fine-tuning or restricted conditioning of pre-trained video models; leverage the inherent information embedded in the data manifold of video priors without additional training.
AI.method: Use pre-trained video models as priors and apply convergent manifold alternating projection (CMAP) iterations to optimize the initial noise, effectively searching the data manifold for optimal novel-view solutions without task-specific training or camera conditioning.
AI.result: NeoMap reportedly achieves state-of-the-art generation fidelity and top-tier view consistency across three benchmarks (Tanks-and-Temples, LLFF, DAVIS), outperforming existing methods.
AI.conclusion: Promising novel-view solutions are encoded in the natural video data manifold learned by pre-trained models; the main challenge is locating this optimal solution, which can be solved by training-free CMAP iterations that refine the initial noise.

title: MMIR-TCM: Memory-Integrated Multimodal Inference and Retrieval for TCM Clinical Decision Support
summary: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) diagnosis, particularly through tongue inspection, faces persistent challenges in subjectivity and reproducibility. The application of multimodal artificial intelligence to TCM clinical tasks, such as syndrome differentiation and prescription generation, is significantly hampered by the semantic gap between visual tongue features and textual reasoning, as well as the lack of large-scale, standardized datasets. To address these challenges, we introduce MMIR-TCM, a novel framework that emulates the diagnostic process of TCM experts by integrating multimodal large language model(MLLM) with memory-augmented segmentation and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Employing a three-stage architecture, MMIR-TCM integrates a training-free Memory-SAM module for robust tongue extraction, a fine-tuned Qwen3-VL model for structured tongue diagnosis generation, and a Qwen3-based RAG component for evidence-grounded clinical decision support generation. The framework was developed and validated using MedTCM, a new large-scale multimodal dataset that we introduce specifically for advanced TCM research. To properly evaluate our framework's clinical accuracy, which existing metrics fail to capture, we also developed TDEU, a domain-specific evaluation metric incorporating semantic understanding and diagnostic importance. Our comprehensive experiments demonstrate that MMIR-TCM significantly outperforms leading models, including GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Flash.

AI.tldr: Introduces MMIR-TCM, a three-stage multimodal framework for tongue-diagnosis in Traditional Chinese Medicine, using memory-augmented segmentation, a fine-tuned Qwen3-VL for structured diagnosis, and a Qwen3-based RAG for evidence-grounded decision support on the new MedTCM dataset, with a domain-specific TDEU evaluation metric; reports superiority over GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Flash.
AI.motivation: Address subjectivity and reproducibility in TCM tongue diagnosis, bridging the gap between visual tongue features and textual reasoning, and mitigating lack of large-scale standardized datasets.
AI.method: Three-stage architecture: (1) Memory-SAM for training-free robust tongue extraction; (2) fine-tuned Qwen3-VL for structured tongue-diagnosis generation; (3) Qwen3-based RAG for evidence-grounded clinical decision support. Introduces MedTCM, a large-scale multimodal dataset, and TDEU, a domain-specific evaluation metric.
