Extensive experiments on the SRDD benchmark demonstrate that UA-ChatDev consistently outperforms existing single-agent and multi-agent software development frameworks across completeness, executability, consistency, and overall quality metrics. Further ablation studies and communication analyses verify that uncertainty-aware interactions enhance code execution reliability.

AI.tldr: Uncertainty-aware multi-agent software development with phase-aware verification to reduce hallucination propagation.
AI.motivation: Mitigate error propagation caused by unreliable intermediate agent outputs in autonomous multi-agent software development, improving final software quality.
AI.method: Token-level log-probability based uncertainty estimation; phase-aware threshold calibration; retrieval-based verification triggered when uncertainty exceeds a threshold; lightweight integration with existing agent interactions.
AI.result: UA-ChatDev consistently outperforms single-agent and existing multi-agent frameworks on completeness, executability, consistency, and overall software quality across SRDD benchmark; ablation and communication analyses support the benefit of uncertainty-aware interactions for reliable code execution.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating uncertainty quantification into multi-agent software development effectively reduces hallucination propagation and enhances reliability and overall software quality.

title: Open-Weather Robust 3D Detection via Dual-Critic Diffusion Alignment
summary: Robust 3D object detection under adverse weather remains a critical hurdle for autonomous driving. Despite progress with LiDAR-4D radar fusion, most methods are constrained by a closed-world assumption, implicitly requiring training and test weather to align in both type and severity. This premise fails in practice: the open-ended nature of weather, and even variations within a single type like rain, cause dramatically different LiDAR degradation patterns, leading to significant performance drops in unseen conditions. To address this, we present Dual-Critic Guided Diffusion Alignment (DCDA), a weather-agnostic framework that learns to recover degraded LiDAR features toward a clean manifold. Rather than modeling specific weather types, DCDA employs a 4D radar-conditioned diffusion process to progressively refine features, guided by two complementary critics. (i) A detection-guided critic, anchored by a pre-trained clean-weather model, ensures that the refined features retain object-level discriminability and localization accuracy. (ii) A weather adversarial critic enforces holistic distributional consistency with clean-weather representations. By aligning features through semantic and distributional constraints rather than explicit weather modeling, DCDA generalizes effectively to unseen weather types and severities without requiring paired data or weather labels. We further introduce a structured open-weather benchmark with held-out type-severity combinations and extensive experiments verify DCDA's advantages.

AI.tldr: A weather-agnostic 4D radar-conditioned diffusion framework (DCDA) improves LiDAR feature restoration under unseen adverse weather, using dual critics (detection-guided and weather adversarial) to align to a clean-weather manifold without weather labels or paired data.
AI.motivation: Open-world weather conditions violate closed-world training assumptions; unseen rain/degradation patterns cause large performance drops. A model that generalizes across weather types/severities without annotated weather data is highly desirable.
AI.method: DCDA uses a 4D radar-conditioned diffusion process to progressively refine degraded LiDAR features toward a clean manifold. It employs two critics: (1) a detection-guided critic anchored to a pre-trained clean-weather model to preserve object-level discriminability and localization; (2) a weather adversarial critic to enforce distributional consistency with clean-weather representations. The approach emphasizes semantic and distributional alignment rather than explicit weather modeling and does not require paired data or weather labels. It introduces a structured open-weather benchmark with held-out type-severity combinations.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show DCDA improves robustness to unseen weather conditions, outperforming baselines that rely on closed-world assumptions or explicit weather modeling; the dual-critic diffusion alignment yields better object detection under diverse weather degradations.
AI.conclusion: Feature-level diffusion refinement guided by dual critics enables weather-agnostic generalization for LiDAR/radar fusion in autonomous driving, supporting robust performance in open-world weather scenarios without weather-label supervision or paired data.

title: Probabilistic Low-Voltage Peak Load Forecasting with Time Series Foundation Models Evaluated on Application-Oriented Metrics
comment: A poster abstract of this publication will be available at the 15th DACH+ Conference on Energy Informatics (2026 in Linz, Austria)
summary: Low-voltage load forecasting is an important component in current and future energy systems with a high degree of electrification and decentralized generation. However, current forecasting methods require significant manual effort, often lack uncertainty estimation and proper peak prediction, and they are often not adequately evaluated in terms of grid requirements. In the present study, we provide an extensive evaluation of short-term net load forecasts of 200 real-world low-voltage feeders with a focus on the rapidly evolving time series foundation models. Our study compares Chronos-Bolt, Chronos-2 and TabPFN-TS to six baseline models and demonstrates superior performance, in particular for Chronos-2. An ablation study, in which weather covariates are omitted, shows that time series foundation models adapt to increased uncertainty, despite the importance of weather information. A novel application-oriented metric links the model's forecasting capabilities in peak prediction to the trade-off in grid asset planning and operation between cost reduction and minimizing the risk of failure.

AI.tldr: Comprehensive evaluation of short-term LV net-load forecasts with time-series foundation models (Chronos-Bolt, Chronos-2, TabPFN-TS) across 200 feeders; Chronos-2 shows strongest performance; ablation shows weather covariates aid uncertainty handling; introduces an application-oriented metric linking forecast quality to grid planning decisions.
AI.motivation: Address the lack of uncertainty-aware, peak-focused, grid-relevant short-term forecasts at low-voltage feeders, suitable for high electrification and decentralized generation, with minimal manual intervention.
AI.method: Empirical evaluation of Chronos-Bolt, Chronos-2, and TabPFN-TS against six baselines on 200 real-world LV feeders; ablation study omitting weather covariates; introduction of a novel metric connecting forecast accuracy to grid asset planning trade-offs.
AI.result: Chronos-2 provides superior forecast performance; weather covariates improve uncertainty handling though models adapt without them; the new metric reveals a trade-off between cost reduction and risk of grid failure in planning.
AI.conclusion: Time-series foundation models are effective for short-term LV net-load forecasting and can inform peak-aware grid planning; Chronos-2 is particularly strong; weather information enhances robustness but models exhibit adaptability without it.

title: Criticality-Based Guard Rail Validation for AI Agent Decisions in Autonomous Telecom Networks
summary: The evolution toward fully autonomous telecommunications networks (Autonomous Network Levels 4-5) requires AI/ML agents to make real-time network decisions without human intervention. However, no standardized runtime mechanism exists to intercept and validate individual inference outputs before they trigger live network state changes, creating risks of erroneous autonomous decisions. This paper proposes the Guard Rail Validation (GRV) framework, a standardizable runtime architecture for intercepting and validating AI-driven decisions before execution. The framework evaluates decisions across multiple weighted dimensions -- including action scope, action type, service criticality, agent autonomy level, reversibility, and temporal behavioural patterns -- to determine a criticality level. Based on this level, graduated validation mechanisms are applied: execute-with-logging, bounds checking, independent agent validation, or multi-agent consensus. The framework additionally provides cross-agent conflict detection with criticality-weighted priority resolution and runtime conformance logging for regulatory compliance (e.g., EU AI Act Article 14). We present the architecture, algorithmic procedures, O-RAN deployment model, and evaluate threat coverage against known AI/ML attacks in telecommunications.

AI.tldr: GRV provides a standardizable runtime framework for intercepting and validating AI-driven decisions in autonomous telecom networks, using multi-dimensional criticality to apply graduated validation (logging, bounds, independent validation, or multi-agent consensus), plus cross-agent conflict resolution and runtime conformance logging for regulatory compliance, with architecture, procedures, O-RAN deployment, and threat coverage evaluation.
AI.motivation: As autonomous networks scale, there is no standardized runtime mechanism to intercept/validate AI inferences before they alter live network state, creating risks of erroneous decisions and regulatory gaps.
AI.method: Define weighted, multi-dimensional criticality (action scope/type, service criticality, agent autonomy, reversibility, temporal patterns); compute a criticality level; apply graduated validation (execute-with-logging, bounds checking, independent validation, multi-agent consensus); implement cross-agent conflict detection with priority resolution; runtime conformance logging; describe architecture, algorithms, and O-RAN deployment; evaluate threat coverage against known AI/ML attacks in telecoms.
AI.result: Proposed architecture and algorithmic procedures; O-RAN deployment model; evaluation of threat coverage against known AI/ML attacks in telecommunications.
AI.conclusion: GRV offers a standardizable runtime mechanism to intercept and validate AI-driven decisions, enabling safer autonomous networks, regulatory conformance, and a foundation for deployment and further research.

title: Understanding Geometric Representations in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers via Subspace Intervention
summary: We introduce a controlled subspace intervention framework to investigate how self-supervised Vision Transformers (ViTs) encode dense geometric information. While linear probing is widely used to assess geometric representations, it treats features as a black box, failing to disentangle the underlying topology. To address this issue, we decompose the weights of converged linear probes to isolate the low-rank subspaces containing explicit geometric signals using Singular Value Decomposition (SVD). Our perspective yields three key insights: (1) Pre-training objectives determine how features are encoded. DINOv2 aligns spatial features for efficient linear extraction, while Masked Autoencoders (MAE) tend to disperse these signals, requiring a broader spatial context. (2) Explicit geometric representations are highly compressible, suggesting dense predictive heads could potentially be constrained to low-rank subspaces with minimal performance loss. (3) The layer-wise task affinity suggests that geometric precision peaks at intermediate layers before yielding to semantic abstraction in the final layers. By connecting internal encoding mechanics with downstream performance, these findings provide a basis for effective feature selection and lightweight decoder design. The source code is available at https://github.com/Zhou-Weichen/Geosubprobe.

AI.tldr: Decomposing converged linear probes with SVD reveals low-rank subspaces carrying explicit geometric signals in self-supervised ViTs, showing pretraining objectives shape geometry, geometry is highly compressible, and geometric precision peaks at intermediate layers.
AI.motivation: Move beyond black-box linear probes to disentangle how dense geometric information is encoded in self-supervised Vision Transformers and assess how pretraining objectives influence geometric representations.
AI.method: Fit converged linear probes, apply singular value decomposition to their weights to isolate dominant low-rank subspaces that carry geometry; compare pretraining regimes (DINOv2 vs MAE); analyze layer-wise affinity between geometry and semantics; evaluate compressibility and implications for decoder design; provide source code.
AI.result: Explicit geometric representations are highly compressible and reside in low-rank subspaces; DINOv2 aligns spatial features for efficient linear extraction, while MAE disperses geometric signals requiring broader spatial context; geometric precision is strongest at intermediate layers before semantic abstraction in final layers.
AI.conclusion: Understanding internal encoding mechanics enables informed feature selection and the design of lightweight decoders, potentially constraining predictive heads to low-rank subspaces with minimal performance loss.

title: Do Newer Lightweight CNNs Perform Better Under Resource Constraints? A Controlled Multigenerational Study of Architecture, Initialization, Training Budget, and Efficiency
summary: Newer lightweight convolutional neural networks are often presented as improving predictive performance and deployment efficiency, but such claims require controlled evaluation. This study compares nine lightweight CNN model packages across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet under a shared downstream protocol. We report top-1 accuracy, macro F1, top-5 accuracy, parameter count, FP32 storage, GMACs, batch-size-1 latency on an NVIDIA L4 and AMD Ryzen 5 5500U CPU, peak PyTorch CUDA allocated tensor memory, and point estimate Pareto frontiers. EfficientNetV2-S achieves the highest observed top-1 accuracy on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 at 97.57% and 86.98%, while RepViT-M1.0 leads Tiny ImageNet at 79.87%. EfficientNet-B0 remains within 0.22, 0.85, and 1.79 percentage points of the best result on the three datasets while using approximately 79% fewer parameters and 86% fewer GMACs than EfficientNetV2-S. It also appears on every evaluated accuracy and resource Pareto frontier, making it the most consistently competitive intermediate-budget option. MobileNetV3-Small has the lowest GMAC count, is the fastest model under both CPU thread settings, and records higher observed accuracy than MobileNetV4-Conv-S on all three datasets. Under random initialization, it leads MobileNetV4-Conv-S by 2.55, 1.76, and 0.99 points, with paired test-set intervals excluding zero for the fixed trained models. EfficientNet-B0 remains 3.29, 10.10, and 17.54 points below its pretrained counterpart after 100 epochs of scratch training, despite requiring about five times the recorded training time. SqueezeNet1.1 has the fewest parameters and lowest peak CUDA allocation, but substantially weaker accuracy. Latency rankings differ sharply between the L4 and CPU environments, showing that GMACs alone do not predict measured inference performance. Overall, newer designs provide selective rather than universal gains

AI.tldr: Comparative evaluation of nine lightweight CNN packages on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet using a uniform protocol; EfficientNetV2-S often achieves top accuracy; EfficientNet-B0 is consistently competitive with fewer parameters/GMACs; MobileNetV3-Small is fastest with low GMACs; SqueezeNet1.1 is parameter-efficient but weaker in accuracy; GMACs do not reliably predict latency; gains are selective rather than universal.
AI.motivation: Test the validity of claims that newer lightweight CNN designs universally improve predictive performance and deployment efficiency by conducting a controlled, cross-model, cross-dataset evaluation with rich resource and latency metrics and Pareto-front analysis.
AI.method: A shared downstream evaluation protocol applied to nine lightweight CNN packages across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet. Metrics include top-1 accuracy, macro F1, top-5 accuracy, parameter count, FP32 storage, GMACs, batch-size-1 latency on NVIDIA L4 and AMD Ryzen 5 5500U CPU, peak PyTorch CUDA allocated memory, and Pareto frontiers.
AI.result: EfficientNetV2-S attains the highest observed top-1 accuracy on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 (97.57% and 86.98%). RepViT-M1.0 leads Tiny ImageNet (79.87%). EfficientNet-B0 remains within small gaps of the best results on all three datasets while using ~79% fewer parameters and ~86% fewer GMACs than EfficientNetV2-S. EfficientNet-B0 appears on every accuracy and resource Pareto frontier, making it a consistently competitive intermediate-budget option. MobileNetV3-Small has the lowest GMACs, is the fastest under both CPU thread settings, and surpasses MobileNetV4-Conv-S in accuracy across all three datasets. Under random initialization, EfficientNet-B0 leads MobileNetV4-Conv-S by 2.55, 1.76, and 0.99 points, with fixed-trained-model intervals excluding zero. After 100 epochs of scratch training, EfficientNet-B0 is 3.29, 10.10, and 17.54 points below its pretrained counterpart, despite roughly five times longer training. SqueezeNet1.1 uses the fewest parameters and shows the lowest peak CUDA allocation but weaker accuracy overall. Latency rankings vary markedly between L4 and CPU environments; GMACs alone do not predict real-world inference performance.
AI.conclusion: Newer CNN designs yield selective gains rather than universal improvements. EfficientNet-B0 stands out as a robust, intermediate-budget option across datasets; model efficiency cannot be inferred from GMACs alone and hardware-aware evaluation with Pareto analyses is essential for deploying lightweight models.

title: Purified OPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation Without Losing How to Think
summary: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) has emerged as a promising paradigm for improving LLM reasoning, where a privileged teacher with access to reference solutions provides token-level supervision on the student's own generated trajectories. However, we find that OPSD consistently fails on long chain-of-thought (long-CoT) reasoning models, yielding at best marginal gains while destabilizing the reflective reasoning capability these models depend on. Through a novel decomposition of the teacher's supervision signal, we identify the root cause: the teacher's supervision is dominated by a reference-induced component that drives rote memorization of reference-specific shortcuts, while the question-conditioned, inference-transferable component is ignored or actively opposed. Based on this diagnosis, we propose a two-step solution. First, we construct a reference-only teacher (the same model conditioned on the reference without the question) to isolate the non-transferable component of the supervision signal; the residual after subtracting this component captures the question-conditioned, inference-transferable correction. Second, we use pointwise mutual information (PMI) as the mechanism to transform this residual into a well-formed PMI target distribution that the student can directly distill from, filtering out the reference-induced shortcut. Experiments on four long-CoT models across two datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over both the base model and standard OPSD, while preserving the models' natural epistemic behavior throughout training.

AI.tldr: OPSD underperforms on long-CoT due to teacher supervision dominated by reference-induced shortcuts; a two-step method isolates transferable signal via a reference-only teacher and PMI-based target distillation, yielding robust improvements across models/datasets.
AI.motivation: Diagnose why OPSD fails on long-CoT reasoning and preserve reflective, non-reference-based reasoning while leveraging teacher guidance.
AI.method: 1) Decompose teacher supervision into a reference-induced component and a question-conditioned, transferable component by using a reference-only teacher. Subtract to obtain the residual. 2) Use pointwise mutual information (PMI) to convert the residual into a well-formed PMI target distribution for distillation, thereby filtering out reference shortcuts.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on four long-CoT models over two datasets shows consistent improvements over the base model and standard OPSD, with maintained epistemic behavior during training.
AI.conclusion: A two-step approach—isolating transferable supervision via a reference-only teacher and PMI-based distillation of the residual—mitigates reference-induced shortcuts in OPSD and improves long-CoT performance while preserving reflective reasoning.

title: Training-free Controllable Human Motion Generation under Heterogeneous Constraints
summary: Training-free controllable motion generation has attracted growing interest for enabling flexible constraint enforcement without constraint-specific training. However, existing training-free methods require constraints to be continuous objective-based with differentiable losses, while many real-world requirements are criterion-based and provide only discontinuous, sparse, or even black-box feedback. In this paper, we propose Motion-Inference-as-Control (MIC), the first training-free motion generation framework that handles both continuous objective-based and criterion-based motion constraints under a shared mechanism. The key idea is to cast diffusion-based motion generation as a stochastic control problem. This perspective not only provides principled and practically effective step-wise control laws that support criterion-based constraints without requiring differentiability and naturally accommodate objective-based constraints as a special case, but also motivates a control-oriented constraint coordination mechanism that adaptively balances and reconciles motion constraints during generation. Experiments across diverse constraint settings demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework.

AI.tldr: Introduces Motion-Inference-as-Control (MIC), a training-free diffusion-based motion generation framework that unifies continuous objective-based and discrete/criterion-based constraints via stochastic control and a coordination mechanism.
AI.motivation: Existing training-free methods rely on differentiable losses for continuous constraints, but many real-world constraints are discontinuous, sparse, or black-box. A single, training-free framework capable of handling both constraint types is needed.
AI.method: Frame diffusion-based motion generation as a stochastic control problem. Derive principled, step-wise control laws that support criterion-based constraints without requiring differentiability, while treating objective-based constraints as a special case. Introduce a control-oriented constraint coordination mechanism to adaptively balance and reconcile multiple constraints during generation.
AI.result: Empirical evaluations across diverse constraint settings demonstrate MIC’s effectiveness in enforcing constraints while maintaining motion quality and flexibility.
AI.conclusion: MIC provides a unified, training-free approach for constraint-aware motion generation, enabling robust handling of both continuous and criterion-based constraints through stochastic control and adaptive coordination.

title: Liquid Latent State Dynamics for Interpretable Turbofan Degradation Modeling
summary: Multivariate time-series models for prognostics are often evaluated by point prediction accuracy, yet their internal states rarely expose a coherent degradation process. We study liquid neural networks as latent dynamics models for aircraft engine health monitoring on the C-MAPSS benchmark. The proposed model encodes a history window into a latent state, evolves that state with a liquid transition model, and decodes future sensor observations. To separate health evolution from operating-condition variation, the latent state is factorized into degradation and condition components. Remaining useful life, monotonic risk, and latent-consistency losses supervise the degradation component, while condition prediction and decorrelation losses discourage operating-condition leakage. Across FD001--FD004, the full disentangled model improves overall sensor forecasting RMSE from 0.2438 for a GRU baseline to 0.2266, with the largest gains on the multi-condition subsets FD002 and FD004. The learned degradation state also forms a clearer temporal degradation axis, reaching an average state-speed Spearman correlation of 0.5960. Direct remaining-useful-life regression remains stronger for the GRU baseline, indicating that the proposed representation is currently more effective as an interpretable world model for degradation dynamics than as a calibrated lifetime regressor. These results suggest that liquid latent dynamics can bridge predictive maintenance forecasting and inspectable health-state modeling.

AI.tldr: A latent dynamics model using liquid neural networks for aircraft engine health monitoring; it disentangles degradation from operating conditions, improving sensor forecasting RMSE and yielding a clearer degradation axis, though RUL regression remains stronger with traditional GRUs.
AI.motivation: To expose a coherent degradation process in multivariate prognostics and separate health evolution from operating-condition variation, enabling interpretable health-state modeling and aligned forecasting.
AI.method: Encode a history window into a latent state, evolve with a liquid transition model, and decode future sensor observations. Factorize latent state into degradation and condition components. Supervise degradation with remaining-useful-life, monotonic risk, and latent-consistency losses; discourage operation-condition leakage with condition prediction and decorrelation losses. Evaluate on C-MAPSS FD001–FD004; compare against GRU baseline.
AI.result: Sensor forecasting RMSE improves from 0.2438 (GRU baseline) to 0.2266 for the disentangled liquid latent model, with the largest improvements on multi-condition subsets FD002/FD004. The degradation state shows a stronger temporal degradation axis (average Spearman 0.5960). Direct RUL regression remains stronger for the GRU baseline, indicating the proposed representation is more effective as an interpretable health-state model than as a calibrated lifetime regressor. Overall, results suggest liquid latent dynamics can connect predictive maintenance forecasting with inspectable health-state modeling.
AI.conclusion: Liquid latent dynamics offer a promising framework to couple accurate forecasting with interpretable health-state representations, potentially guiding maintenance decisions through a transparent degradation axis, though at present they do not outperform conventional RUL regression in direct lifetime prediction.

title: Copewell: A Multi-Agent Swarm Architecture for Equitable Mental Wellness Support
summary: Mental health disorders affect nearly one billion people globally, yet 75% of individuals in low- and middle-income countries receive no treatment due to workforce shortages, cost barriers, and stigma. Current AI-powered wellness solutions predominantly rely on single-mode conversational interfaces that suffer high abandonment rates and fail to provide measurable, immediate relief calibrated to users' dynamic emotional states. This paper presents Copewell, a novel multi-agent swarm system designed to expand access to mental wellness support through human-centered AI principles. Our architecture introduces three technical innovations: (1) a multi-source assessment framework integrating self-reported, physiological, and contextual data to mitigate algorithmic bias; (2) valence-arousal emotion mapping using Russell's Circumplex Model of Affect to route users to specialized AI agents; and (3) dual-mode intervention delivery combining conversational support with evidence-based sensory wellness protocols. We examine the sociotechnical design considerations underlying Copewell's development, including a privacy-first architecture, embedded ethical oversight through a dedicated Ethics Supervisor agent, and participatory design informed by mental health practitioners. Early practitioner engagement and beta deployment inform design decisions and identify directions for future empirical evaluation. This work contributes to responsible AI discourse by demonstrating how technical architecture can operationalize equity and safety principles from inception.

AI.tldr: Copewell introduces a multi-agent swarm for mental wellness with multi-source assessment, Russell-based emotion routing, and dual-mode interventions; designed with privacy and ethics oversight to broaden access while addressing AI biases.
AI.motivation: Address global mental health burden and access gaps—especially in LMICs—where workforce shortages, cost, and stigma limit treatment; critique of single-mode AI wellness tools and abandonment risks.
AI.method: Proposes a three-pronged technical design: (1) multi-source assessment integrating self-report, physiological, and contextual data to reduce bias; (2) valence-arousal emotion mapping using Russell's Circumplex Model of Affect to route users to specialized AI agents; (3) dual-mode intervention delivering conversational support plus evidence-based sensory wellness protocols. Employs a multi-agent swarm architecture, privacy-first design, an Ethics Supervisor agent, and participatory design with mental health practitioners; early practitioner engagement and beta deployment inform ongoing design and future empirical evaluation.
AI.result: Proposes a design framework and initial prototype with practitioner input; reports no empirical outcomes yet but demonstrates a path toward equity and safety in AI mental health tools and outlines directions for future evaluation.
AI.conclusion: Advances responsible AI in mental health by embedding equity, safety, and stakeholder involvement from inception; outlines a scalable, multi-modal, ethically supervised system to expand access to mental wellness support and sets the stage for future empirical validation.

title: Mirror Illusion Art
comment: CVPR 2026 Highlight, also got an Efficient CVPR award
summary: Mirror Illusion Art is a novel reflection-conditioned 3D illusion where one object yields two target appearances (front and mirror). The task is formulated as inverse design from two target 2D images (front and mirror) to a printable 3D object with geometry and texture. Prior topology-driven and shadow-based approaches demand substantial manual effort, optimize shape only, and often yield non-smooth or incomplete geometry. To address these challenges, we propose AutoMIA, an automated Mirror Illusion Art design pipeline that jointly optimizes shape and color. To stabilize optimization and suppress artifacts, four mechanisms are introduced: (1) projection-alignment component (PAC) selection to reduce surface noise, (2) position-weighted adaptive (PWA) suppression for background noise, (3) internal voxel preservation (IVP) to prevent internal fractures, and (4) shape-color decoupled (SCD) optimization that balance shape and color optimization. AutoMIA generate diverse smooth Mirror Illusion artworks successfully both in the digital and physical world, with only around 76s design time and 2.6 GB memory on average using a single RTX 3090, advancing inverse graphics and computational design. Our code is available at https://github.com/zxp555/AutoMIA.

AI.tldr: AutoMIA automates joint optimization of 3D shape and texture to realize Mirror Illusion Art from two target 2D views (front and mirror), addressing prior manual/topology-based designs. It achieves smooth, printable geometry with ~76s design time on a single RTX 3090, using four artifact-suppression mechanisms and a decoupled shape-color optimization. Code released.
AI.motivation: Existing inverse-design pipelines for mirror-illusion art rely on topology-driven/shadow-based methods requiring manual intervention, optimize only geometry, and often yield noisy or incomplete geometry. There is a need for automated, robust joint optimization of shape and color to produce high-quality, printable 3D objects that reproduce two target views.
AI.method: AutoMIA introduces four mechanisms to stabilize optimization: (1) projection-alignment component (PAC) to reduce surface noise, (2) position-weighted adaptive (PWA) suppression to reduce background noise, (3) internal voxel preservation (IVP) to prevent internal fractures, and (4) shape-color decoupled (SCD) optimization to balance shape and color updates. The pipeline jointly optimizes geometry and texture to match two target 2D views (front and mirror), enabling digital and physical outputs with efficient resource usage (≈76 s, ≈2.6 GB on RTX 3090).
AI.result: The approach yields diverse, smooth Mirror Illusion artworks in both digital and physical forms. It demonstrates rapid design of inverse-graphics-driven prints and advances computational design, with publicly available code at the referenced repository.
AI.conclusion: Automating geometry and color optimization for mirror-based inverse design reduces manual effort, mitigates artifacts, and produces high-quality, printable 3D objects that satisfy dual target views, highlighting AutoMIA as a robust framework for inverse graphics and computational design.

title: Fast and Accurate Anomaly Detection in Time Series
summary: Anomaly detection is a critical and evolving field in Machine Learning, with applications targeting different domains such as cybersecurity, finance, healthcare, manufacturing and IoT (Internet of Things) systems. Traditionally, anomaly detection algorithms have been designed using both supervised and unsupervised learning paradigms. The fundamental challenge in real-world anomaly detection scenarios is related to the inherent class imbalance (anomalies are typically rare) and, for supervised methods, to the scarcity of labelled anomalous data. Indeed, labelling is both expensive and time-consuming. Conversely unsupervised methods do not require labelling, but may suffer from high false positive rates when deployed in safety-critical applications. In this work we introduce a novel unsupervised algorithm for anomaly detection in time series based on the Haar discrete wavelet and a suitably designed $t$-test. We establish the theoretical foundation of the proposed $t$-test and, through extensive experimentation across 343 datasets, demonstrate that our algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised and self-supervised benchmarks.

AI.tldr: Unsupervised time-series anomaly detection using Haar discrete wavelet transform and a specially designed t-test; strong empirical performance across 343 datasets.
AI.motivation: Class imbalance and scarcity of labeled anomalies hinder supervised methods; unsupervised approaches risk high false positives; aim to provide a robust, theoretically grounded unsupervised method.
AI.method: Leverages Haar wavelet decomposition to capture multi-resolution temporal patterns and applies a theoretically grounded t-test to identify anomalies at multiple scales. The approach is unsupervised and designed for time-series data.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on 343 datasets shows the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised and self-supervised baselines.
AI.conclusion: The method offers a solid unsupervised detection framework with theoretical foundation and strong empirical performance; potential for real-time deployment; further work could explore parameter sensitivity and extensions to other wavelets or multivariate signals.

title: AgenticSTS: A Bounded-Memory Testbed for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: Memory for a long-horizon LLM agent is a contract about what each future decision is allowed to see. The simplest contract appends past observations, tool calls, and reflections to every prompt, which makes prior context easy to access but also turns it into a jumbled mixture in which the effect of any single memory component is hard to isolate. We introduce and instrument an alternative bounded contract: every decision is made from a fresh user message assembled by typed retrieval, with no raw cross-decision transcript appended. The prompt thus stays bounded across runs of any length, and any single layer can be ablated in isolation. We instantiate the contract in Slay the Spire 2, a closed-rule stochastic deck-building game whose runs require hundreds of tactical and strategic decisions. A public online benchmark of frontier LLMs on the same game reports zero wins at the lowest difficulty across five configurations, and the developer-reported human win rate at the same difficulty is 16%; the task is hard but not saturated. Within our harness, a fixed-A0 ablation shows the largest observed difference when triggered strategic skills are enabled: the no-store baseline wins 3/10 games and adding the skill layer 6/10. At this sample size the comparison is directional rather than statistically decisive (Fisher exact p\approx0.37); a cross-backbone probe and public accumulating-context baselines are reported as operational comparisons rather than controlled tests of the contract variable itself. We release a reproducible testbed: 298 completed trajectories with condition tags, frozen memory/skill snapshots, prompt records, and analysis scripts -- an agent design and a validated, reusable methodology for studying how explicit memory layers shape long-horizon LLM-agent decisions.

AI.tldr: Proposes a bounded memory contract for long-horizon LLM agents, enabling isolated analysis of memory layers by reconstructing per-decision prompts via typed retrieval instead of concatenating full transcripts; tested in Slay the Spire 2 with ablations, yielding directional but not stat-sig improvements, and released a reproducible testbed.
AI.motivation: Address the difficulty of attributing decisions to individual memory components when using a traditional all-past-context prompt, which blurs effects due to jumbled, shared context across decisions.
AI.method: Introduce a per-decision bounding contract where each decision uses a fresh user message assembled by typed retrieval; no raw cross-decision transcript is appended. Implemented in Slay the Spire 2. Compare a no-store baseline to an ablated memory layer (skill layer) under a fixed-A0 setting; report results from 298 completed trajectories with condition tags, plus cross-backbone and public baselines for context; provide reproducible data and analysis scripts.
AI.result: In the main test, no-store achieved 3/10 wins while adding the skill layer yielded 6/10 wins (p ≈ 0.37; not statistically decisive). Frontier LLM benchmark reports zero wins at lowest difficulty across five configurations. The work also includes a cross-backbone probe and public accumulating-context baselines for operational comparison.
AI.conclusion: Memory architecture significantly shapes long-horizon decision-making under a bounded contract, and the proposed framework enables isolating memory components. However, evidence is directional and limited by small sample size and domain specificity; a reproducible testbed is released to support further systematic study.

title: UnderOneFacade: Worldwide Facade Semantic Segmentation Benchmark Dataset
summary: Globally consistent semantic digital twins require centimeter-accurate and geographically transferable 3D facade segmentation. However, progress in facade parsing is limited by the lack of large-scale, standardized benchmarks for evaluating cross-domain generalization. Existing datasets are geographically narrow, semantically inconsistent, or insufficiently precise. We introduce UnderOneFacade, the largest cross-country and cross-continent 3D facade benchmark to date, comprising centimeter-accurate point clouds with hierarchical, harmonized, and architecturally grounded semantic labels totaling 2.7 billion annotated points. Through a systematic evaluation of representative point-, graph- and transformer-based architectures, we show that current methods struggle to recognize fine-grained architectural elements and degrade significantly across geographic domains, with the best models achieving only up to 33 IoU on the fine-grained LoFG3 benchmark. By combining geometric precision with standardized semantics at unprecedented scale, UnderOneFacade establishes a rigorous benchmark for developing robust and transferable 3D segmentation models. The dataset, evaluation scripts, and pretrained models will be released upon publication.

AI.tldr: UnderOneFacade is a large cross-country 3D facade benchmark with 2.7B annotated points and centimeter-accurate semantics, revealing that current methods struggle with fine-grained, cross-domain generalization (up to 33 IoU on LoFG3).
AI.motivation: Address the lack of large-scale, standardized benchmarks for cross-domain generalization in 3D facade segmentation to enable globally transferable, centimeter-accurate semantic models for digital twins.
AI.method: Construct a centimeter-accurate multi-country 3D facade dataset with hierarchical, harmonized semantic labels; evaluate representative point-, graph-, and transformer-based architectures on cross-domain generalization, including a fine-grained LoFG3 benchmark; provide dataset, evaluation scripts, and pretrained models.
AI.result: Current state-of-the-art methods show degraded performance across geographic domains; best models reach up to 33 IoU on LoFG3, indicating substantial room for improvement in fine-grained, cross-domain segmentation.
AI.conclusion: UnderOneFacade sets a rigorous, large-scale benchmark for developing robust and transferable 3D facade segmentation methods, promoting progress toward globally consistent semantic digital twins; dataset and tools to be released upon publication.

title: A Memory Efficient Unified Algorithm for Online Learning of Linear Dynamical Systems
summary: Motivated by the challenge of stabilizing a general unknown linear dynamical system (LDS) from observations, we study the natural prerequisite of online prediction. Our goal is to achieve sublinear regret with a memory footprint that adapts to the intrinsic complexity of the dynamics rather than the full hidden -- state dimension. We focus on the practically central regime of systems with low instability complexity -- eigenvalues outside the real stable interval that do not decay rapidly, together with non-semisimple modes-potentially embedded in an otherwise stable real spectrum of much higher dimension; we write $k$ for this count. This regime is the primary setting in which stabilization is plausible: we show that many systems with high instability complexity cannot be stabilized without exponentially large controls. Thus, prediction is meaningful for stabilization precisely when the instability complexity is small. Within this regime, we introduce a unified online algorithm that handles every LDS (including non-diagonalizable systems with complex or exploding modes) with a learnable parameter count of $\widetilde{O}(k)$. Finally, we prove a lower bound showing that $k$ is a valid complexity measure: any filter-based predictor needs at least $k$ filters. Experiments corroborate our theory: on a high-dimensional system, our predictor sharply outperforms prior methods at an equal parameter budget.

AI.tldr: Introduces an online predictor for unknown linear dynamical systems that achieves sublinear regret with a parameter count scaling as ~k, where k is the instability-complexity. Provides a lower bound and empirical validation, showing prediction is meaningful only when k is small.
AI.motivation: Stabilizing unknown linear dynamical systems from observations is challenging; objective is online prediction with a memory footprint that adapts to intrinsic dynamics rather than full state dimension, and to identify regimes where stabilization is feasible (low instability complexity).
AI.method: A unified online algorithm that handles all LDS (including non-diagonalizable, complex, or exploding modes) with a learnable parameter count of ~O(k); theoretical analysis linking regret/feasibility to instability complexity k; a lower bound showing any filter-based predictor needs at least k filters.
AI.result: Demonstrates sublinear regret with memory ~O(k) in the low-instability regime; proves that high instability complexity generally requires exponentially large controls for stabilization; empirical results on high-dimensional systems show the proposed predictor outperforms prior methods at equivalent parameter budgets.
AI.conclusion: Instability complexity k is the intrinsic measure governing feasibility and resource requirements for online stabilization. When k is small, effective prediction and stabilization are possible with near-optimal (in k) parameter scaling; otherwise, stabilization becomes impractical without exponential resources.

title: A Hippocampus for Linear Attention: An Exact Memory for What the Recurrent State Forgets
summary: Linear-attention and state-space language models compress the prefix into a fixed-size recurrent state, yielding O(1) memory at the cost of a lossy exact memory: when many key--value associations compete, earlier facts are overwritten and needle recall degrades. Inspired by Complementary Learning Systems, we give linear attention a hippocampal complement. HOLA (Hippocampal Linear Attention) keeps the usual delta-rule state as a compressive memory and adds a bounded exact KV cache, forming a semiparametric test-time memory: the state models linearly compressible structure, while the cache stores associations that should not be forced through that state. The cache writes without a learned eviction module, keeping tokens with large beta * ||e||, the prediction residual actually committed to the state; a decoupled RMSNorm-gamma cache read then turns these exact KV pairs into sharp retrieval rather than soft averaging. At 340M parameters trained on 15B SlimPajama tokens, HOLA lowers Wikitext perplexity from 27.32 to 22.92 (-16.1%), below a full-attention Transformer++ (26.88), and improves LAMBADA perplexity from 30.95 to 30.26. It also achieves the best linear in-context retrieval and remains much more robust than GDN or a matched HOLA+recency cache on RULER needle-in-a-haystack recall out to 32k tokens (16x its training length).

AI.tldr: HOLA augments linear attention with a hippocampus-inspired semiparametric memory by adding a bounded exact KV cache to the compressive delta-rule state, yielding strong perplexity improvements and robust long-context retrieval, outperforming both standard linear attention and full-attention baselines on several tasks.
AI.motivation: To mitigate the lossy memory problem of fixed-size recurrent states in linear attention models, which overwrites earlier facts when many key–value associations compete; inspired by Complementary Learning Systems (hippocampus-cortex separation).
AI.method: Introduce HOLA: maintain delta-rule compressive state; add a bounded exact KV cache, written without eviction; cache writes triggered by large beta * ||e|| (prediction residual large), cache read via a decoupled RMSNorm-gamma mechanism to produce sharp retrieval; semiparametric memory combining compressive state and exact KV store; evaluated on 340M param model trained on 15B SlimPajama tokens.
AI.result: Wikitext perplexity improves from 27.32 to 22.92 (-16.1%), beating full-attention Transformer++ at 26.88; LAMBADA perplexity improves from 30.95 to 30.26; achieves best linear in-context retrieval; robust against GDN and recency caches on RULER needle-in-a-haystack recall up to 32k tokens (16x training length).
AI.conclusion: HOLA demonstrates that a semiparametric memory—combining a learnable compressive state with a bounded exact cache—yields superior long-context modeling and retrieval with better efficiency, suggesting a viable path beyond pure full-attention or purely compressive models.

title: Spatio-Temporal and Clinical Conditioning for Fine-Grained Radiology Report Retrieval
summary: Radiology is vital to modern healthcare, but rising imaging demand and persistent workforce shortages strain reporting capacity and clinical workflows. Automated radiology report generation has the potential to support radiologists and help alleviate this burden; however, existing retrieval-based methods remain rigid, lack explicit anatomical grounding, and do not account for longitudinal disease progression or available clinical context. In this work, we introduce STAR3, a multimodal, spatio-temporal, attentive retrieval framework for radiology report generation that aligns region-level anatomical information with clinical indications and longitudinal changes across chest X-ray studies. Our framework employs an object detector to identify anatomically meaningful regions and retrieves semantically relevant report sentences conditioned on both current clinical context and changes observed between prior and current examinations. This design enables anatomically and temporally grounded report generation that better reflects clinical reporting practice. Experiments on the MIMIC-CXR dataset demonstrate that STAR3 outperforms current retrieval-based approaches on retrieval, NLP and clinical metrics, highlighting the value of conditioning retrieval anatomically, temporally and clinically for advancing automated radiology report generation.

AI.tldr: STAR3 introduces a multimodal, spatio-temporal retrieval framework for radiology report generation that grounds retrieval in anatomically defined regions and longitudinal context, outperforming existing retrieval-based methods on MIMIC-CXR.
AI.motivation: Healthcare imaging demand and radiology staffing shortages necessitate automated report generation. Existing retrieval-based methods are rigid and lack explicit anatomical grounding and longitudinal/contextual information.
AI.method: STAR3 uses an object detector to identify anatomically meaningful regions, then retrieves semantically relevant report sentences conditioned on current clinical context and changes between prior and current chest X-rays, enabling anatomically and temporally grounded generation.
AI.result: Experiments on MIMIC-CXR show STAR3 outperforms current retrieval-based approaches across retrieval, NLP, and clinical metrics by incorporating anatomical, temporal, and clinical conditioning.
AI.conclusion: Conditioning retrieval on anatomical regions, temporal changes, and clinical context yields more clinically faithful radiology reports and advances automated report generation.

title: Beyond the Performance Illusion: Structure-Aware Stratified Partitioning and Curriculum Distributionally Robust Optimization for Spatially Correlated Domains
summary: Performance evaluation in AI systems commonly assumes that random dataset splits produce independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) subsets. We show that this assumption often breaks down in spatiotemporally correlated domains such as aerial surveillance, precision agriculture, and medical imaging, leading to two systematic failures: data leakage, where correlated samples span training and validation splits and inflate performance estimates, and hidden stratification, where errors on minority subpopulations are obscured by aggregate metrics. To address these issues, we propose a unified evaluation and training framework for spatially correlated data. We introduce Structure-Aware Stratified Partitioning (SASP), which constructs validation splits that reduce spatiotemporal leakage while preserving meaningful class balance, and Curriculum Distributionally Robust Optimization (CDRO), a curriculum-based relaxation of distributionally robust training that stabilizes optimization under these stricter splits. Across multiple benchmarks, this combination yields consistently improved generalization, more reliable confidence calibration, and exposes failure modes that remain hidden under conventional random-split evaluation.

AI.tldr: Proposes SASP and CDRO to tackle data leakage and hidden stratification in spatiotemporal AI; improves generalization and calibration under non-i.i.d. splits.
AI.motivation: i.i.d. assumption often fails in spatially correlated domains, causing leakage and biased metrics; need unified evaluation/training approach.
AI.method: Structure-Aware Stratified Partitioning (SASP) for leakage-reducing, balanced splits; Curriculum Distributionally Robust Optimization (CDRO) for stable optimization under stricter splits.
AI.result: Consistent generalization gains, better confidence calibration, and uncovering failure modes not visible with random splits across multiple benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Unified framework improves reliability of evaluation and robustness of models in spatially correlated data environments.

title: Grounded autonomous research: a fault-tolerant LLM pipeline from corpus to manuscript in frontier computational physics
comment: 39 pages, 5 figures. Accepted at the ICML 2026 AI for Science Workshop (https://openreview.net/forum?id=R5YXaPgUAx). Includes the pipeline-generated companion physics manuscript as an appendix. Data and scaffolding archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21126996
summary: Autonomous-research agents have demonstrated end-to-end LLM automation in machine-learning sandboxes where execution provides calibration. Frontier physical science differs categorically: physical reasoning underlies every methodology choice, toolchains are often underdocumented, and calibration must come from external literature anchors - which unscaffolded agents cite but do not confront, hallucinating plausible, unverifiable results from internal priors. We present a pipeline that runs end-to-end from a corpus of 11,083 recent condensed-matter physics arXiv papers to a publication-grade manuscript with three substantive physics findings (here on altermagnetic piezomagnetism): the agent autonomously conceives a research direction by mapping the corpus, calibrates methodology by reproducing published references, conducts novel first-principles computations, and writes the manuscript - grounded in literature throughout, across 47 fresh-context sessions in six phases sharing only on-disk state, with 2,162 literature-consultation events. Fault tolerance emerges from redundancy: fresh-context isolation, distributed grounding, and adversarial review catch what any single session misses; pre- and post-pilot stages are fully autonomous, and pilot requires bounded human intervention only at reproduction failures - operational knowledge curation, not scientific direction. Two paired failure modes - a pre-architecture baseline and a no-pilot ablation - isolate structurally enforced numerical confrontation at calibration checkpoints as the operative grounding mechanism. The primitives, characterized failure modes, and quantified intervention pattern lay a foundation for autonomous research in high-stakes scientific domains beyond computational physics.

AI.tldr: An autonomous, literature-grounded research pipeline that ingests 11k condensed-matter arXiv papers to produce a publication-grade manuscript with three physics findings, featuring robust fault-tolerance and bounded human intervention.
AI.motivation: To overcome hallucination and miscalibration in unscaffolded autonomous agents by anchoring end-to-end research pipelines to external literature and validated methodology, enabling reproducible, publication-ready results in high-stakes physical science.
AI.method: An end-to-end pipeline that maps a large corpus of arXiv papers, calibrates methods by reproducing published references, conducts novel first-principles computations, and writes a manuscript. It operates across 47 fresh-context sessions with on-disk state and 2,162 literature-consultation events, using redundancy (fresh-context isolation, distributed grounding, adversarial review) for fault tolerance; stages include pre-pilot, pilot with bounded human intervention only at reproduction failures, and post-pilot autonomous stages.
AI.result: Produced three substantive physics findings on altermagnetic piezomagnetism and a publication-grade manuscript grounded in literature, demonstrating autonomous research with explicit grounding mechanisms and quantified interaction patterns across multiple sessions and reviews.
AI.conclusion: The work defines primitives, failure modes, and intervention patterns that underpin autonomous research in high-stakes scientific domains beyond computational physics, laying a foundation for robust, literature-grounded automation.

title: Evaluating Vision-Language Models as a Zero-Shot Learning Alternative to You Only Look Once and Optical Character Recognition for Nigerian License Plate Recognition
summary: License Plate Recognition (LPR) systems are critical tools in traffic monitoring, security enforcement, and urban mobility management. Traditional LPR systems often rely on a multi-stage pipeline involving object detection using You Only Look Once (YOLO) and Optical Character Recognition (OCR), which suffer from limitations such as high resource demands, poor performance in unstructured environments, and the need for large annotated datasets. This study explores the potential of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) as a unified, zeroshot learning solution for Nigerian license plate recognition. Using a curated dataset of 88 challenging real-world images collected in Nigeria, we evaluate five selected VLMs: Gemini 2.0 Flash Exp (Google DeepMind), Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (Alibaba), GPT-4o (OpenAI), Claude 4 Sonnet (Anthropic), and Llama 3.2 Vision 90b (Meta). Results based on Character Error Rate (CER) reveal that Gemini and Qwen significantly outperform other models in both accuracy and robustness, on the challenging image scenarios. This work highlights the practical advantages of VLMs over YOLO+OCR, questions the claims by model providers, and compares the performances of the VLMs.

AI.tldr: Zero-shot license plate recognition using Vision-Language Models on 88 Nigerian images; Gemini 2.0 Flash Exp and Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct outperform other VLMs and YOLO+OCR in CER and robustness.
AI.motivation: Address limitations of traditional multi-stage LPR pipelines (resource-intensive, poor in unstructured environments, relies on large annotated data) by investigating unified zeroshot VLMs for Nigerian license plate recognition.
AI.method: Benchmark five VLMs (Gemini 2.0 Flash Exp, Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, GPT-4o, Claude 4 Sonnet, Llama 3.2 Vision 90b) on a curated set of 88 real-world Nigerian license plate images; evaluate using Character Error Rate (CER); compare against a YOLO+OCR baseline; analyze performance in challenging scenarios and discuss model-provider claims.
AI.result: Gemini 2.0 Flash Exp and Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct deliver the best CER and robustness among the tested models; several VLMs outperform the YOLO+OCR baseline, highlighting practical advantages of VLMs for LPR and casting doubt on some provider claims.
AI.conclusion: VLM-based zeroshot LPR is a promising direction for real-world, unstructured environments with limited annotated data; the study supports the superior performance of certain VLMs (Gemini and Qwen) over others and over traditional pipelines, but is limited by the small dataset and scope; future work should expand datasets, test prompting strategies, and assess generalization across geographies.

title: SA-HGNN: Sample-Adaptive Hyperbolic Graph Neural Network for EEG-Based Depression Recognition
summary: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have been widely used to capture spatial functional connectivity patterns to improve electroencephalography (EEG)-based depression recognition performance. However, the functional connectivity of brain networks in patients with depression exhibits an inherent hierarchical structure, making it difficult to capture accurate connection patterns. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel model named Sample-Adaptive Hyperbolic Graph Neural Network (SA-HGNN), which aims to accurately extract the authentic hierarchical structure of depression-affected brain networks. Specifically, the proposed model comprises three core modules. First, a Sample-Adaptive Graph Construction module dynamically constructs personalized brain network topologies to capture more complex spatial relationships within the brain network. Second, hyperbolic graph convolution is employed to overcome the representation bottlenecks of Euclidean space, leveraging hyperbolic geometry to precisely capture latent hierarchical relationships within the brain network. Finally, an Attention Pooling module adaptively filters out highly redundant noise channels in EEG signals, effectively mitigating the interference of inherent noise on the authentic hierarchical topology. Extensive experiments on public EEG datasets demonstrate the superior performance of our method across resting-state and task-related paradigms, validating its robustness to noise and efficacy in capturing abnormal functional connectivity patterns in brain networks of patients with depression.

AI.tldr: SA-HGNN is a novel EEG-based depression recognition model that combines sample-adaptive graph construction, hyperbolic graph convolution, and attention pooling to capture and denoise hierarchical brain connectivity patterns, achieving robust state-of-the-art results on public datasets.
AI.motivation: Depression-related brain networks exhibit intrinsic hierarchical structure that is not well captured by traditional Euclidean GNNs. There is a need for sample-specific topology construction and memory-efficient representation to accurately model functional connectivity and suppress noise.
AI.method: 1) Sample-Adaptive Graph Construction to dynamically build personalized brain networks per sample; 2) Hyperbolic Graph Convolution to exploit hyperbolic geometry and capture latent hierarchical relationships; 3) Attention Pooling to filter redundant noisy EEG channels and mitigate noise impact on topology; evaluated on resting-state and task-related EEG datasets.
AI.result: The model achieves superior performance across resting-state and task paradigms, showing robustness to noise and improved capture of abnormal functional connectivity patterns in depression compared to baselines.
AI.conclusion: SA-HGNN effectively models the hierarchical structure of depression-affected brain networks in EEG data, offering a robust and adaptable framework for identifying depression-related connectivity patterns and potentially enhancing diagnostic performance.

title: DRIFTLENS: Measuring Memory-Induced Reasoning Drift in Personalized Language Models
summary: Personalization changes what a model says to a user; we show that it can also change the reasoning trajectory used to justify the response. Modern LLMs personalize interactions by storing user attributes, preferences, and prior context, then injecting this information into future prompts. We study whether such memory reshapes reasoning on open-ended questions where no single ground-truth answer exists. To quantify this effect, we introduce DRIFTLENS, a ground-truth-free framework that maps each expressed reasoning step to a value category and measures divergence between a question's no-memory trajectory and its trajectory under injected user-attribute memory. We first validate that DRIFTLENS distinguishes content-free pragmatic noise from substantive reasoning changes. Across four LLMs and 10 user-attribute categories, including age, occupation, and disability, user-attribute memory induces medium-to-large reasoning drift above each model's pragmatic-noise floor, even when final answers remain fluent, on-topic, and plausible. We then evaluate GRPO- and DPO-based post-training methods for reducing drift. Both reduce drift, but neither uniformly dominates; effects on downstream capability, helpfulness, and instruction following are model-and reward-dependent. These results suggest that memory-induced reasoning drift is a measurable and only partly mitigated failure mode of personalized language models.

AI.tldr: Personalization memory can alter LLMs' reasoning trajectories as well as outputs; DRIFTLENS quantifies this open-ended reasoning drift, finding measurable drift across models and attributes; post-training methods can reduce drift but inconsistently across capabilities.
AI.motivation: To determine whether injecting user-attribute memory in personalized LLMs reshapes the reasoning process, not just responses, and to quantify this drift without a ground-truth for reasoning steps; and to evaluate mitigation strategies.
AI.method: Introduce DRIFTLENS, a ground-truth-free framework that maps each expressed reasoning step to a value category and measures divergence between the no-memory trajectory and the memory-injected trajectory for open-ended questions. Validate its ability to distinguish informative drift from pragmatic noise. Test across four LLMs and ten user-attribute categories (e.g., age, occupation, disability). Evaluate GRPO- and DPO-based post-training methods for drift mitigation.
AI.result: DRIFTLENS detects medium-to-large reasoning drift induced by user-attribute memory, exceeding the pragmatic-noise floor, while final answers remain fluent and on-topic. Post-training methods (GRPO and DPO) reduce drift but do not uniformly dominate; impact on downstream capabilities, helpfulness, and instruction-following is model- and reward-dependent.
AI.conclusion: Memory-induced reasoning drift is a measurable, partially mitigable failure mode of personalized language models, warranting further study and careful design of personalization mechanisms.

title: ComplexMimic: Human-Scene Interaction Imitation in Complex 3D Environments
summary: Physics-based Human-Scene Interaction (HSI) imitation learning is crucial for embodied intelligence as it bridges the gap between kinematic 3D motions and real-world dynamics. However, most existing methods focus on simplified scene settings, leaving complex environments largely unexplored, which limits their applicability in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we focus on HSI mimicry in complex environments. Under this complex setting, we observe an inherent trade-off between successfully performing interaction and maintaining natural, physically plausible motions. To address this challenge, we propose ComplexMimic, a framework that reconstructs diverse HSI by interpreting imperfect MoCap data. First, we introduce a Dual Flow Strategy, which learns two complementary experts: an imitation expert for accurate motion tracking and an interaction expert for collision-aware adaptation in complex scenes. Second, naive multi-expert distillation, which treats all experts equally, often under-samples challenging behaviors, limiting effective learning. To mitigate this issue, we propose a difficulty-aware distillation strategy that adaptively weights supervision and prioritizes hard-yet-learnable trajectories guided by failure statistics and learning progress signals. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms current state-of-the-art methods. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/LuPan23/ComplexMimic.

AI.tldr: ComplexMimic introduces a dual-expert, difficulty-aware distillation framework for physics-based human-scene interaction imitation in complex environments, achieving state-of-the-art results on three benchmarks by balancing motion plausibility with collision-aware interaction.
AI.motivation: Existing HSI imitation methods focus on simplified scenes, leaving complex environments underexplored and creating a trade-off: achieving accurate interaction can degrade physically plausible motion. This work aims to bridge the gap by learning from imperfect MoCap data in complex scenes.
AI.method: Proposes Dual Flow Strategy with two experts: an imitation expert for accurate motion tracking and an interaction expert for collision-aware adaptation. Replaces naive multi-expert distillation with a difficulty-aware distillation strategy that adaptively weights supervision based on failure statistics and learning progress. Reconstructs diverse HSI from imperfect MoCap data and validates on three benchmark datasets.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation shows the proposed method outperforming current state-of-the-art methods on three benchmarks, demonstrating improved balance between accurate imitation and physically plausible interaction.
AI.conclusion: ComplexMimic provides an effective framework for HSI in complex environments, enabling more natural, collision-aware motions while improving imitation accuracy; code is released for reproducibility.

title: kNNGuard: Turning LLM Hidden Activations into a Training-Free Configurable Guardrail
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in domains requiring guardrails to detect unsafe, off-topic, or adversarial prompts. Existing guardrails predominately rely on fine-tuning to build classifiers, which often suffer from low generalization and high inference latency. We present kNNGuard, a training-free guardrail that utilizes the activation space of an off-the-shelf LLM. Given a small bank of 50 safe and unsafe prompts, kNNGuard extracts hidden activations and performs multi-layer kNN fusing activation-space and embedding-space scores for classification. Across six domains spanning topical and security prompts, kNNGuard achieves competitive or superior F1 compared to fine-tuned state-of-the-art guardrails while running 2.7x faster than the best comparable guardrail, and 10x faster than a fine-tuned safety classifier without gradient updates or fine-tuning. Domain adaptation requires only updating the labeled bank, which can be constructed in under 10 seconds and several orders of magnitude faster than established guardrails. We also analyze the impact of system prompts, layer selection, and integration into production LLM pipelines as a configurable, low-latency guardrail.

AI.tldr: kNNGuard is a training-free guardrail for LLM prompts that uses k-nearest neighbors in the model’s activation and embedding spaces, built from a small bank of 50 labeled prompts, to classify prompts as safe or unsafe with competitive F1 and lower latency versus fine-tuned baselines; rapid domain adaptation by updating the bank.
AI.motivation: To address the need for scalable, low-latency guardrails in LLM deployments that generalize beyond fine-tuned classifiers and avoid expensive gradient updates.
AI.method: Compute hidden activations from a provided LLM, fuse multi-layer activation-space and embedding-space scores via kNN using a small bank of 50 labeled prompts (safe/unsafe) to classify prompts without any gradient updates.
AI.result: Across six domains (topical and security prompts), kNNGuard achieves competitive or superior F1 compared to state-of-the-art fine-tuned guardrails and runs ~2.7× faster than the best comparable guardrail and ~10× faster than a fine-tuned safety classifier; domain adaptation is rapid, requiring only updating the labeled bank (≤10 seconds).
AI.conclusion: A training-free, low-latency guardrail approach that generalizes via a small labeled example bank and activation-space kNN fusion, suitable for production integration and domain adaptation with minimal latency.

title: Hardware-Enforced Semantic Coordination for Safety-Critical Real-Time Autonomous Systems
summary:
Recent advances in agentic AI are producing increasingly complex autonomous systems that integrate large language models, world models, optimization engines, specialized neural architectures, autonomous platforms, and human operators. While much current research focuses on improving reasoning capabilities, safety-critical real-time deployment also requires bounded and verifiable coordination among heterogeneous components operating concurrently under uncertainty. Software-mediated coordination presents fundamental limitations in domains where bounded latency, deterministic coordination, and enforceable safety guarantees are essential.
  Hence, we propose a hardware-enforced semantic coordination architecture in which selected coordination semantics are implemented directly at the hardware level via field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). The approach builds on the Topic-Based Communication Space Petri Net (TB-CSPN) framework, which separates semantic reasoning from interaction management.
  In this approach, selected TB-CSPN coordination mechanisms are mapped onto FPGA primitives, creating a hardware-native semantic coordination layer. Focus is not on acceleration, but on enforcing temporal synchronization, semantic gating, authorization constraints, and bounded coordination behavior directly in hardware. Semantic reasoning remains adaptive and software-driven, while embedded coordination semantics become deterministic.

AI.tldr: Hardware-enforced semantic coordination via FPGA-implemented TB-CSPN for deterministic, bounded, safe coordination in agentic AI, preserving software-driven semantic reasoning.
AI.motivation: Software-mediated coordination often fails to provide bounded latency, deterministic behavior, and enforceable safety guarantees in safety-critical, real-time autonomous systems. Hardware-level coordination semantics aim to address these limitations.
AI.method: Map TB-CSPN coordination semantics onto FPGA primitives to create a hardware-native semantic coordination layer. The semantic reasoning remains software-driven, while coordination enforcement (temporal synchronization, gating, authorization, bounded behavior) is implemented in hardware for determinism.
AI.result: Proposes an architectural design and framework: a hardware-enforced layer that guarantees deterministic coordination and safety semantics, while preserving adaptive software-based semantic reasoning.
AI.conclusion: Hardware-enforced semantic coordination can deliver bounded, verifiable coordination and safety guarantees in agentic AI, at the cost of increased hardware complexity and potential reduced flexibility; future work includes formal verification and integration with dynamic software reasoning.

title: Hierarchical Anti-Aesthetics: Protecting Facial Privacy against Customized Diffusion Models
summary: The rise of customized diffusion models has fueled a boom in personalized visual content creation, but it also introduces serious risks of malicious misuse, thereby posing threats to personal privacy. Image aesthetics are strongly correlated with human perception of image quality. Motivated by this observation, we address facial privacy protection from a novel aesthetic perspective by degrading the generation quality of maliciously customized models, thus reducing facial identity leakage. Specifically, we propose a Hierarchical Anti-Aesthetics (HAA) framework that exploits aesthetic cues at multiple perceptual levels. HAA consists of two key branches: (1) Global Anti-Aesthetics, which degrades overall aesthetics and generation quality by constructing a global anti-aesthetic reward mechanism and a corresponding loss; and (2) Local Anti-Aesthetics, which disrupts facial identity by using a local anti-aesthetic reward mechanism and loss to guide adversarial perturbations toward facial regions. By integrating both branches, HAA achieves anti-aesthetic degradation from a global to a local level during customized generation. Extensive experiments show that HAA outperforms existing methods in identity removal, providing an effective tool for protecting facial privacy.

AI.tldr: Proposes Hierarchical Anti-Aesthetics (HAA) to degrade generation quality of maliciously customized diffusion models by leveraging global and local anti-aesthetic cues, reducing facial identity leakage and enhancing privacy.
AI.motivation: Rising use of personalized diffusion models raises privacy risks, particularly facial identity leakage. Since image aesthetics correlate with perceived quality, degrading aesthetics offers a route to limit leakage without altering non-face content.
AI.method: A two-branch framework: Global Anti-Aesthetics degrades overall aesthetics with a global reward and loss; Local Anti-Aesthetics applies perturbations guided by a local reward and loss to disrupt facial identity at facial regions. The two branches are integrated to enforce anti-aesthetic degradation from global to local during customized generation.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that HAA outperforms existing methods in identity removal and provides effective protection for facial privacy.
AI.conclusion: Hierarchical approach successfully degrades aesthetics at multiple perceptual levels, offering a practical tool for protecting facial privacy in customized diffusion-model generation.

title: Fourier Neural Operators for Rayleigh-Bénard Convection
summary: We propose an improved Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) for modeling two-dimensional Rayleigh-Bénard convection by predicting time increments instead of full solutions, achieving higher accuracy than a standard FNO baseline. The resulting model is compact (314k parameters, 1.26 MB) and fast (7 ms inference), while maintaining similar accuracy as demonstrated in previous benchmarks. We show that although FNOs generalize to finer meshes, accuracy remains limited by the resolution of the training data.

AI.tldr: An enhanced Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) for 2D Rayleigh–Bénard convection predicts time increments rather than full states, achieving higher accuracy than a standard FNO with a compact 314k-parameter model (1.26 MB) and ~7 ms inference; accuracy is bounded by the resolution of the training data, though the model generalizes to finer meshes.
AI.motivation: To achieve more accurate and efficient surrogates for Rayleigh–Bénard convection by re-targeting the prediction to time increments and by evaluating how mesh refinement interacts with training-data resolution.
AI.method: Develop an improved FNO architecture that predicts time increments instead of full state fields for 2D RB convection. The model is compact (314k parameters, ~1.26 MB) and yields ~7 ms inference. Comparisons are made against a standard FNO baseline, with analysis of generalization to finer meshes.
AI.result: The proposed method achieves higher accuracy than the standard FNO baseline while remaining compact and fast. It maintains similar accuracy to prior benchmarks. It demonstrates that FNOs can generalize to finer meshes, but overall accuracy remains limited by the resolution of the training data.
AI.conclusion: Time-increment prediction with a compact FNO yields improved efficiency and accuracy within the constraint that training-data resolution caps attainable accuracy. For further gains, higher-resolution training data or alternative architectures may be needed; the approach is a practical step toward efficient PDE surrogates for RB convection.

title: Steerability via constraints: a substrate for scalable oversight of coding agents
comment: Accepted to the Deep Learning for Code Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, Seoul, South Korea, 2026
summary: Coding agents are capable; human oversight is the bottleneck. Unconstrained agents introduce security risks, erode codebase scalability, and make human review increasingly costly.
