Extensive experiments demonstrate that EADP improves the accuracy-efficiency trade-off of VLMs, robustly preserving fine-grained visual cues under strict token budgets while achieving SoTA performance on challenging multimodal benchmarks.

AI.tldr: Entropy-Aware Dense Pruning (EADP) improves VLM pruning by filtering textual noise via entropy and optimizing token selection as a submodular maximization with a spatial prior, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy-efficiency on multimodal benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Dense instructions and fine-grained queries require preserving subtle visual cues; existing pruning methods degrade performance due to two bottlenecks: widespread textual noise corrupting dense cross-modal scoring and feature fragmentation from naive token selection.
AI.method: A two-stage framework: (1) entropy-based filtering of textual input to produce a robust instruction-relevance score by quantifying textual noise; (2) token selection cast as a submodular maximization problem with a spatial prior to ensure a holistic, non-redundant visual representation instead of simple Top-K.
AI.result: Experiments show improved accuracy-efficiency trade-offs, robust preservation of fine-grained visual cues under strict token budgets, and state-of-the-art performance on challenging multimodal benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Entropy-aware structured compression effectively mitigates textual noise and feature fragmentation in dense pruning, enabling reliable and efficient VLMs under tight token budgets and broad applicability to dense-instruction tasks.

title: GeoMix: Descriptor-Free Visual Localization via Global Context and Multi-Detector Training
summary: Descriptor-free visual localization eliminates high-dimensional descriptor storage, preserves scene privacy, and simplifies map maintenance, yet its accuracy still lags far behind descriptor-based pipelines. We identify this gap to insufficient geometric discriminability in geometry-only matching. Without visual appearance, current methods underutilize local geometry cues, lack the global context among keypoints, and overfit to a single keypoint detector. We further observe that descriptor-free matching naturally enables multi-detector training, as heterogeneous keypoints can be optimized in a shared geometry-only space without aligning descriptor spaces. Building on these insights, we propose GeoMix, a descriptor-free 2D-3D matching framework that strengthens geometric discriminability at three levels. Locally, directional and distance-aware embeddings enrich neighborhood aggregation with fine-grained spatial structure. Globally, learnable context nodes aggregate and redistribute scene-wide information via cross-attention to resolve ambiguities beyond local receptive fields. At the training level, Mix-Training exploits this detector-agnostic geometry space to learn representations across multiple keypoint detectors. Extensive experiments on MegaDepth, Cambridge Landmarks, 7Scenes, and Aachen Day-Night show that GeoMix sets a new state of the art among descriptor-free methods, reducing 75th-percentile rotation error by 89\% and translation error by up to 90\% over the previous best, while generalizing zero-shot to unseen detectors and narrowing the gap to descriptor-based pipelines. Code is available at $\href{https://github.com/YejunZhang/Geomix}{\text{this links}}$.

AI.tldr: GeoMix is a descriptor-free 2D-3D matching framework that boosts geometric discriminability by combining local directional/distance-aware embeddings, global context via cross-attention, and detector-agnostic Mix-Training. It achieves state-of-the-art among descriptor-free methods and narrows the gap to descriptor-based pipelines, with strong zero-shot generalization to unseen detectors.
AI.motivation: Descriptor-free visual localization trades off appearance for privacy and map maintenance but suffers from lower accuracy due to insufficient geometric discriminability: lack of appearance cues, underutilization of local geometry, absence of global scene context, and overfitting to a single detector.
AI.method: GeoMix strengthens discriminability at three levels: (1) locally, directional and distance-aware embeddings enhance neighborhood geometry; (2) globally, learnable context nodes with cross-attention aggregate scene-wide information to resolve ambiguities; (3) during training, Mix-Training enables detector-agnostic learning across multiple detectors within a shared geometry space.
AI.result: On MegaDepth, Cambridge Landmarks, 7Scenes, and Aachen Day-NightGeoMix sets new state-of-the-art among descriptor-free methods, reducing 75th-percentile rotation error by 89% and translation error by up to 90% over the previous best, and demonstrates zero-shot generalization to unseen detectors; narrows the gap to descriptor-based pipelines.
AI.conclusion: Descriptor-free matching can achieve competitive accuracy with robust geometric discriminability, and GeoMix demonstrates strong generalization across detectors and strong performance gains, making descriptor-free localization more practical; code is available.

title: Towards Robustness against Typographic Attack with Training-free Concept Localization
comment: 15 pages main text, provisionally accepted to ECCV 2026
summary: Models trained via Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) serve as the foundational vision encoders for most modern Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs). Despite their widespread adoption, CLIP models exhibit a critical yet underexplored failure mode: irrelevant text appearing within images confounds visual representations, biasing them toward lexical meaning rather than true visual semantics. This robustness issue, commonly described as a Typographic Attack (TA), exposes a vulnerability that poses a significant risk to safety-critical applications such as autonomous driving. To achieve interpretable and effective robustness against TA, we propose a novel, training-free mechanistic interpretability method. Our method provides sampling-based interpretations of hidden state representations and quantitatively attributes semantic versus lexical focus to individual attention heads. Through probabilistic analysis and circuit mining, we isolate specific Vision Transformer (ViT) components that disproportionately encode lexical information, thereby identifying the mechanistic source of TA. We further show that simple interventions applied directly to the identified circuits, without any additional training, can substantially improve robustness against Typographic Attacks in object classification. These interventions, such as selective adjustment of attention weights, also outperform both supervised and training-free defense methods. Our experiments demonstrate that applying the proposed intervention to the vision encoders of several state-of-the-art LVLMs yields substantial gains in Visual Question Answering accuracy under Typographic Attack interference on RIO-Bench. These results confirm both the efficacy and the generalizability of our mechanistic approach. Code is released at https://github.com/Liu-524/SamplingTAR.

AI.tldr: Training-free mechanistic interpretability reveals and mitigates Typographic Attacks in CLIP-based LVLMs by locating lexical-encoding circuits in ViTs and adjusting attention to improve robustness without retraining.
AI.motivation: CLIP-based visual encoders are vulnerable to irrelevant typographic cues that bias representations; actionable, training-free defenses are needed for safety-critical applications.
AI.method: Sampling-based interpretation of hidden states; probabilistic analysis and circuit mining to identify heads/circuits with lexical bias; apply lightweight, training-free interventions (e.g., adjusting attention weights) to the identified circuits.
AI.result: Interventions substantially improve robustness to Typographic Attacks; outperform supervised and training-free baselines; gains in VQA accuracy under TA on RIO-Bench; demonstrated generalizability across state-of-the-art LVLMs; code released.
AI.conclusion: Mechanistic, training-free approach can reliably isolate and correct lexical biases in CLIP-based vision encoders, enhancing safety and robustness with simple circuit-level interventions.

title: Seek to Segment: Active Perception for Panoramic Referring Segmentation
summary: Existing referring segmentation models passively process static images captured from fixed perspectives, limiting their applicability in Embodied AI, where agents must perform active perception in the continuous 360$^\circ$ environments. To bridge this gap, we introduce a novel task: Active Panoramic Referring Segmentation (APRS). In this setting, an agent is required to adjust its viewing direction ($Δθ, Δφ$) to explore the 360$^\circ$ environment, seeking the object specified by a user instruction for segmentation. To tackle this challenging task, we propose PanoSeeker, a memory-augmented agent for efficient APRS. Rather than relying on heuristic scanning, PanoSeeker integrates a Vision-Language Model (VLM) with EgoSphere, an explicit spatial visual memory. By progressively integrating sequential local observations into a unified 360$^\circ$ representation, EgoSphere enables the agent to plan efficient and non-redundant search trajectories. Once the target is found, the agent performs active viewpoint alignment and outputs the segmentation mask. Furthermore, we curate an expert-annotated search trajectory dataset with memory timelines for Supervised Fine-Tuning, followed by Reinforcement Learning post-training to explicitly optimize PanoSeeker's exploration efficiency. Extensive experiments on our newly established APRS benchmark demonstrate that PanoSeeker achieves superior search efficiency and segmentation accuracy, significantly outperforming adapted state-of-the-art baselines.

AI.tldr: Introduces Active Panoramic Referring Segmentation (APRS) and PanoSeeker, a memory-augmented agent that uses EgoSphere and a Vision-Language Model to actively search 360° environments for a referred object, with supervised then RL training, achieving superior efficiency and segmentation accuracy against baselines.
AI.motivation: Static, passive referring segmentation on fixed views fails in embodied, 360° settings; an active perception framework is required to explore and localize the referred object efficiently while maintaining segmentation performance.
AI.method: Proposes PanoSeeker, which fuses a Vision-Language Model with EgoSphere, an explicit 360° visual memory, to incrementally integrate local observations into a unified panoramic representation. The agent plans non-redundant search trajectories, performs active viewpoint alignment upon finding the target, and outputs a segmentation mask. Training uses an expert-annotated search trajectory dataset with memory timelines for supervised fine-tuning, followed by reinforcement learning to optimize exploration efficiency.
AI.result: On the newly established APRS benchmark, PanoSeeker achieves superior search efficiency and segmentation accuracy, significantly outperforming adapted state-of-the-art baselines.
AI.conclusion: APRS demonstrates effective active perception and memory-based planning for panoramic referring segmentation, with a practical training pipeline (supervised then RL) and a new dataset to support future research.

title: From SRA to Self-Flow: Data Augmentation or Self-Supervision?
summary: Representation alignment has become an effective way to accelerate diffusion transformer training and improve generation quality. Recent self-alignment methods, such as SRA and Self-Flow, further remove the dependency on external pretrained encoders by constructing alignment within the diffusion model itself. However, the mechanism behind the improvement from SRA to Self-Flow, dual-time scheduling, remains under-examined: Self-Flow attributes its gain to interactions between tokens at different noise levels, where cleaner tokens help infer noisier ones. In this work, we revisit this explanation and ask whether the gain instead comes from data augmentation along the noise dimension. To disentangle these factors, we introduce Attention Separation, which preserves the same dual-timestep input as Self-Flow while blocking attention between tokens assigned to different noise levels. Surprisingly, removing such interaction does not degrade performance and can even improve it, suggesting that the improvement from SRA to Self-Flow mainly comes from data augmentation. Furthermore,We show that Attention Separation itself provides an augmentation effect by splitting a single image into multiple effective training parts to expand the training data. Based on these observations, we combine self-representation alignment with dual-timestep and attention-separation augmentation, and demonstrate the effectiveness of this design on ImageNet.

AI.tldr: This work questions what makes Self-Flow better than SRA in diffusion transformers. It finds that improvements mainly come from data augmentation along the noise dimension, not from interactions between tokens at different noise levels. It introduces Attention Separation to block cross-noise token attention, shows this ablation does not hurt and can help, and reveals Attention Separation itself acts as augmentation by splitting images into multiple training parts. The authors then combine self-representation alignment with dual-timestep and attention-separation augmentation and validate the approach on ImageNet.
AI.motivation: Disentangle the factors behind the performance gains from SRA to Self-Flow in diffusion models, testing whether token interactions across noise levels or data augmentation along the noise dimension drives the improvement.
AI.method: Introduce Attention Separation to preserve dual-timestep inputs while blocking attention between tokens of different noise levels; perform ablations to assess the impact of cross-noise interactions; demonstrate that removing these interactions does not degrade (and may improve) performance; show that Attention Separation provides augmentation by partitioning a single image into multiple training parts; combine self-representation alignment with dual-timestep and Attention Separation augmentation and evaluate on ImageNet.
AI.result: Ablation shows that blocking cross-noise token attention does not degrade performance and can improve it, indicating the gain arises mainly from data augmentation along the noise dimension. Attention Separation itself acts as an augmentation by effectively creating multiple training parts from a single image. The integrated approach with dual-timestep alignment and Attention Separation augmentation yields strong results on ImageNet.
AI.conclusion: The primary driver for the improvement from SRA to Self-Flow is data augmentation along the noise dimension rather than inter-token interactions across noise levels. Attention Separation provides a novel augmentation mechanism, and combining it with dual-timestep self-representation alignment offers effective performance gains, demonstrated on ImageNet.

title: PointDiT: Pixel-Space Diffusion for Monocular Geometry Estimation
summary: State-of-the-art single-image 3D reconstruction methods often rely on complex hybrid architectures and loss functions, or compress geometry into latent spaces in order to leverage pre-trained latent diffusion models. In this work, we show that such architectural overhead and intricate loss formulations are unnecessary. We introduce a minimalist pixel-space Diffusion Transformer, built on a plain ViT, that operates directly on raw 3D point map patches and is conditioned on image tokens from a pre-trained DINOv3. Unlike existing latent diffusion approaches, we train our diffusion backbone entirely from scratch, eliminating the need for point map tokenizers. Despite its simplicity, our approach surpasses complex latent-based diffusion models while remaining significantly simpler than hybrid alternatives. Notably, it produces sharper geometric structure and is more robust in highly ambiguous regions, such as transparent objects.

AI.tldr: Minimalist pixel-space diffusion Transformer for 3D reconstruction from raw 3D point map patches, trained from scratch, conditioned on pre-trained image tokens, surpassing latent diffusion models with simpler architecture.
AI.motivation: Reduce architectural complexity and loss formulation in single-image 3D reconstruction by avoiding latent diffusion and point-map tokenizers; leverage direct pixel-space diffusion on 3D data while maintaining strong conditioning from image features.
AI.method: A diffusion Transformer built on a plain ViT that operates directly on raw 3D point map patches. It is conditioned on image tokens from a pre-trained DINOv3 and trained entirely from scratch without a point-map tokenizer.
AI.result: The approach outperforms complex latent diffusion models, achieving sharper geometric structure and greater robustness in highly ambiguous regions (e.g., transparency) while remaining simpler than hybrid methods.
AI.conclusion: A minimal, pixel-space diffusion approach can match or exceed the performance of latent and hybrid architectures for single-image 3D reconstruction, reducing architectural and training overhead.

title: Alignment Is All You Need For X-to-4D Generation
summary: Generative diffusion models excel at synthesizing high-quality images, videos, and 3D content under multimodal control. However, arbitrary user-defined modality-to-4D (X-to-4D) generation remains challenging due to the high cost of constructing diverse datasets and the limited scalability of existing methods. This paper presents Align4D, a flexible framework that translates any-modal input into coherent video-3D pairs, using video to guide 4D motion and 3D data to shape 4D geometry. Align4D introduces three key techniques: (1) Object Distance Alignment, which searches Video-Aligned and Multiview-Aligned Object Distances (VAOD/MAOD), respectively, to reconcile 4D renderings with video and the priors of multiview diffusion models; (2) Motion-Geometry Joint Alignment, which constrains known and unknown views through synchronized video and 3D inputs, ensuring consistent 4D generation; and (3) Asynchronous Optimization, which decouples Gaussian attribute and deformation network training to enhance motion and geometry fidelity. We further propose the X4D dataset, which integrates prompt, image, video, and 3D data for benchmarking. Experiments on X4D and Consistent4D demonstrate that Align4D achieves state-of-the-art quality and consistency in X-to-4D generation. Project page: https://miaoqiaowei.github.io/Align4D/.

AI.tldr: Align4D offers a flexible X-to-4D generation framework guided by video and 3D data, introducing VAOD/MAOD alignment, Motion-Geometry Joint Alignment, and Asynchronous Optimization, plus the X4D benchmark; claims state-of-the-art in X-to-4D generation.
AI.motivation: Arbitrary modality-to-4D synthesis is hampered by the need for large, diverse datasets and scalability limits of current methods; a generalizable, data-efficient approach is needed to map any input modality to coherent 4D content.
AI.method: Three core techniques: Object Distance Alignment (VAOD/MAOD alignment with video/multiview priors); Motion-Geometry Joint Alignment (synchronizes known/unknown views via video and 3D inputs to ensure consistency); Asynchronous Optimization (decoupled Gaussian attribute estimation and deformation-network training). Also introduces X4D dataset for benchmarking.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on X4D and Consistent4D shows state-of-the-art quality and temporal consistency for X-to-4D generation; project page provided; demonstrated improvements over baselines.
AI.conclusion: Align4D provides a flexible, scalable solution for arbitrary modality-to-4D translation, enabling higher-quality and more consistent 4D content, and introduces a standardized benchmark for this task.

title: WorldDirector: Building Controllable World Simulators with Persistent Dynamic Memory
summary: We present WorldDirector, a highly controllable video world model framework designed for persistent dynamic object memory and unrestricted viewpoint exploration. Unlike existing world models that entangle physical dynamics with pixel rendering and rely on continuous visual observation to sustain motion, our framework explicitly decouples semantic motion orchestration from visual generation. By leveraging an LLM to coordinate 3D trajectories with camera movements and subsequently employing these orchestrated trajectories as control signals for video generation, our approach ensures strict physical logic and appearance stability, successfully preserving the exact visual identities of dynamic entities even when they re-enter the scene after prolonged periods out of view. Experimental results demonstrate that our method supports the synthesis of complex and extended events with unprecedented controllability and persistent dynamic object memory. Project Page: https://worlddirector.github.io/

AI.tldr: A decoupled, LLM-guided video world model (WorldDirector) that achieves persistent dynamic object memory and controllable long-horizon synthesis by separating semantic motion orchestration from video rendering, using 3D trajectory coordination as control signals.
AI.motivation: Current world models entangle physics with rendering and rely on continuous observations; there is a need for persistent memory of dynamic objects and explicit control over motion and viewpoint for long, complex events.
AI.method: Utilize a large language model to plan and coordinate 3D trajectories and camera movements; use these orchestrated trajectories as control signals for video generation; decouple semantic motion from visual rendering to preserve exact identities and physical consistency, even after objects re-enter the scene after occlusion.
AI.result: Empirical results indicate enhanced controllability for long-horizon events, with persistent dynamic object memory and preservation of object identities across occlusions; demonstrated via extended synthesis capabilities and a project page for reference.
AI.conclusion: The approach demonstrates that decoupling motion orchestration from rendering enables strict physical logic and stable appearance in video synthesis, enabling persistent dynamic object memory and highly controllable long-horizon generation; further work may explore generalization, efficiency, and broader scene complexity.
